description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: the lab's outfittings are flawless, perhaps too perfect for mortal hands (+2 General Quality, +2 Vis Extraction).

name: Flawless Tools
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: the lab's tools are legendarily perfect (+2 Items).

name: Flaws of the Weaponsmith
description: A Perdo Terram 25 spell invented by Philippus Niger that rusts away up to 100 metal objects, such as the arms and armor of 30 men.

name: Fleets of Venice
description: Heavily oversubscribed Venetian trading-fleet investments assumed unable to fail, whose occasional loss of ships to weather or piracy can cascade into an unraveling city economy.

name: Florilegium
description: A category of compiled Hermetic book noted by dedicated students of a subject, rarer than the Roots and Branches and found in libraries specializing in its theme.

name: Flumen of Tremere
description: A Tremere magus, parens of Goliard and former leader of Blackthorn, who captured the Wild Hunt in 1154 and passed into Final Twilight in 1187.

name: Focus of Flambeau
description: A Flambeau magus at Burnham, Scintilla's filius, about whom little else is known.

name: Fog of Confusion
description: A Muto Auram ritual (Level 45) that turns a bank of fog into a silvery mist too thick to see through, harassing and confusing those within it.

name: Fooling the Eye
description: A CrIm 10 miniature spell creating species of a swift bright object that makes the target's eyes track toward the magus, enabling Eye Range spellcasting.

name: Forceless Casting
description: A technique of deliberately casting a spell with Penetration Total of 0 so it cannot affect a magus's Magic Resistance, used in tournaments and group spellcasting.

name: Forest Law
description: A separate legal system applying in royal forests, prohibiting hunting, wood-cutting, and fires, enforced by foresters and forest eyres.

name: Forest Paths
description: Mystical paths through the forests of the Rhine Tribunal that a magus may explore; ascending the Glade of the Seven Waterfalls grants deeper understanding of the Forest.

name: Forest of Shining Stone
description: A Great Work at Durenmar where Bonisagus's epitome The Art of Magic has been etched into 36 clear crystals each six feet high.

name: Forge of Hephaestus
description: Sacred forges built by Hephaestus, the three Hermetic ones located at Verdi (Sardinia), Lemnos, and Mount Olympus, serving as Verditius Initiation chambers.

name: Forgettable Face
description: A Minor, General Virtue making a character hard to notice or describe, imposing -3 on rolls to identify him but incompatible with great beauty or charisma.

name: Form of the (Temperament) Heartbeast
description: A Muto Animal 20 spell with four temperament versions (sanguine, choleric, melancholic, phlegmatic) that enhances an animal form's humoral correspondences; modeled from Birna's innate abilities.

name: Formula
description: A researched recipe of experimental philosophy, like a Laboratory Text, describing how to make astrological inceptions, alchemical reagents, or pharmaceutical theriacs.

name: Fornax of Tremere
description: Goliard's filia at Blackthorn, an ugly and rude mature maga rumored to specialize in Rego and Mentem to make people entertain her.

name: Fortunata of Jerbiton
description: A powerful eleventh-century spirit master of House Jerbiton who defeated many non-Hermetic enemies but was forced into exile and disappeared into Final Twilight after 1120.

name: Fortunatus of Jerbiton
description: A magus of House Jerbiton whose Creo Imaginem illusions often have a small religious icon worked into their structure due to how he invents his spells.

name: Founding of the Order
description: The historical establishment of the Order of Hermes, predating which some traditions held antipathies against House Diedne.

name: Fountain of Youth
description: A magical fountain deep in the forest sought by Alexander of Jerbiton; drinking from it infused his blood with the power of youth, enhancing his longevity rituals.

name: Fourth Crusade
description: A late-12th-century crusade for which the Venetians built a fleet; unable to pay, the Crusaders were forced to sack Constantinople in 1204, and many cycled-out Venetian warships later mysteriously disappeared.

name: Fourth Lateran Council
description: A Church council of 1215 that forbade clergy from cautery or surgical incision and obliged physicians to require patients to summon a confessor before treatment.

name: Frail
description: A Minor General Flaw making the character weak of build with a -3 penalty to Soak score.

name: France
description: A kingdom of Mythic Europe whose king the king of England owes fealty for mainland possessions; home to Cluny, the Champagne fairs, and Laon, and which can be saved from demons in a saga.

name: Franciscan
description: One of the two major new mendicant friar orders of the early thirteenth century, whose members take vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience and travel preaching.

name: Franconia
description: A large and important region of the Rhine Tribunal containing some of the greatest German cities, with no single ruler; land shared between emperor and church.

name: Frankfurt
description: A trading city founded by Charlemagne at the 'Ford of the Franks' on the River Main, home to about 10,000 citizens and host of imperial elections.

name: Frau Holle
description: A modest Holzfrau who in the nine days before Walpurgis Night travels the land on a rickety wagon, pursued by the Wild Hunt, before ascending the Brocken and revealing herself as the goddess Walpurga.

name: Frau Wacholder
description: A wood-wife who is the genius of the juniper tree, invoked to make thieves give up their booty.

name: Frau Wode
description: The female leader of a Wild Hunt that haunts the Elbe river, accompanied by shadowy boatmen carrying invisible passengers.

name: Fredegisa the Quaesitor
description: A reforming idealist quaesitor at Schola Pythagoranis, a brilliant young student of all laws who devises new structures of Hermetic law.

name: Freedom of Movement
description: A common automaton power (base effect 25, Mentem requisite) letting the automaton walk toward areas pointed out to it.

name: Freeing the Striding Tree
description: A Rego Herbam spell (Level 30) like Lord of the Trees but enabling the tree to walk half as fast as a human; a botched Concentration roll causes the tree to attack the caster.

name: Freiberg
description: The biggest of the mining towns in the Ore Mountains, founded in 1186 after silver and tin were discovered.

name: Fria
description: The goddess worshiped by the old Germanic tribes alongside Woden, Thunor, and Tius.

name: Friderich Invigilor
description: The filius of Drogo Invigilor, similarly investigated by House Guernicus for his association with the Salian dynasty.

name: Friesland
description: A broad, flat, swampy territory bordering the North Sea, sparsely populated and home to the independent Friesian people and the Friesian Islands.

name: Fulda
description: An important pilgrimage site and home to a wealthy monastery, burial place of the martyred English monk St. Boniface.

name: Fulmonious
description: A magus of House Tytalus who, with Schwall of Bjornaer, founded the covenant of Rheinstein in the Rhine Gorge in 1123 AD.

name: Furioso
description: A Sorcerous Musician who lacks Subtle Magic, used as a contrasting example to Orlando in Performance Magic.

name: Fury
description: A Major Story Flaw in which a violent temper overwhelms the character, sending him into uncontrollable rage.

name: Fury of the Charging Bull
description: A ReAn 20 spell that enrages a target animal (up to Size +3), sometimes used by School of Vilano followers to make animals attack enemies, though unpredictably.

name: Gabai
description: A Minor Social Status Flaw marking the character as the local Jewish tax collector appointed by the community council, with a negative Tax Collector Reputation.

name: Gallery
description: A Minor laboratory Structure Virtue: an interior gallery or platform lets someone view the whole lab without disturbing it (+1 Safety, +1 Aesthetics, +1 Teaching).

name: Galley
description: An oar-propelled single-masted vessel popular with Italian maritime powers and Byzantine states, designed to ram enemies and discourage piracy.

name: Galli
description: A sect of nature worshippers once associated with the wild lands beyond the Roman Empire, later integrated into the Cult of Diana, said to be the origin of a True Merinitae Initiation Script.

name: Ganelon
description: A leading magus of the Ash Gild who declared Wizard War on Aschlaranda and Schadrit and pursued them into the Black Forest, never to be heard from again.

name: Gangrene
description: A Minor Sanguine Disease in which evil spirits in an improperly cleaned wound putrefy the blood; common after a botched Wound Recovery roll.

name: Garden of Eden
description: The biblical paradise referenced in the Divine material of the setting.

name: Garotillo
description: A Serious Choleric Disease from excessive exercise inflaming the choler; its second stage spreads to the windpipe causing suffocation.

name: Garrinchus
description: A newly apprenticed magus of House Ex Miscellanea at Fengheld's Rheingasse chapter, companion of Wilhelm Weiss and a member of the Apple Gild; his master was an expert in physick.

name: Gascony
description: A region of southwestern France, the probable birthplace of Flambeau the Founder around 715 AD.

name: Gateway
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Virtue: the lab sits at a supernatural gateway such as a regio entrance, faerie realm, or Mercere Portal.

name: Gathering of the Stormy Might
description: A Rego Auram spell (Level 40) like Clouds of Thunderous Might but producing a larger storm that can cover the entire visible sky.

name: Gaudy
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the lab's decoration is tasteless and excessive (+1 Upkeep, -1 Aesthetics, +1 Imaginem).

name: Gaze of Death
description: A Corpus power of the basilisk Sordus (8 points) that inflicts an incapacitating wound on anyone his gaze rests upon.

name: Geirlaug
description: A notable contemporary House Flambeau Archmaga of Montverte covenant in the Normandy Tribunal, renowned for her great age, power, and mastery of Ignem.

name: Gelon
description: Verditius's first apprentice and the first Primus of House Verditius; he attended the original Grand Tribunal, won the first Contest, and perpetuated the Corsican blood feud.

name: Genomi
description: Earth elementals known to the Order as genomi, rarefied from unworked earth, rock, or metal; long-lived, patient predators that crave the moisture of living beings and make excellent guards.

name: Gentle Caress of Aesclepius
description: A CrCo 30 Ritual spell that improves all of the target's wounds by one level of severity and instantly heals Light Wounds.

name: Geoffrey de Mandeville
description: A treacherous noble who, charged with treason in 1143, ravaged the East Anglian fens and destroyed the covenant of Natura Antiqua before being killed in 1144.

name: Geoffrey de Marsh
description: The justiciar of Ireland refusing to come to England to account for his office's revenues, possibly seeking to form a palatinate with vice-regal authority.

name: Geoffrey de Nevile
description: The seneschal of Poitou who returned to England to resign his office, claiming he lacked the resources to carry out his role.

name: Gerald of Wales
description: A churchman who campaigned much of his life to make St. Davids an archbishopric over the Welsh sees, author of The Journey Through Wales.

name: Gerard
description: A grog used in the complex combat example, with combat statistics and skills Single Weapon 6 and Leadership 2, who fights his faerie duplicate.

name: Gerbert of Aurillac
description: A scholar said in legend to have stolen a book of magic from a Saracen wizard and made a golden oracular head; Hermetic seekers covet his rumored treasures.

name: Gerfallon of Criamon
description: The tattooed, shape-shifting Criamon leader of Semitae since 1151 who maps the covenant's wanderings and pursues the Enigma; shows no signs of aging.

name: Gerfallon of Semitae
description: A magus of the tribunal whom some magi believe carved the strange cup-and-ring markings at Roughting Linn, though he will not confirm it.

name: Gerontocracy
description: A Free covenant governance choice in which the oldest members rule.

name: Gharad Ex Miscellanea
description: The second oldest maga at Cad Gadu, nearly blind and beset by Twilight delusions; rarely leaves her sanctum.

name: Ghent
description: A place near which the Spinnen Blood family line of the Faerie Blood Virtue originated.

name: Ghibellines
description: One of the two factions feuding over Florence since 1216, splitting the city along with the Guelphs.

name: Ghost
description: The disembodied spirit of a dead person, associated with Mentem; ghosts can be warded against, summoned, coerced, or controlled by Mentem magic.

name: Giant
description: Large Magic-realm Corpus creatures detailed in the bestiary.

name: Giant Blooded
description: A Virtue making a character larger than a normal human, so that a wound that would be Medium for a normal human is only Light for them.

name: Giant's Dance
description: The great stone circle Merlin magically moved from Mount Killaraus in Ireland to Britain, erecting it around the tomb of those slain at Ambrius (Stonehenge).

name: Giants' Blood
description: A heritage that makes its bearer unusually large and strong; Great William has giants' blood and stands just under eight feet tall.

name: Gift of the Frog's Legs
description: A Rego Corpus spell (Level 15) that allows the target to leap up to 15 feet vertically or 25 feet horizontally.

name: Gift of the Tortured Bowels
description: A Rego Corpus 10 spell that inflicts a sudden intestinal cramp and bout of diarrhea, used therapeutically by medically inclined magi to purge putrefied humors.

name: Gifted Companion
description: A character type a hedge wizard may become if the opening of his Arts fails or he declines the risk, joining the Order without full magus status.

name: Gifted Companions
description: Hedge wizards new to the Order, or those resisting conversion to Hermetic magic, who have The Gift and one or more Supernatural Abilities but do not open their Arts; the Scinnfolk are an example.

name: Gilbertine Order
description: The order of St. Gilbert of Sempringham, confined to eastern England and unique in having both male (Augustinian canons) and female (Benedictine nuns) members.

name: Gillomaur
description: The king of Ireland who swore the Britons would take no stone from his kingdom; his naked army was defeated and he was slain in a wood while fleeing.

name: Gilpatrick
description: An Irish-born baccalaureate student at the University of Paris and companion-level character with the Entrancement Ability and Latent Magic Ability, indebted to the bishop of Dublin.

name: Glam
description: A revenant of the walking dead from The Saga of Grettir the Strong who rode on house-tops by night and terrorized a district after his death.

name: Glass-blower
description: A covenfolk template for a dwarf-blooded glassblower craftsman with Faerie Blood and Great Dexterity, able to make clear glass.

name: Glastonbury Tor
description: A commanding hill near Glastonbury where St. Collen confronted Gwynn ab Nudd's faerie castle.

name: Gleam of the Freshly-Polished Glass
description: A Perdo Terram 25 spell that keeps a lab's equipment immaculately clean, granting the Spotless Virtue while cast monthly but raising Warping by one.

name: Gleemen
description: A group of jugglers warned of by northern clerics as tainted by the infernal, accused of diabolical powers, robbery, and sacrificing stolen children to a demon patron.

name: Glesig
description: A master maga of House Merinita at Irencillia, most versed in the subterranean fae and specializing in Terram magics; her copper hair is a Twilight effect and her familiar is the troll caricature Humnel.

name: Gloom of Evening
description: A Perdo Ignem spell (Level 10) that substantially drops the level of light in a target room, making it gloomy with deep shadows.

name: Glowing Footprints of the Thief
description: A MuIm 20 synaesthetic spell that makes a person's sweat traces visible by transforming olfactory species into iconic species.

name: Gmünd
description: A town in the Stauferland founded by Conrad III in the 12th century, named after the Hohenstaufen dynasty; it lies on the ancient Roman limes and specializes in luxuries.

name: God
description: The supreme being of the Divine Realm in Mythic Europe.

name: Godfroi
description: An example agent of Carolus, a merchant who handles stolen goods and is influential in local government and the Merchant Guild; held by Fear of Carolus.

name: Goetic Art of Binding
description: A Goetic Art used by a sahir to bind the Buran of Yenghissar; an Infernal supernatural ability for trapping spirits.

name: Golden Cider
description: The power gained at the Avenue of Death on the Path of Strife, which makes mystical things mundane; many followers use it upon themselves near death to relinquish The Gift.

name: Golden Fleece
description: The treasure the Argonauts voyaged to retrieve, during which Orpheus saved them from the sirens.

name: Golden Head of Gerbert
description: A legendary golden head crafted by Gerbert of Aurillac said to answer yes or no to any question; rumored to be used in Verditius Mystery Cult initiations.

name: Golden Maiden of Hephaestus
description: An ancient automaton created by Hephaestus and left in his forge; Verditius alone could understand it and made it function for seven days.

name: Golden Map
description: A solid-gold, gemstone-marked copy of an ancient Roman map given to Augustus Caesar; coveted as an enchantment shape and possible Arcane Connection, and rumored by some pagans to sustain the Dominion.

name: Goliardic tradition
description: A tradition of wandering, irreverent student-poets famously led by the Archpoet, spreading debauchery and satire across Germany and Italy.

name: Golias of Tytalus
description: An old Tytalus magus at Blackthorn who feigns being newly gauntleted; the covenant's best political dealer, with unknown magical interests.

name: Gorgias
description: A Sophist and pupil of Empedocles quoted in the Analects of Tytalus who taught the arts of persuasion and deceit, illustrating the corrupting power of words.

name: Goslar
description: A Free Imperial City on the northern edge of the Harz Mountains, famed for the silver mines of the Rammelsberg, which are flooding due to spiteful gnomes.

name: Gossip of the Marketplace
description: A Creo(Rego) Mentem 20 spell invented by Imanitos Mendax that implants information in a target who is then compelled to pass it on to friends.

name: Gothic shapeshifters
description: An Infernal Gothic witch-cult that enslaved ancestor-spirits to shapeshift; Birna's former tradition, surviving in secret in the forests of Pomerania and reviling Birna.

name: Granada
description: A region whose harried magi monitor the largest uncontrolled portal at the Pillars of Hercules for creatures that might harm Europe.

name: Grand Entrance
description: A Free laboratory Structure Virtue: an elaborate entranceway leads to the lab, impressing observers (+2 Aesthetics).

name: Grant Flaw
description: A special power of the Holm Oak of Romowe that inflicts the Depression Flaw upon anyone who breaks a branch or kills an animal in its grove.

name: Gratian
description: A Benedictine monk at Bologna who completed the Decretum, a collection of ecclesiastical laws, contributing to Bologna's legal reputation.

name: Gravis
description: A journeyman magus of House Bonisagus at Irencillia pursuing a fascination with the fae; despite great Faerie Lore he cannot grasp Faerie Magic, and his caricature is the grumpy dwarf Danket.

name: Great Characteristics
description: A Virtue boosting a character's physical or mental Characteristics; held by the Blacksmith template.

name: Great Dexterity
description: A Virtue providing an exceptionally high Dexterity Characteristic, taken by the glass-blower and burglar templates.

name: Great Stamina
description: A Minor General Virtue boosting the Stamina Characteristic; required of Nephilim.

name: Great William
description: A Redcap with giants' blood standing just under eight feet tall; interested in magical theory, with boots of swiftness and an enchanted accurate axe.

name: Great Work
description: Beautiful learning structures created as alternatives to books that embody their creators' values, studied as summae or tractatus, costing at least 100 Mythic Pounds to build.

name: Greater Collection
description: The sum of all Hermetic libraries, which great libraries coordinate to build by specializing in areas of weakness; Durenmar aids its construction as a spare copy of its own collection.

name: Greater Expansion
description: A Major laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab is greatly enlarged with at least double the usual equipment for specialized tasks.

name: Greater Feature
description: A Major laboratory Structure Virtue: the lab prominently features a unique extensive structure aiding certain lab work, granting +2 Aesthetics and 3 Specialization points.

name: Greater Focus
description: A Major laboratory Structure Flaw: an existing Greater Feature is the overwhelming focus of the lab, enhancing it but hindering unrelated activities (-2 General Quality).

name: Greater Guardian
description: A Major laboratory Supernatural Virtue: a powerful supernatural creature (Might 20+) that is not the owner's familiar resides in and protects the lab.

name: Greater Horde
description: A Major laboratory Supernatural Virtue: a large community of minor supernatural creatures serves and protects the lab and assists with simple tasks.

name: Greater Illusion
description: A Major laboratory Supernatural Flaw: a major aspect of the lab is merely an illusion; a balancing Major Virtue is taken but its effects are negated.

name: Greater Infernal Power
description: A Major Supernatural Virtue for corrupted beasts adding 5 to Infernal Might and granting an Infernal Power requiring a Penetration total.

name: Green Dragon of Labin
description: A dragon famously slain by the Flambeau magus Vilano, who crushed it with two falling trees using only indirect spells.

name: Gregorius of Bonisagus
description: A young Bonisagus magus, one of the newly arrived members of Libellus.

name: Grendel
description: A troll that terrorized King Hrothgar's hall until slain by Beowulf; its kin still haunt the bogs of Zealand and plague the covenant Heorot.

name: Grifo
description: An example famous maestro affiliated with the Divine realm, commissioned to paint a wall mural for the bishop of Milan.

name: Grim
description: An example grog used to illustrate disease and demonic possession rules, who is assailed by a Demon of Scrofula.

name: Grime's Graves
description: About a dozen large pits with tunnels in a Norfolk chalk hill, believed to be inhabited by faerie folk; those who wander too close at night tend to vanish, and strange lights are seen.

name: Grimgroth
description: A figure of the Order named as a trademark in the book's front matter.

name: Growth of the Creeping Things
description: A Muto Animal spell (Level 15) causing a small creature like an insect, mouse, or toad to grow to four times its normal size, increasing any venom.

name: Gruffyd ap Llewelyn
description: A Welsh king who attacked England, besieged Blackthorn and sacked Cad Gadu; magi suspected him of being a returned Díedne magus due to his name.

name: Guard
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Virtue: a shield grog stands permanent duty at the lab's entrance to dissuade intruders (+1 Aesthetics).

name: Guardian of the Forest
description: A self-declared role, usually taken by a Bjornaer magus, claiming a forest or wilderness as personal Hermetic territory; treated as the Oath of Fealty Sacrifice rather than a Quest.

name: Gudruty-kom the Giant
description: A giant Daimon (Magic Might 40, Auram), master of hail who can stretch his mouth from the ground to the clouds and swallow storms and spells; once revered in the lands of the Albanians.

name: Guelphs
description: One of the two factions feuding over Florence since 1216, splitting the city along with the Ghibellines.

name: Guest of the House
description: A Minor General Virtue making a magus politically a member of House Criamon while built using another House's rules.

name: Guglielmo de Pusterla
description: The podesta of Bologna who forbade the Oath of Matriculation, demanding masters swear loyalty to the city rather than to non-city organizations.

name: Guild Lore
description: An Organization Lore Ability covering the rules and bylaws of a guild, required at increasing scores for journeymen, masters, senior masters, and deans.

name: Guild of Watermen
description: A particularly powerful guild in large cities lacking sufficient bridges, such as Paris and Venice; watermen ship goods and passengers along rivers, coasts, and fords.

name: Gunhilda
description: A member of the covenfolk of Oculus Septentrionalis whose elder sister Matilda serves as autocrat and Henri's housekeeper.

name: Gunhilda Henrasdottir
description: A Follower of Jerbiton (age 31), daughter and filia of Henri de Tours, a young maga specializing in housecraft who is married to Estrid.

name: Gunter
description: Klaus's apprentice in the worked example, a storyguide character with Strength +1 and Swordsmith 3 who is trained over the course of the example.

name: Guy (son of Perceval)
description: The ten-year-old eldest child of the Redcap Perceval and Lucy.

name: Gwawrieir
description: The eldest swynwraig and effective leader of the Columbae who opposed joining Pralix; found strangled within her own protective circle while wearing the enchanted robes that became the Robes of Dusty Dawn.

name: Gwenn (the white mantle)
description: King Arthur's white mantle in the Dream of Rhonabwy; anyone wrapped in it can see everyone while remaining invisible.

name: Gwenwynwyn
description: A persistent Welsh foe of Llywelyn, lord of Powys who repeatedly switched allegiance between Llywelyn and King John.

name: Gwydyon
description: The librarian and autocrat of Cad Gadu, a large, resigned man in his fifties who keeps the neglected library from outright ruin.

name: Gwyndolen
description: The wife of Colomen who, with him, adapted the Columbae's ward-powers to Hermetic magic and spread their ward-spells through the Order.

name: Gwynedd
description: An ancient Welsh principality in the north, centered on the fort of Aberffro; ruled by Llywelyn the Great.

name: Gwynn ab Nudd
description: The king of the faeries and of Annwfn, who dwells in a faerie castle on Glastonbury Tor; St. Collen banished him and his castle with holy water.

name: Gydryty-kom the Giant
description: A Magic-realm Auram giant of Might 40 in the bestiary.

name: Gymir
description: A powerful demon whose earthly fief is Scandinavia, warring against Radegast and against the Dominion's incursion into the Northlands; he uses natural catastrophes, the Norse people, and the corrupted Holy Vehm as weapons.

name: Gyöngy
description: A sorceress who never joined the Order but whose magpie-heartbeast descendants founded the Sept of Gyöngy during the Schism War.

name: Hachim al'Khalejj
description: A quiet Muslim magus of House Criamon at Waddenzee (age 36), filius of Hassan of Fengheld, whose knowledge of astrology aids the pirates' raids.

name: Hagen
description: Gunther's powerful and treacherous vassal in the Nibelungenlied who murders Siegfried, steals and sinks the Nibelung treasure, and is finally decapitated by Kriemhild.

name: Halfgrim
description: An example grog who suffers Light and Medium wounds in combat and is treated with First Aid and Palliative Care at a covenant.

name: Hallucinations
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is afflicted by vivid hallucinations that seem like true visions but are figments of imagination.

name: Hamburg
description: A Free Imperial City and trading port on the River Elbe with a violent history of Viking and Wendish raids, occupied by Valdemar II in 1216; once home to St. Ansgar before the see moved to Bremen.

name: Hans
description: Klaus's journeyman employee in the worked example, a storyguide character with Strength +2 and Swordsmith 5.

name: Hardness of Adamantine
description: A MuTe 25 spell that instills a metal object with supernatural hardness, making it nearly unbreakable and boosting armor Protection by +2 or weapon damage by +1.

name: Harmony
description: In Criamon cosmology, the force that attracts and promotes cohesion; one of the two great forces of the universe, reflected by the Art of Creo.

name: Harnessed Magic
description: A Minor, Hermetic Virtue giving great control over one's spells, allowing the magus to cancel his own spells and magic items by concentrating.

name: Harold
description: An example character who knows Performance Magic (Hunt) and casts Hunter's Tracks of the Faerie Glow while hunting.

name: Harold's Vengeance
description: A covenant founded in 1066 in the East Anglian fens by Saxon magi seeking to drive William the Conqueror from England; Marched and destroyed by 1068 for repeated Code violations.

name: Harut
description: One of two fallen angels who, per the Qur'an, taught sihr (magic) to mankind to tempt them from Islam.

name: Hassan El-Megrayhi
description: A master of Fengheld of House Criamon who maintains a lone tower (Turris Acontiarum) in the Kyffhauser Mountains studying the stars with a single mute companion.

name: Hassan of Fengheld
description: A magus of Fengheld who is the Hermetic parens of Hachim al'Khalejj of Waddenzee.

name: Hatred
description: A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character hates someone or some group so much that hurting them dominates his life.

name: Hatred for Seekers
description: A Minor Ordeal Flaw from the Bind Curse Initiation, a burning loathing for other magi not of the House who seek Hephaestus-made items.

name: Hauberk of Sublime Lightness
description: A PeTe 30 spell that renders a suit of metal armor nearly weightless, reducing its Load while leaving its bulk unchanged.

name: Haunt of the Living Ghost
description: A Creo Imaginem spell (Level 35) with an Intellego requisite that projects the caster's image and voice to a place to which they have an Arcane Connection, often used to attend inter-covenant councils remotely.

name: Haunted
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab is home to a haunting spirit that occasionally disturbs the owner (+1 Warping, -1 Aesthetics, +2 Mentem).

name: Hearing the Silent Chorus
description: An Intellego Imaginem 15 spell invented by academic magi that lets the recipient barely hear the unheard sounds of planetary orbits (musica mundana), granting a bonus to astrology or song composition.

name: Heart of the Lion
description: A CrMe 15 spell that instills indomitable courage, raising the target's Brave Personality Trait by +3, sometimes leading to recklessness.

name: Heartbeast Temperament
description: The classification of heartbeasts into four classical temperaments (sanguine, choleric, melancholic, phlegmatic), which may be pure or aspected.

name: Hecate
description: A powerful faerie goddess who once saved Byzantium from Phillip of Macedon and lives in a regio coincident with Constantinople, entered only via a ritual path lit by a crescent moon.

name: Heinous Architecture
description: A Minor laboratory Structure Flaw: the chamber is deliberately inauspicious or perverse (-1 General Quality, -2 Safety, +1 Warping, -2 Aesthetics).

name: Heirs to Merlin
description: A Hermetic lineage within House Merinita descended from Ambrosius, who practice Charm, Story, and Symbolic Magic and serve as advisors to faerie courts.

name: Hekate
description: A spirit named among the Daimons, the Witch; Tytalus claimed his black dog familiar was a son of Hekate and brother to Kerberos.

name: Helios
description: A famous Younger Titan, the Sun, named among the offspring of the Titans.

name: Hellequin
description: A cursed spirit at the center of a mobile regio (Hellequin's Hunt, a host of the dead), tasked with guiding souls unable to reach Heaven onto their resting place.

name: Helm of Invisibility
description: A wondrous helmet made by an armorer that makes the wearer invisible (Craft Level 16).

name: Hengest
description: Leader of the treacherous Saxons who murdered the flower of Britain as they ate, prompting King Aurelius to build a monument.

name: Henry IV
description: An emperor who died in Liege after excommunication and forced abdication; the bells of Speyer would not toll for him until his excommunication was posthumously revoked.

name: Henry Murdac
description: An abbot sent from France in 1144 to bring Fountains Abbey into line with Cistercian practice, later contentiously elected archbishop of York, after which a mob sacked and burned Fountains.

name: Henry V
description: An emperor who deposed his father Henry IV, later sought his posthumous absolution, and was tormented on his deathbed by his betrayed father's apparition.

name: Henry VI
description: An emperor who imprisoned Richard the Lionheart at Burg Trifels in 1193.

name: Henry fitz Ailwyn
description: The first Lord Mayor of London, who served for 23 years from 1193 and oversaw the city's first modern charter in 1204.

name: Henry fitz Count
description: The son of the old earl of Cornwall and sheriff of that county, who withholds receipts from the treasury and usurps royal prerogative while trying to claim the earldom.

name: Henry of Essex
description: One of Henry II's constables who deprived St. Edmund of his rights; defeated in a 1163 trial by combat after seeing the vengeful vision of St. Edmund, he became a monk at Reading.

name: Henry the Fowler
description: Duke of the Saxons who received the German crown in 919 and defeated the Magyar hordes at Riade in 933.

name: Hera
description: Greek goddess and parthenogenetic mother of Hephaestus, who retrieved him to Olympus and was tortured by Zeus in a mechanized chair.

name: Herbalism (Virtue)
description: A Minor General Virtue granting skill in folk remedies and natural magic via the unique Herbalism Ability, plus 50 experience points and the ability to make theriacs and ligatures.

name: Herculaneum
description: Ancient ruins destroyed (with Pompeii) by a volcanic eruption, traditionally used as the strife-saturated investiture site for the Station of Blood and Bronze on the Path of Strife.

name: Hercules
description: A god and hero of legendary strength, identified by the Romans with the Gaulish Ogmios and worshiped as protector of the magical springs at the Sanctuary of Hercules.

name: Hermann
description: The chief of the Cheruski, trained in Roman service, who rallied the German tribes and destroyed Varus's legions at the Battle of the Teutoburger Forest in 9 AD.

name: Hermes Trismegistus
description: The legendary sage to whom magi attribute the maxim 'As above, so below,' cited regarding astrology and the Stone of Death.

name: Hermetic Experience
description: A Minor, General Virtue for a character with experience among the magi of the Order of Hermes, granting 50 extra experience points for relevant Lore or Latin.

name: Hermetic Fair
description: A gathering of the Order held in a vast twelve-sided quartz-walled hall in the Alps, supported by impossible ivory trees.

name: Hermetic Inclination
description: A maestro Virtue allowing a score in a specific Hermetic Form, used to instill spell-like effects into artwork while creating it.

name: Hermetic Mid-Summer Fair
description: A fair held by a covenant in the Tribunal of the Greater Alps each early June, lasting up to eight days, where magi trade vis, books, and enchanted devices; an auction is run by the Quaesitores on the fourth day.

name: Hermetic Patron
description: A Minor Story Flaw, available to Redcaps or magi, in which an older magus or established Redcap watches over and aids the character in exchange for service.

name: Hermetic Sahir
description: A tradition referenced as the model for relocating the Corrguineach; wizards who command spirits.

name: Heroic Virtues
description: A category of Virtues (with associated Flaws) from Houses of Hermes: True Lineages that maestros may also choose.

name: Heron of Alexandria
description: Ancient inventor whose works inspired the wonderful steam-rotator machines powering an Unnatural Law covenant.

name: Herrit of Tytalus
description: A young Tytalus magus among the members recruited to Nigrasaxa.

name: Herrod of Hohenbourg
description: The most famous woman painter of 1220, recently deceased, whose book Hortus deliciarum showcases her illuminations.

name: Hersfeld
description: A town dominated by a large imperial Benedictine abbey, whose springs are known for magical restorative powers.

name: Hertha
description: A powerful faerie goddess who bathes in Hertha Lake each Walpurgis Night, drowning a chosen mortal in return for blessing local farmers with good harvests; served by the priestess Zora.

name: Hertha Lake
description: A mysterious dark lake in the Stubnitz Forest near Crintera where the goddess Hertha bathes every Walpurgis Night and then drowns a chosen mortal in exchange for good harvests.

name: Hespera
description: The namesake of the enchanted lab item The Bookstand of Hespera.

name: Hexentanzplatz
description: A rocky crag in the northeastern Harz with a Faerie aura of 2 where the witches of the Harz gather every April before proceeding to the Brocken.

name: Hibernation of the Slumbering Turb
description: A ReMe 35 ritual Texture-Target spell, invented by Odorpes, that puts anyone touching the caster to sleep until the Spring Equinox.

name: Hidden Virtues
description: Fixed, occult qualities of objects granted by astral influences and ordained by God that cannot be explained by their substance.

name: Hide to Parchment
description: A Rego Animal 10 spell that stretches, shaves, and dries animal hides into writing-ready vellum as if a percamenarius had worked them.

name: Hiding in the Crowd
description: A PeIm 10 transparency spell that makes the caster selectively invisible to a single person by destroying a thin cone of emitted species, useful in city crowds.

name: Hiems
description: A Winter covenant of medium power, declined to six magi, occupying a largely uninhabited complex of caves, tunnels, and towers in a magical forest now haunted by a returned dragon.

name: High Crimes
description: Serious Hermetic charges that the pirates of Waddenzee would face if the mundane authorities moved against them with no Tribunal support.

name: Highly Cognizant
description: A Virtue held by the most dangerous faeries, allowing them to adapt and change their roles to feed on human emotional energy.

name: Hilda
description: An immense female covenant grog (custos) born and bred at Fengheld, a skilled mace-and-shield warrior with Great Strength and prime leadership material, given as a gift to young magi.

name: Hildebrand
description: Dietrich of Bern's man-at-arms who kills Kriemhild after discovering the bodies of Gunther and Hagen.

name: Hinder the Gift
description: A Perdo Vim 55 enchanted effect in the Wizard's Bridle that reduces the Casting Total of any spells by 25 points as a constant effect.

name: Hippian
description: One of the two ethical viewpoints of House Tytalus's Philosophy of Conflict, represented by anticlockwise spiral symbolism indicating introspection.

name: Hippian Ethics
description: A branch of Tytalan philosophy named after the Sophist Hippias that holds some unwritten divine laws are intrinsic to nature and necessary curbs on selfish physis; symbolized by an anticlockwise spiral.

name: Hippias
description: A Sophist quoted in the Analects of Tytalus who believed in the fundamental unity of mankind through unwritten laws of divine provenance; the Hippian view is named after him.

name: Hirsau
description: The most powerful Benedictine monastery in Germany, founded 1059 with the relics of St. Aurelius and modeled on Cluny; with a Divine aura of 5, it has been immune to the faerie attacks beset other Black Forest monasteries.

name: Holstein
description: A territory between the North Sea and Baltic under the control of the Danish king Valdemar II, where new port towns are springing up.

name: Holy Land
description: The region of the Crusades where Saracen wizards practice and some Flambeau magi fight non-Hermetic wizards.

name: Holy Sepulcher
description: The place where Christ was buried, an example of a site with a Divine aura of 10 arising where God directly intervened.

name: Homing Instinct
description: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue letting a character always know the way to a number of known locations and have fixed Arcane Connections to them.

name: Homobonus
description: A patron saint of merchants and of cloth and tailoring; a citizen of Cremona who died in 1197 and was canonized in 1199.

name: Hooks
description: Features of a covenant that lead to stories and provide points to spend on Boons; come in Major, Minor, and Unknown forms.

name: Horn of the Champions
description: An invested magical horn kept at Castra Solis that can alert and instantly summon senior Flambeau magi from anywhere in Mythic Europe via Arcane Connections.

name: Hornet Fire
description: A Muto Ignem spell (Level 10) with a Rego requisite that turns a fire into a swarm of insect-sized fireballs that harass a target, imposing a penalty and extra botch dice without dealing real damage.

name: Horrid Wilting
description: A Herbam power of the basilisk Sordus that kills every living plant within 5 paces and rots vegetable matter; he cannot control it.

name: Horrifying Appearance
description: A Major Supernatural Flaw for corrupted beasts making the creature hideously deformed and unable to pass as a member of its original species.

name: Horrifying Appearance – Snake Legs
description: A Major Supernatural Flaw in which the character has snake-like tails instead of legs, a deformity that can be hidden under clothing but not while moving.

name: Hospitaller Knights of St. John
description: A military order present in Acre that controls its own section of the city.

name: Hosvir Goatlegs
description: A Clan Wilkis magus of the Sept of Orn obsessed with rebelling against the Norman nobility of England; trained Ealwynn and Coenwulf.

name: Hounds of Anwyn
description: Faerie hounds said to leave the faerie court to chase the dead across Wales by night.

name: House Criamon Lore
description: An Ability quantifying a magus's understanding of House Criamon's task, strategy, paths, stations, and clutches; required at increasing scores to reach higher stations.

name: House Merinita Lore
description: The Ability Merinitae use to Initiate their House Mysteries, representing knowledge of all the House's secret rites, mysteries, and legends; common to all members.

name: House Mysteries
description: The Bjornaer Mysteries (Heartbeast, Secret Name, Sensory Magic, Theriomorphy) Initiated by Clan Ilfetu that allow magi to emulate their ancestors.

name: House Tytalus Lore
description: A Hermetic lore Ability concerning the history and customs of House Tytalus, exemplified by the Analects of Tytalus summa.

name: House of Flambeau
description: (Not present)

name: House of Wisdom
description: The most famous madrasah, in Baghdad, a center for translating Syriac, Persian, and Greek texts into Arabic; historically destroyed by Mongols in 1258.

name: Houses of Hermes
description: The twelve Houses that organize the Order of Hermes, now split into three groups of four: Mystery Cults, True Lineages, and Societates. They remain the same Houses as in earlier editions.

name: Hovel
description: A Major laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the lab is cramped, neglected, and filthy, little more than a stinking dump (-1 General Quality, -2 Upkeep, -2 Safety, -3 Health, -4 Aesthetics).

name: Hrools
description: Intelligent ferret-like creatures dwelling in warrens near the ruined Calebais laboratory of Ierimyra, who still protect the lab.

name: Hrothgar
description: Former king of the Danes whose hall site is now occupied by the covenant Heorot; he was terrorized by the troll Grendel until the hero Beowulf slew it.

name: Huarwar
description: A Welsh faerie who helped complete Offa's Dyke in 787 in exchange for cattle; now eats parts of the dyke and villages when not paid.

name: Hugh Foliot
description: The archdeacon of Shropshire who became bishop of Hereford in 1219 and was an employer of Robert Grosseteste.

name: Hugh de Lusignan
description: The count of Marche, a powerful vassal of the king in Poitou and husband of Queen Isabella.

name: Hugh of Lincoln
description: A former bishop of Lincoln who began the rebuilding of the minster in 1192 and is being considered for canonization; associated with the miracle of St. Hugh's Swan at Stow.

name: Human Figment of the Waking Mind
description: A Creo Mentem spell that places a hallucinatory person, seen and heard only by the target, into the target's common sense.

name: Humble
description: A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character always believes others are more skilled and better than himself.

name: Humnel
description: Glesig's faerie caricature, which has taken the seeming of an immense troll and become her faerie familiar, very protective of his mistress.

name: Hunger for (Form) Magic
description: A Major Supernatural Flaw in which the character has become dependent on consuming 1 pawn of vis of a particular Form each season or lose Fatigue Levels.

name: Hunter's Sense
description: An Intellego Animal spell (Level 30) letting the caster sense the shapes and primary motivations of all animals above a chosen size that can be heard.

name: Huntress in the Wood Lore
description: The Ability required to Initiate the grades of the Huntress in the Wood cult, with set thresholds for advancing from kerykes to eumolpids.

name: Hydra
description: A many-headed monster whose teeth provide Shape and Material bonuses of +6 Creo and +8 regeneration.

name: Hypernestoria
description: Mysterious lands reached via the regio where the Axis Magica emerges from the other side of the Earth's sphere, few of whose contents are known to Criamon magi.

name: Hywel Dda
description: The legendary lawgiver who created the laws of Wales many centuries ago, laws still known by wise men across Wales.

name: Höllental
description: A tortuous and haunted valley winding up from the center of the Black Forest, the only route to the Feldberg and the King of the Black Mountain.

name: Ibn Wahshiya
description: Author of The Book of Poisons, quoted for a recipe combining mouse, hellebore and other ingredients to make a fatal poison.

name: Ice Cavern
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: the lab is built of never-melting ice in the far north or atop a mountain (+1 Upkeep, +1 Warping, +2 Aesthetics, +2 Rego or Terram).

name: Ice of Drowning
description: A Rego Aquam spell (Level 35) that turns part of a body of water into jagged ice chunks that pound against anything on the surface, damaging swimmers and small boats.

name: Iddawg son of Mynyo
description: A horseman who captured Rhonabwy and led him across the sea to King Arthur's court in the dream.

name: Idris
description: A powerful faerie giant who controls all the land around the Welsh mountain that bears his name, able to call mist and ruin crops, with fox servants.

name: Idyllic Surroundings
description: A Free laboratory Structure Virtue: the lab sits in a charming peaceful location such as a vale or garden (+2 Health, +1 Aesthetics).

name: Ierimyra
description: A maga of the former covenant of Calebais whose ruined laboratory remains haunted by her ghost.

name: Ignatio
description: A grog used in combat examples, fighting with a shortsword and round shield, who defeats the Infernal wolf Polandrus and later fights his faerie duplicate.

name: Ilfetu
description: One of Birna's six apprentices, told to 'Teach,' a swan from ancient Frisia, the only one to learn the Ritual of Twelve Years from Birna; founder of Clan Ilfetu.

name: Ilium
description: A port town on the Aegean coast south of Constantinople, located in a faerie regio enterable only by ships with faerie pilots, ruled by the faerie lord Priam who claims descent from Zeus; possibly the legendary Troy or a faerie imitation.

name: Image from the Wizard Torn
description: A Rego Imaginem spell (Level 35) with an Intellego requisite that separates the caster's image from their body so it can speak and be seen through, leaving the caster invisible and silent.

name: Imagined Folk Tradition Vulnerability
description: A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character sincerely believes he is vulnerable to traditional wards and folk magic like the fey, and sabotages such wards.

name: Imanitosi
description: Prima of House Verditius who succumbed to Final Twilight in September 1219 while experimenting in her laboratory.

name: Imbued with the Spirit of (Form)
description: A Minor, Hermetic Virtue letting a magus who absorbed an elemental's powers substitute Long-Term Fatigue for vis of the chosen Form.

name: Immortality of the Forest
description: A new Major General Virtue linking one's life force to a forest, so that while remaining within its supernatural aura one makes no Aging roll but gains a Warping Point each year.

name: Immortals
description: In House Criamon's cosmology, a perfect race of spiritual beings that fell into the material world; magi (or all people) are reincarnated immortals.

name: Immune to Disease
description: A Major, Supernatural, Tainted Virtue marking a character as a powerful demon's property so lesser disease demons refuse to harm him.

name: Immunity
description: A Virtue rendering people and objects within a covenant's aura immune to a specified form of damage, influence, or Flaw.

name: Immunity to Cold
description: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue making normal cold harmless to the character, though extreme magical cold still affects him.

name: Impious Friend
description: A Minor Story Tainted Flaw in which a minor demon poses as a friend of the character to guide him toward a tragic destiny.

name: Impregnable
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab is completely inaccessible except through powerful magic, e.g. requiring a Muto Terram spell (-2 Aesthetics).

name: In Christ's Footsteps
description: A Rego Corpus spell (ReCo 5) created by Falke that allows the caster to walk on water.

name: Incantation of Putrid Wine
description: A Muto Aquam spell (Level 15) that makes all liquids within a target room vile and malodorous for weeks or months.

name: Incantation of Summoning the Dead
description: A ritual Rego Mentem spell that calls up a person's ghost, requiring the place of death, the corpse, or knowledge of the ghost's full name.

name: Incantation of the Body Made Whole
description: A Creo Corpus ritual (Level 40) that heals all wounds to a human body, but not missing limbs, diseases, or poison damage.

name: Incendior Homines
description: A Creo Ignem 30 enchanted weapon (wand, ring, or brooch) providing heavy firepower that envelops a target in flame for +15 damage with +8 Penetration, usable by unskilled grogs.

name: Incognizant
description: A faerie trait indicating it does not even know it is a faerie, following its role because it has no potential to understand any other option.

name: Increased Hubris
description: A Minor Ordeal Flaw making a Verditius magus more proud and self-centered, granting experience to increase his Hubris score by one level.

name: Independent Craftsman
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character works poorly with others, treating his Leadership and Craft or Profession Abilities as three levels lower when collaborating.

name: Indescribable Face
description: A Minor, General Virtue making a character hard to describe and separate from others, either by being unremarkable or by a distracting striking feature.

name: Indiscreet
description: A Major Story Flaw in which the character is unable to keep a secret, compelled to tell all unless he succeeds on an Intelligence-based stress roll.

name: Ineslemen
description: A Minor, Social Status Virtue for a member of one of the religious tribes of the Tuareg, with authority over disputes and immunity from feudal demands; exists only in North Africa.

name: Inexhaustible Supplies
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: the lab is blessed with magically replenishing ingredients that never run out (-3 Upkeep, +1 Warping).

name: Infamous Master
description: A Minor Hermetic Flaw in which the character's master was a diabolist or fool, causing other magi to treat the character with contempt.

name: Inferior Equipment
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the lab is outfitted with shoddy wares (-1 General Quality, -1 Upkeep).

name: Inferior Tools
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the lab's tools are crudely crafted and prone to breakage (-1 Upkeep, -1 Safety).

name: Infernal Heirloom
description: A Minor, Supernatural, Tainted Virtue giving the character a magical item inherited from a diabolist, useful but drawing its owner toward a demon.

name: Infernal Smoke of Death
description: A Muto Auram spell (Level 40) that turns fire smoke into a thick corrosive cloud inflicting +25 corrosion damage to anyone immersed in it.

name: Infested
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the lab has an animal or plant infestation, e.g. mice, a vine, or fungi (-1 Safety, -1 Aesthetics, +1 Animal or Herbam).

name: Inhabitants
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab is shared with other creatures who consider it their home (-1 Safety, -1 Aesthetics).

name: Initiation Ordeal
description: A price of Initiation involving acquiring a Flaw, losing a Virtue, or increasing a Minor Flaw to Major, reducing future Initiation Target Levels.

name: Initiation Quest
description: A component of an Initiation Script consisting of a lengthy journey with a series of challenges.

name: Initiation Sacrifice
description: A component of an Initiation Script in which the Initiate gives up time, wealth, knowledge, or power.

name: Ink of Noblest Metals
description: A Muto Terram 20 spell with Aquam requisite that transforms gold into a liquid applied as ink, reverting to solid metal when it expires.

name: Inmost Companion
description: A Muto Mentem spell (Level 40) with an Animal requisite that makes the target's mind physical as a bird; if the bird is killed the target dies, as their mind has been killed.

name: Inner Mysteries of House Bjornaer
description: Mysteries by which a Bjornaer magus, through atavism, gains an inner heartbeast (epitome, chimera, or anima) modeled on a Great Beast ancestor.

name: Insatella
description: The Prima of House Mercere, an unGifted Redcap who inherited the role from her father and manages the House from Harco in the Roman Tribunal.

name: Inscription on the Soul
description: A Minor Virtue allowing a magus to craft his own body into a talisman via tattoos, learned mainly by Criamon magi of the Path of the Body.

name: Instant Loyalty of the Rebellious Turb
description: A CrMe 50 ritual cast at a midwinter gathering that grants up to 100 people a 'Loyal to Covenant' score of +4 while inflicting Warping Points each year.

name: Intuition of the Forest
description: An Intellego Herbam spell (Level 10) giving an intuitive sense of how to get along in a forest, granting +3 to nature-oriented rolls there.

name: Invisible
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: the lab interior and outfittings are invisible, requiring magical means to see them (+1 Warping, halve Aesthetics, +2 Imaginem).

name: Invocation Magic
description: A Mystery Virtue the Titanoi cult can Initiate.

name: Invocation of Weariness
description: A Perdo Corpus spell (Level 20) that causes the target to lose a Fatigue level, often via singsong melodies that lull the victim into drowsiness.

name: Invoke the Pact of Zelos
description: A ReVi general-level Ritual spell that forms a pact with the Daimon Zelos by targeting one of his Aspects to perform a specific service.

name: Ioannes Acer
description: A young journeyman follower of Merinita at Irencillia, a knight with the Gift and Flawless Magic who specializes in Herbam and rides his stag caricature Kervus; youngest apprentice of Archmage Vinaria.

name: Irene the Younger
description: A Byzantine princess who became a Verditius maga and famous inventor of magical paintings and figurines, founding her confraternity.

name: Irnerius
description: A charismatic jurist at Bologna, the first to teach the Corpus Iuris Civilis, who put the university on the map through the study of Roman law.

name: Islam
description: One of the three Divine religions in Mythic Europe; Muslims live within a Dominion aura indistinguishable from the Church's, and a significant number of magi are Muslims.

name: Islamic Law
description: An Academic Ability, the Muslim version of Civil & Canon Law, drawn from the Qur'an and the Sunna.

name: Isle of Arran
description: An island where the eldest magus of the Path of Beacons lives in a regio of his own creation.

name: Isle of Ushant
description: A flat-topped island off Brittany with vertical cliffs and treacherous reefs, on which the Tytalus Domus Magna Fudarus is built.

name: Istria
description: The region in the Transylvanian Tribunal from which the Flambeau magus Vilano hailed.

name: Istvan Padas
description: A master of House Bjornaer holding the Seat of the Horse at Crintera, with a stallion heartbeast; the youngest and most willful Elder, a Wilderist descended from Magyars and lover of Zora.

name: Items of Quality
description: A Minor House Inner Mystery of Verditius for creating non-enchanted items whose latent magical bonus is drawn to the surface via runes, not resisted by Magic Resistance.

name: Itinerarium
description: A House Jerbiton tradition of a sponsored tour undertaken by apprentices near the end of training, mirroring young Romans' tour of Greece, Ephesus, Troy, and Egypt; originated accidentally with Anna of Naples.

name: Iudicium of Guernicus
description: The ancient senior quaesitor of the tribunal who presides at meetings from Blackthorn; bears a tattoo of a scarlet serpent and favors Intellego and Mentem magic.

name: Jack-of-All-Trades
description: A Minor, General Virtue letting a character attempt Ability rolls without a score and without extra botch dice.

name: Jakin
description: One of two great hollowed stone pillars ("he establishes") of Solomon's temple legend that hold treasures of the ancient Hebrews.

name: Jami'at al-Qarawiyyin
description: A madrasah in Morocco described as the oldest madrasah in existence.

name: Janis
description: Leader of Crintera's Swan Clan and volkv (priest) of the Forest Brothers, the covenant's contact among the pagan people of Rügen, often consulted by the magi on island matters.

name: Janus
description: A dead titanic god of doorways whose ghost pours wisdom into the ears of those who sleep on his grave, near a Merinita portal to Arcadia.

name: Jart
description: The master of Tabanus and the leading Traditionalist within House Guernicus, favoring a strict interpretation of the Code.

name: Jason
description: The leader of the Argonauts who, on Chiron's advice, brought Orpheus on the voyage to retrieve the Golden Fleece.

name: Jennis
description: Richenda Spinosa's faerie caricature, a male version of the Polish maga who is helping her come to terms with her fae side.

name: Jeremias filius Guernicus
description: A magus, author of De Lapii, the Branch of Terram summa, in 1220.

name: Jerome the Scribe
description: A scribe for whom Victor of Mercere is tasked with purchasing particular pigments in town.

name: Jerusalem Hospital
description: The most famous hospital instituted for those injured on Crusade, built by the Order of St. John.

name: Jewish Temple in Jerusalem
aliases: the last remnants of the Jewish temple in Jerusalem
description: The remnants of the Jewish temple in Jerusalem, cited as an example of a place with a Divine aura of 10.

name: Jinxed
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is a magnet for bad luck, being biased to be the one affected whenever chance determines misfortune.

name: Jiphella
description: An immense Ex Miscellanea maga of Dankmar (age 73), biological daughter of Schadrit and master of Mentem magics who keeps the covenfolk under her spell.

name: Jocelin
description: A Redcap in his late twenties with brown hair and green eyes; favors new covenants and carries a ring of magic resistance and an enchanted shield.

name: John Scottus
description: A scholar who in the ninth century corrected the error of two predeterminations, one good and one evil.

name: John de Garlande
description: Author of the famous 13th-century craft manual Dictionarius, covering moneychangers, clasp makers, cup makers, jewelers, and harness makers.

name: Jon Arnsson
description: A 98-year-old master of House Bjornaer holding the Seat of the Stag (protector) at Crintera, with a lion heartbeast; a devout Christian Harmonist with divided loyalties.

name: Jonaquil of Merinita
description: A young Merinita magus, one of the newly arrived members of Libellus.

name: Jonathan Tweet
description: Ars Magica co-creator who wrote the game's preface; an in-world author note rather than a setting figure.

name: Josce fil' Isaac of London
description: An important London usurer who currently holds the office of archpresbyter, the crown-appointed Jewish representative.

name: Joseph of Arimathea
description: The companion who came to Britain with Christ and later carried Christ's blood in a vessel, traveling west with eleven companions to found the first church at Glastonbury.

name: Jove
description: A pagan deity cited as an example of an earth-shakingly important figure with a Might score in the 51-60 range.

name: Judaic Lore
description: A General Ability covering knowledge of Jewish cultural practice such as poetry, folklore, and songs.

name: Judaism
description: One of the three Divine religions in Mythic Europe; Jews live within a Dominion aura, and a scattering of magi are Jewish.

name: Julian of Flambeau
description: A magus of House Flambeau whose version of The Beast Remade gives transformed beasts bright red hair in their new form.

name: Junius of Verditius
description: An old, powerful Verditius magus of Semitae who makes the covenant's enchanted wagons and works secretly on an unrevealed project.

name: Just an Instant
description: A Minor, General Virtue letting a character who briefly looks about a room detect and remember anything of interest without Awareness checks.

name: Justin of Tremere
description: A young Tremere magus, one of the newly arrived members of Libellus.

name: Justinian
description: Roman emperor referenced in connection with civil law in the setting.

name: Ka'aba
description: A holy site in Mecca cited as an example of a place with a Divine aura of 10 where God intervened directly.

name: Kaeso
description: Founder of the Mithraic tradition within House Flambeau; a hedge wizard of the Cult of Mithras recruited by Apromor who founded the covenant of Castra Solis.

name: Karaite Magic
description: The Major Hermetic Flaw of the Karaites tradition, reflecting their religious restrictions on magic.

name: Kassala
description: A location in Alodia, the most remote of the three Nubian kingdoms on the southern reaches of the Nile, home to the Mortuary Society that practices Kassalan Exorcism.

name: Kassalan Dust
description: A dust of powdered gold, myrrh, and spices made by the Mortuary Society of Kassala, required for Kassalan Exorcism and granting a +3 Shape & Material bonus against the dead.

name: Kassalan Exorcism
description: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue allowing minor exorcism spells via the rites of the Mortuary Society of Kassala, aligned to the Magic Realm and using Kassalan Dust.

name: Katzenveit
description: A Waldgeist (wood-spirit) who haunts the forests of the Fichtelgebirge (Spruce Mountains).

name: Keeper of the Path
description: The figure who tests aspirants at the Path of Strife's Initiation site, requiring them to negotiate the Labyrinth of Strife.

name: Kerberos
description: A figure to whom Tytalus claimed his black dog familiar was brother, alongside being a son of Hekate.

name: Kerry Mountains Pool
description: A deep black pool in the Kerry Mountains of Hibernia where the ancient Irish cast votive offerings to their ancestors; a Bjornaer ancestor site.

name: Kervus
description: Ioannes Acer's faerie caricature, which has taken the form of a huge stag capable of bearing his weight, which he rides everywhere.

name: King Aurelius
description: A king of Britain who sought to build a monument to his murdered people and was advised by Merlin to bring the Giant's Ring from Ireland.

name: King Baldwin I of Jerusalem
description: King of Jerusalem; an encounter with him led the pirate-merchant Godric to repentance and pilgrimage.

name: King Dagobert
description: Seventh-century king who founded Saint Denis's Lendit Fair near Paris, once the most important fair in France.

name: King Holly
description: The faerie ruler of the northern Holly Forest among the Courts of the Seasons, a tyrannical and cold-hearted Winter King who battles King Oak; possibly linked to the leader of the Wild Hunt.

name: King Mark of Cornwall
description: One of Arthur's under-kings who later held Tintagel as his seat.

name: King Oak
description: The faerie ruler of the southern Oak Forest among the Courts of the Seasons, a regal and generous Summer King who battles King Holly; touchy of honor and takes words literally.

name: King Richard's Ring
description: A wondrous gold ring that protects the wearer from fire (+5 Soak), named after Richard the Lionhearted and the legendary ring he wore on crusade (Craft Level 16).

name: King Sel
description: A king said to be buried on horseback with his treasury within Silbury Hill near Avebury, his tomb protected by a curse that strikes dead would-be robbers.

name: King Sigebert
description: The king who founded the abbey at Bury St. Edmund's in 633.

name: King Stone
description: A large stone standing apart from the Rollright Stones circle, the most magical of the lot, whose chips are supposed to ward against demons.

name: King Valdemar I of Denmark
description: Danish king who invaded the island of Rügen in 1168, threatening Crintera's pagan aura.

name: King William Rufus
description: A king of England who summoned Eadric Wilde and his faerie wife to London out of a wish to look upon them.

name: King's Bench
description: One of the highest English courts of appeal, fixed at Westminster by Magna Carta, trying important civil and treason cases and issuing writs; its senior justice is Martin of Pattishall.

name: Kingdom of Asturias
description: A kingdom in northern Spain where Laberius served as court magician and fought the Moors during the early Reconquista.

name: Kingdom of Denmark
description: The kingdom that constrains travel in the Baltic Sea.

name: Kingdom of Jerusalem
description: The Crusader state of the Holy Land whose major port and nominal capital is Acre, constantly at risk from Muslim forces.

name: Kirist of Flambeau
description: A young, fiery-tempered Flambeau magus of Voluntas specializing in Ignem who is committed to the greater good of the Order.

name: Klaus
description: A companion-level craftsman example character, master of the Swordsmiths' Guild, with the Virtue Touched by the Divine Realm, who makes greatswords and a wondrous flaming greatsword.

name: Kleon of Criamon
description: A magus of House Criamon who spent years in the Thuringian Forest performing dangerous experiments with raw vis, became riddled with Warping, and likely perished in a Twilight episode.

name: Kludie
description: The most powerful faerie hound variant, from Belgium, able to take large forms of dog, cat, bat, horse or frog, walking on its back legs and preceded by supernatural blue flames.

name: Klynoites
description: Pater of the magus who assassinated Prima Kalliste; he Marched his own filius and became the next Primus of House Tytalus, denouncing House Flambeau at Tribunal.

name: Knife of Human Bone
description: Philippus Niger's talisman, a wickedly curved dagger of human bone enchanted to stay razor-sharp, with attunements for Precise Destruction, Destroy Body, and Destroying Minds.

name: Knights Hospitaller
aliases: Knights of the Hospital of St. John of Jerusalem
description: A military order of monk-knights holding land across Christendom whose English houses gather funds and supplies for the Levant.

name: Knights of Blanik
description: The sleeping army of St. Wenceslaus, knights seated motionless in stone chairs in an underground hall within the Divine regio of Mount Blanik, awaiting their call to arise.

name: Knows People
description: A Minor, General Virtue letting a character act as a social middleman, requesting a 'bait' once per story to gain aid from a non-player character.

name: Kolding
description: A small trading town at the head of Kolding Fjørd on the border between the Kingdom of Denmark and the Duchy of Schleswig, with about 200 inhabitants relying on fishing and a weekly farm market.

name: Koldun
description: Shamanic wizards from the Novgorod Tribunal who abandoned their pagan priesthood for sorcery; a Witches of Thessaly variant tradition.

name: Kore
description: A nature-oriented deity whose name eumolpids of the Huntress may learn through the Mysteries of Names of Power and Invocation Magic.

name: Krak des Chevaliers
description: A real fortress cited as a forebear of the Superior Engineering concentric-castle style.

name: Kratos
description: The Daimon of might, bodily strength, and sovereign rule, son of Styx and Pallas, referenced in the Analects of Tytalus as a constant companion of the Founder.

name: Krios
description: An Elder Titan of leadership and father of Pallas the Titan of war-craft.

name: Kronos
description: The Greek representation of time in serpent form, whose coils appear as scaly marks on the wrists of some Criamon ghosts.

name: Kropel
description: A good-natured dwarflike creature of the Harz who travels abroad hidden by his hat of fog.

name: Kupala
description: A faerie lord who guards the Fire Flower in Slavic lands and from whom Richenda Spinosa is descended, source of her secret faerie blood.

name: Kutna Mine
description: A fantastically rich silver mine opened by the Cistercian monks of Sedlec, where a monk named Anton found silver rods sprouting; site of a story seed about a magus secretly mining silver with magic.

name: Kyffhauser Mountains
description: A double line of hills on the Saxony-Thuringia border, legendary resting place of famous kings (notably Frederick Barbarossa) and site of Fengheld's Turris Acontiarum chapter.

name: Laberius
description: A hermit-wizard of the ancient Roman cult of Mithras who healed and trained the young Flambeau, later killed by sahirs in Iberia.

name: Laboratory
description: A magus's workshop for magical experimentation; one standard laboratory exists per magus in the baseline covenant.

name: Labyrinth
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab's exterior is a maze or structural puzzle, favored by some Criamon magi (-1 Safety, -1 Health, -2 Aesthetics, +2 Mentem or Vim).

name: Labyrinth Meditation
description: A non-magical Criamon ritual of walking a maze while contemplating a problem to improve concentration, granting a bonus to a single subsequent roll.

name: Labyrinth of Strife
description: A tangled structure of tunnels at the Path of Strife's Initiation site that magi can only escape by performing feats violating Criamon tenets of apt action.

name: Lacerta
description: A Clan Arelie magus of an Iberian sept, parens of Natrix.

name: Lacuna
description: A 'hole' within an urban environment where the Dominion does not dominate, allowing magi to cast spells without realm interaction penalties; may carry other auras.

name: Ladislaus
description: A trusted companion of Roznov covenant who haunts the Prague slave market using his Magic Sensitivity to identify and filter out Gifted children among the slaves for delivery to Coeris.

name: Lady Godgifu
description: The legendary noblewoman of a story seed whose lord promised to reduce taxes if she rode naked through the marketplace.

name: Lair
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: a creature hides or hibernates in the lab, known or unknown (-1 Safety, +1 Warping).

name: Lake District
description: The region where the covenant Ungulus sits in a carved tower on a ridge, and where Aquila rides the thermals in eagle form.

name: Lake Nemi
description: A sacred lake in the Roman Tribunal in whose waters Huntress initiates may bathe on the Ides of August during the Eumolpid initiation.

name: Lammergeyer
description: The bearded vulture deemed by House Jerbiton the correct falconry raptor for magi; its bones make particularly good magical flutes and it has deep orange iron-rubbed plumage.

name: Languedoc
description: A region of central southern France where Brother Julian wanders and preaches against the spread of the Cathar heresy.

name: Lapis Maior
description: The legendary Greater Stone long sought by alchemists, said to convert pure base metals into gold.

name: Lapis Minor
description: A Level 20 Alteration Reagent creating a reddish waxy stone whose touch purifies a precious metal from its alloy; called the Lesser Stone, distinct from the sought-after Greater Stone.

name: Lares Lore
description: An Ability used by Vestals to interact with lares (household spirits, also called penates), domestic faeries of the home and community.

name: Large
description: A Minor, General Virtue setting Size to +1 so the character is six to seven feet tall, with wounds in six-point intervals.

name: Larinda
description: A young Ex Miscellanea maga of Dankmar (age 20), daughter and filia of Jiphella, with a sunny disposition and affinities for Animal, Herbam, Aquam, and Auram.

name: Larus Egg-Thief
description: Clan Chief of Clan Maruhs, a wandering magus with a skua (seabird) heartbeast who haunts the coasts of western Europe.

name: Last Flight of the Phoenix
description: A CrIg 50 spell in which the caster immolates himself in a white-hot blast doing +45 damage; an early version was found in Flambeau's own lab notes, used by magi with Greater Immunity to fire.

name: Latin Quarter
description: The left-bank Paris district of jumbled houses where masters and students live, a lawless place of books, learning, drinking, and gambling.

name: Law of Names
description: A magical principle by which knowing a ghost's full name allows it to be summoned, as used in the Incantation of Summoning the Dead.

name: Laws of Edward the Confessor
description: 12th-century English laws under which the King owns all Jews and their property, relevant to a Minority Boon covenant in England.

name: Laws of Hospitality
description: The Rhine Peripheral Code rules, derived from German guest-laws, governing the duties of guests and hosts and entitling a magus to request hospitality at any legal covenant for a vis fee.

name: Learn (Ability) From Mistakes
description: A Minor, General Virtue granting experience points in a chosen Ability the first time per session the character botches or narrowly fails a roll.

name: Learn Chirurgy from Mistakes
description: A Virtue commonly taken by empirici allowing them to learn the Chirurgy Ability from their failures.

name: Leather Ripper
description: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue granting the power to destroy a group of leather objects, as a PeAn(He) 30 effect.

name: Leccacorvo
description: The Genoese bank cited as a legendary money/banking income example.

name: Lech
description: One of the three legendary founding brothers of the Slavic peoples, who continued on to settle in Poland.

name: Leczyca
description: A covenant established in Poland in 1052 by refugees from Grand Silesia to reinforce the New Slavonic Tribunal's authority over the Slavic lands.

name: Legatus a latere
description: A cleric authorized to act on behalf of the Pope with his full power; granted Divine Magic Resistance of 20.

name: Legatus missus
description: A cleric with papal authorization for a single purpose; granted Divine Magic Resistance of 15.

name: Lemnos
description: The island where Hephaestus settled and took twelve forge-companions; site of a Forge of Hephaestus, a Verditius covenant (Ingasia), and an all-Verditius community.

name: Leo III
description: The Byzantine Emperor who in 729 ordered the destruction of images of Christ and the saints and forbade crosses in worship, prompting the formation of the League of Iconophiles.

name: Leonardo Fibonacci of Pisa
description: A reclusive Pisan mathematical genius (Int +4, Com +5) who discovered the golden section / Fibonacci sequence and wrote the tractatus Liber abbaci; his work can aid Aristotelian Magic Theory and Herbam research.

name: Leprosy (Flaw)
description: A Major Flaw gained by the victim of the leprosy disease, imposing a Living Condition penalty and reputation effects.

name: Lesser Expansion
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab is enlarged with some specialized equipment (+1 General Quality, +2 Upkeep, 1 Specialization point).

name: Lesser Feature
description: A Minor laboratory Structure Virtue: the lab features a unique structure aiding certain lab work, granting +1 Aesthetics and 1 Specialization point.

name: Lesser Focus
description: A Minor laboratory Structure Flaw: an existing Lesser Feature is the central focus of the lab, enhancing it but hindering unrelated activities.

name: Lesser Guardian
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Virtue: a supernatural creature (less than Might 20) not the owner's familiar resides in and protects the lab (+1 Safety).

name: Lesser Horde
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Virtue: a small group of semi-intelligent creatures helps in the lab (+1 General Quality, +1 Upkeep, +1 Safety, +1 Aesthetics).

name: Lesser Illusion
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: one apparent merit of the lab is merely an illusion; a balancing Minor Virtue is taken but its effects are negated.

name: Lesser Infernal Power
description: A Minor Supernatural Virtue for corrupted beasts adding 2 to Infernal Might and granting an Infernal Power that cannot have a Penetration total.

name: Lessini Mountains
description: The mountains where the Alps cross into Italy, site of Dietrich Von Bern's ornate tomb filled with dragon-blood-enchanted arms.

name: Leucrota
description: A mythical beast whose tongue provides a Shape and Material bonus of +6 to mimicking human voices.

name: Liber abbaci
description: Leonardo of Pisa's book (1202), a Quality 14 tractatus on Artes Liberales (arithmetic) covering interest, square roots, alloy percentages, and the golden section; reading it aids Herbam research and Aristotelian Magic Theory.

name: Liber de Lumine
