description: A Tractatus on Ignem (Quality 11) by Elaine concentrating on light as an aspect of the Form of Ignem.

name: Libuse
description: The Gifted granddaughter of Czech who had a great vision at Vysehrad Rock foretelling her husband Premysl, founder of Bohemia's ruling dynasty.

name: License of Absence
description: A Major, General Virtue for a priest relieved of some duties, giving an extra free season each year; only available to Priest Social Status.

name: Liege
description: A prince-bishopric and market city where the River Legia joins the Meuse, grown from the martyrdom site of St. Lambert; its most famous bishop was Notger.

name: Life-Linked Art
description: A Major Supernatural Virtue letting an artist wound himself while working to increase artwork's Aesthetic Quality, making the piece a permanent Arcane Connection.

name: Ligature
description: A small charm of parchment, stones, or herbs worn around the neck containing an Arcane or Sympathetic Connection, employing natural principles to grant a bonus to a single die roll.

name: Light Shaft of the Night
description: A Rego Ignem spell (Level 20) that collects moonbeams and starlight into a controllable vertical shaft of soft silvery light, castable only under the night sky.

name: Lightless
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab is totally dark and its contents cannot be seen, requiring other means of spatial perception (-1 Upkeep, +1 Warping).

name: Limes
description: A line of defensive forts reinforced by magic built by the Roman legions under Mercurian guidance, delineating the empire's northern extent and first fracturing the Hercynian Forest.

name: Lincoln
description: An important town and seat of a powerful bishop, left in poor material state by the battle of Lincoln in 1217; its castle is held by Nicola de Hay.

name: Line of Muj
description: A mythic lineage from the Balkans whose ancestor made a pact with a magical guardian spirit, blessing his descendants with great strength and power over storms; surviving members live in the Transylvanian Tribunal and belong to House Tremere.

name: Lineage of Hercynius
description: A Bonisagus lineage descended from Hercynius, the penultimate apprentice of Bonisagus, which founded Waldherz to pursue primal forest magic and was largely destroyed in the Schism War.

name: Lineage of Irmele
description: A line of wandering, weather-working magi within House Bonisagus founded by Irmele filia Trianoma, prominent among the peregrinatores and the Linden Gild.

name: Lingering Injury
description: A Minor General Flaw in which an old injury won't heal, penalizing physical rolls and worsening with age.

name: Linguist
description: A Minor, General Virtue increasing all Language Advancement Totals and character-generation language experience by a quarter.

name: Lion of the North
description: An Ars Magica sourcebook describing Pralix's war against Dav'nalleous, referenced in-text.

name: Little William
description: A Redcap over six feet tall and heavily built who obtained a longevity potion; the only Redcap to wear armor (enchanted lighter chainmail) and a skilled fighter.

name: Living
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab's structure is alive, e.g. inside a faerie tree or the belly of a slumbering beast (-2 Safety, +2 Warping).

name: Living Quarters
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab contains furniture so the owner can live and sleep in it, a small benefit to lab work but bad for health.

name: Llewellyn
description: The last primus of House Diedne, last seen at Bryn-Celli-Ddu, whose parting words (Llewellyn's Curse) are carved into the passage wall there.

name: Llewellyn's Curse
description: The carved parting words of Llewellyn, last primus of House Diedne, vowing that the House will last and return to haunt its enemies as long as nature endures.

name: Llewelyn
description: The last primus of House Díedne, whose name fueled magi's belief that Gruffyd ap Llewelyn was a returned Díedne magus.

name: Llywelyn
description: The prince of Wales who nominally acknowledges Henry as lord but controls south Wales and wages low-level war on the Anglo-Norman Marcher barons.

name: Llywelyn ab Iorwerth
description: Prince of Gwynedd since 1194, a great warrior and politician who has come nearer than anyone since the Romans to unifying Wales.

name: Lochoch of Fox Lungs
description: A Theriac of Level 20, Potency Strong, a syrupy medicine made from boiled honey that cures phthisis, a Major phlegmatic disease, over a month.

name: Locksmiths' Guild
description: The guild of locksmiths, which historically did not develop until the late 14th and early 15th centuries; in the 13th century locks are made by specialist smiths.

name: Lohengrin
description: The golden-haired knight drawn by a swan who defeated Telramund and wedded Elsa on condition she never ask his name; he departed when she finally did. His legend forms part of Wolfram von Eschenbach's Parzival.

name: Loire
description: A river near whose mouth an island was a college for Druidic priestesses in the years before the formation of the Order.

name: Loki
description: The multi-faceted and often malevolent Norse god from whom some Ex Miscellanea claim the Nemthengacha tradition descends.

name: Long Meg and Her Daughters
description: A roughly hundred-meter stone circle in the Lake District whose stones cannot be reliably counted and are thought to be the petrified bodies of a witch and her daughters; Long Meg is a sandstone pillar that bleeds if chipped.

name: Long Winded
description: A Virtue possessed by all Rottweiler grogs.

name: Look at Me
description: A Creo Mentem spell that creates a thought in a target's imagination, causing him to look directly at the caster and make eye contact.

name: Loose Magic
description: A Minor Hermetic Flaw that halves the magus's Advancement Total whenever he tries to Master spells.

name: Lord Guigues of Dauphiné
description: A noble who commissioned Hephaestion to build a mechanized tin magpie automaton for his bedchamber.

name: Lord of the Trees
description: A Rego Herbam spell (Level 25) that causes a tree to move its branches and bend its trunk as mentally directed; a large tree gains Initiative, Attack, and Damage scores.

name: Lore-master
description: A covenfolk template scholar versed in many Lore Abilities including Arcane Lores such as Dominion, Faerie, Infernal, Magic, and Order of Hermes Lore.

name: Lorelei
description: A nymph that haunts the Rhine and sings men to their doom.

name: Lorris
description: A small town in France first granted customary rights by King Louis VI, later confirmed by Louis VII in 1155, whose generous customs included freeman status after a year and a day.

name: Lost in the Memory
description: A Muto Mentem spell that fills the target's mind with memory, causing him to relive past scenes while neglecting all but basic urges.

name: Lotharingia
description: The middle kingdom of the divided Carolingian empire that belonged to Lothar, later reabsorbed into Germany and divided into Upper and Lower Lorraine.

name: Lousy Ingredients
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the lab is supplied with dirty, impure, or poor-quality ingredients (-1 General Quality, -1 Upkeep).

name: Low Ceiling
description: A Free laboratory Structure Flaw: the ceiling is below the requisite ten feet, hampering some magical activities (-1 General Quality, -1 Safety, -1 Aesthetics).

name: Low Tolerance
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character cannot easily withstand pain and fatigue, increasing related penalties.

name: Lucas
description: A magus of the Waddenzee covenant whom Imanitos got on well with during his stay there.

name: Lucas von Beck
description: An aggressive Follower of Flambeau at Waddenzee (age 45), son of a German altgraf and expert in Perdo magics who has begun studying necromancy using bodies from his pirate raids.

name: Lucidia of Flambeau
description: A young Flambeau maga, one of the newly arrived members of Libellus.

name: Luctatio
description: A covenant in the Roman Tribunal between Milan and Verona, founded in 1172, heavily involved in Lombard politics; its Tytalus magi aided Milan against Barbarossa.

name: Lucy
description: The wife of the Redcap Perceval, living at Mercer House with their children; she believes their daughter Maud has the Gift.

name: Lug
description: The Celtic and Gallic god of trade and commerce, also a sun deity associated with war, crafts, poetry, music, and magic, known as Lleu, Lugh, and Lugus.

name: Lumen's ring
description: A ring possessed by Lumen of Jerbiton that makes her appear as a man, allowing her to travel to monasteries in disguise.

name: Luneburg
description: A wealthy city built on extensive salt mines, where subsidence causes houses to tilt over rickety streets.

name: Lungs of the Fish
description: A Muto Aquam spell (Level 20) with an Auram requisite that turns water into air as it enters the lungs, allowing the caster to breathe water.

name: Lupercus
description: Ulf's ancestor who haunts the Bielowezca Forest as an immense wolf Great Beast and may impart the secret of the Inner Heartbeast.

name: Lust for Life
description: A Major Curse (Creo Mentem effect) making the victim obsessed with sensual pleasure, requiring rolls to do anything besides follow compulsions.

name: Lux Draconis
description: An undistinguished covenant founded in 915 in the Pennines; barely clinging to survival, it died out by 1100 and Blackthorn claimed its property.

name: Lymphae
description: Water elementals (the 'pure waters') rarefied only from naturally occurring liquids; the best learners among elementals, they collect and mix substances and attack by pulling foes down to smother them.

name: Lyonesse
description: A drowned land that once stretched from Cornwall to the Scilly Isles, Tristan's birthplace, sunk by the anger of the Fair Folk; its town was called Lyon and its remains can be seen at low tide.

name: Madrasah
description: An Islamic higher-education school attached to a mosque and run by religious leaders, privately endowed and supported by student tuition.

name: Maenads
description: Women devoted to Dionysus who tore Orpheus limb from limb in a wild rampage.

name: Magdeburg
description: A city on the Elbe favored by Otto the Great, seat of an archbishopric and center of missionary activity over the Eastern Marches; origin of the Magdeburg Law.

name: Magi Orbi
description: Magi who began in a different House but were exiled and found refuge in House Ex Miscellanea; they retain their former House's rules but lose its privileges and secrets.

name: Magians
description: The original priestly caste of Persia, of which the Median tribe of Magians were the true blood ancestors granting the Magian Lineage Virtue.

name: Magic Addiction
description: A Major Hermetic Flaw in which the magus craves casting magic and struggles to stop casting spells until he drops from exhaustion.

name: Magic Item (Virtue)
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: a magic item is installed in the lab, granting Virtues, Flaws, or Specialization changes; treated as Minor if very large.

name: Magic Items
description: A Minor General Virtue granting a Redcap 25 extra starting levels of magic items plus accelerated improvement, reflecting devotion to the House.

name: Magic Theory roll
description: Library trap mechanic: a magus following uncorrected deliberate-error lab notes who fails an Intelligence + Magic Theory roll against Ease Factor 12 rolls as if he botched an experiment.

name: Magical (Being) Companion
description: A Minor Story Flaw in which the character is accompanied by an intelligent magical being he must regularly look after.

name: Magical Animal Companion
description: A useful minor Flaw giving a character a magical animal companion; listed as a resource increasing an agent's Resistance Strength.

name: Magical Beast
description: A creature of magic with Magic Might that can be created at high levels of Creo Animal, requiring requisites for its powers and a Vim requisite for its magical nature.

name: Magical Fascination
description: A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character is intensely interested in supernatural and magical phenomena to the exclusion of other motivations.

name: Magical Heating
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: heating is provided magically, functioning as Superior or Excessive Heating without space and Upkeep cost.

name: Magical Lighting
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: lighting is provided magically, functioning as Superior or Excessive Lighting without space and Upkeep cost.

name: Magical Memory
description: A Minor Hermetic Virtue allowing a magus to reproduce magical creations without keeping laboratory texts, getting the benefit of a Lab Text from memory.

name: Magical Mount
description: A Minor General Virtue granting a mount or beast-of-burden with Cunning and a Magic Might Score up to 25 that obeys simple verbal commands.

name: Magical Oven
description: A Creo Ignem 20 enchanted device shaped as an iron box encased in fire-brick whose interior becomes red-hot on command to cook food.

name: Magical Wolf
description: A magical creature (Magic Might 20, Animal) resembling a slightly large gray wolf that watches over all wolves in its range, can split into a pack of duplicates, and instantly slay any wolf it strikes.

name: Magical constructs
description: Non-human servants at Ungulus, including human-form constructs, self-working animated brooms, knives and pans, warning bells, and invisible bound spirits serving as guards and messengers.

name: Magister et Artibus
description: A Major Social Virtue (university master of arts) listed as a high-Resistance social status on the Resistance of Agents Table.

name: Magnantrum
description: Covenant founded around 1111 in a cave under Salisbury Plain; disintegrated in 1187 due to internal disputes.

name: Maiden Castle
description: A large set of hilltop earthworks south of Dorchester in Dorset, seemingly deserted but said in local tales to be a faerie stronghold where the fay may be met on the correct night.

name: Maimonides
description: A Jewish philosopher who wrote The Guide for the Perplexed in 1190, a great summa on Jewish philosophy infused with Aristotelian ideas, sparking the Maimonidean Controversy.

name: Mainz
description: Formerly the Roman city Moguntiacum, raised to an archbishopric by St. Boniface; its archbishop is Archchancellor of the Empire and primas germaniae, and its see is a Holy See with a Divine aura of 7.

name: Major Breakthrough
description: A significant advance in Hermetic theory; the Aegis of the Hearth was a Major Breakthrough, while inventing variant parameters of it would require at least a Minor Breakthrough.

name: Major Magical Focus in Spirits
description: A Major Magical Focus developed by Titanoi magi during apprenticeship, applying to all supernatural entities with a naturally insubstantial form including ghosts.

name: Maker of Textured Vessels
description: A Minor Supernatural Virtue allowing a character to craft vessels with impressed mystical patterns that grant a +3 bonus in a single Ability to their owner.

name: Maker of Water Vessels
description: A Minor Supernatural Virtue allowing a character to make magical water vessels whose drinker may swap an Ability score for the crafter's Craft: Potter score.

name: Malediction
description: A Flaw a sahir might acquire from botched dealings with jinn during apprenticeship.

name: Malignant Magus
description: A Minor Story Supernatural Flaw where a Twilight-loosed piece of the magus's psyche manifests as an adulteration that attacks his enemies without his consent.

name: Manifest Sin
description: A Minor Supernatural Flaw in which a past sin stains the character's spirit and is manifest to those who can perceive hidden things, penalizing social interactions.

name: Mannus
description: Son of the god Tuisto, from whom the word 'man' derives, who sired the fathers of the three German tribal groups.

name: Marbaid of Flambeau
description: A magus of House Flambeau whose wizard's sigil is connected to an obsession with blood, turning his water spells into gushes of blood.

name: Marcher Lords
description: Anglo-Norman lords holding land in or along the borders of Wales, including the Marshals, de Braoses, Mortimers, and Bohuns, whose lordships function much like palatinates.

name: Marco
description: A disreputable Redcap, frequently described as a liar and charlatan, who reports many strange tales of covenants.

name: Margaret of Beverley
description: An English-born pilgrim who disguised herself as a man and helped defend the wall when Jerusalem fell to Saladin in 1187, later becoming a nun at Laon; an example of a woman warrior dressing as a man.

name: Marguerite of Flambeau
description: A beautiful but rude maga of House Flambeau, sole inhabitant of Fengheld's Fengheld House chapter in Cherbourg, who considers mundanes beneath her.

name: Maria
description: A young woman near Mount Etna who has the Visions Flaw, feeling an empathy for fire and able to predict the volcano's eruptions through her dreams.

name: Marie de France
description: A twelfth-century poet whose twelve lais are the best-known examples of that form of courtly-love poem.

name: Marking the Territory
description: A ReCo 15 Scent-Target spell that bars Corpus-associated intruders from a warded area marked by the caster's scent.

name: Martial of Tytalus
description: A magus of House Tytalus who collects turtle shells inscribed with bellicose Latin quotations.

name: Martin of Pattishall
description: The senior professional justice at the court of the King's Bench.

name: Martin the Alchemist
description: An example philosopher and alchemist with Philosophiae 5 who learns and concocts the Cement reagent and writes Laboratory Texts for fellow alchemists.

name: Maruhs
description: One of Birna's six apprentices, told to 'Strive,' from her own tribe, whose name means 'stallion' in Old Gothic; founder of Clan Maruhs.

name: Marut
description: One of two fallen angels who, per the Qur'an, taught sihr (magic) to mankind to tempt them from Islam.

name: Mask the Odor of Magic
description: A spell used in conjunction with a magically maintained persona enchantment to hide magical traces.

name: Masons' Guild
description: The only craft guild that operates internationally, whose members travel across Mythic Europe in army-like groups to build cathedrals, churches, and castles.

name: Master (Virtue)
description: A free Social Status Virtue specific to the Rhine, granting the rank of magister, the right to train apprentices, and the use of a retired magus's voting sigil.

name: Master of Kennels
description: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a character who manages the kennels of a noble patron, responsible for training, breeding, and health of the dogs.

name: Master of None
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character cannot stick at a task for longer than a season, preventing reapplication of experience points to the same Ability or Art in a year.

name: Mastering the Unruly Beast
description: A Rego Animal spell (Level 25) allowing the caster to command an animal to perform any act it is capable of by touching it.

name: Mathieus of Constantinople
description: A contemporary House Jerbiton Archmagus trained in Constantinople but long resident in Paris, who gave up the study of magic but grew more active after Constantinople's fall.

name: Matthew II
description: The duke who succeeds Dietrich III as duke of Upper Lorraine in 1220.

name: Maud (daughter of Perceval)
description: The two-year-old daughter of the Redcap Perceval and Lucy, suspected of having the Gift.

name: Mausoleum of Herlicarnasus
description: An epic site chosen as the headquarters of the example league The Singers in Hollow Rooms.

name: Mecklenburg
description: A region whose nobility still secretly come to Rethra to honor their god; its Slavic princes are drawn into the schemes of Radegast.

name: Medieval Universities
description: Autonomous corporations of masters and scholars seeking independence from ecclesiastical and secular authority; in 1220 there are nine, organized into faculties, nations, and hospices.

name: Meles of Bjornaer
description: A young Bjornaer magus, one of the newly arrived members of Libellus.

name: Melusine
description: A water faerie whose blood is borne by the Breton Seirenes bards.

name: Memory of the Distant Dream
description: A Creo Mentem spell (Level 20) that inserts a full false memory into a person's mind, revealed as false on a successful Intelligence roll; the memory vanishes when the duration expires.

name: Men-an-Tol
description: A holed round stone with two pillars in a Cornish field, said to have healing powers (crawling through the hole) and divinatory powers (placing a gift and asking a question).

name: Menagerie
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab contains a collection of live animals (+1 Upkeep, -1 Safety, -1 Aesthetics, +2 Animal).

name: Mental Construct
description: A Major laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab exists entirely in the magus's mind via a powerful Creo Mentem ritual, limited by his Intelligence and unable to support familiar-bonding, item enchantment, or teaching.

name: Merchant Guild
description: A guild of merchants granted by charter, holding monopolies (such as Ipswich's monopoly on milling) and operating a court for resolving disputes in towns like Freiburg.

name: Merchant Venturer
description: A Social Status Virtue used to purchase the Typical merchant income band.

name: Mercurian cults
description: Cults among the Hermetic magi whose members often succumb to the Vulnerable Casting Flaw.

name: Mercurian lineage
description: A Hermetic magical lineage descended from the Roman priests of Mercury, granting Mercurian Magic and predating the Order of Hermes.

name: Meririm the Meridian Devil
description: A demon who commands the demons haunting the meridian region between the poles and rules an Order of Aerial Powers.

name: Merlin's Well
description: A spring on the escarpment of Alderley Edge in Cheshire, marked by an inscription and a carved face said to represent Merlin, where Arthur and his knights are said to sleep beneath the Edge.

name: Merry Maidens
description: A stone circle of nineteen granite boulders at Land's End, said to be girls turned to stone for dancing on Sunday to the music of the Pipers, who were demons.

name: Metz
description: The largest and most important city of Upper Lorraine, originally Roman Divodurum, a wealthy Free Imperial City since 1143 and former capital of Austrasia and Lotharingia.

name: Microcosmic Station
description: An advanced Station on the Criamon Path of the Body; Primi who achieve it are active administrators coordinating the House's ventures.

name: Midusulf
description: One of Birna's six apprentices, told to 'Lead,' founder of Clan Midusulf, whose name means 'mead-wolf' (bear) in Old Gothic.

name: Midwife
description: An almost exclusively female practitioner whose Chirurgy skills are employed throughout pregnancy and childbirth, sometimes having her thumbs surgically removed to assist births.

name: Milan
description: A north Italian city near the iron mines of the southern Alps, famous for armaments and its capacity to produce enormous numbers of weapons to order.

name: Mild Aging
description: A Minor General Virtue granting a +1 bonus to the Living Conditions Modifier on aging rolls and a +3 bonus to survive an aging crisis.

name: Milo of Bonisagus
description: An Archmage of House Bonisagus who prepared for his archmage contest while a member of Schola Pythagoranis, then joined Durenmar.

name: Mimer the Old
description: A minor deity in the Scandinavian pantheon from whom Wayland learned smith-craft techniques.

name: Mimizan
description: A covenant in the Provençal Tribunal with only two members, one of whom is the Praeco Dama.

name: Minerva
description: A pagan goddess whose image in high relief is carved into rock just south of Chester and is said to continue to watch over the city.

name: Minnesingers
description: A type of German minstrel copying the northern French style with emphasis on knightly combat and sensual love, exemplified by Walther and Wolfram.

name: Minor Enchantments
description: A Minor Supernatural Virtue giving the character items with magical powers designed as Hermetic enchantments totaling 25 levels or less.

name: Minor Potency
description: A Virtue granted at the first Station of the Criamon Path of the Body, conferring potency in an aspect of the Art of Corpus.

name: Minor Supernatural Ability
description: A Virtue granting a minor supernatural power, gained by long-lived Durenmar covenfolk in their seventh decade.

name: Miracles
description: The direct intervention of God in the world, which can do anything, cannot fail, and cannot be resisted by any other power including creature Magic Resistance.

name: Miriam
description: Flavius of Jerbiton's wife, of unclear cultural group and magical tradition; she attended the First Tribunal in an undescribed capacity and is buried beside Jerbiton.

name: Missing Ear
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character cannot accurately locate the direction of sounds, suffering a penalty to hearing rolls.

name: Missing Equipment
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Flaw: a lack of equipment makes one or two activity types totally impossible (-1 Upkeep).

name: Missing Hand
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character has lost a hand, penalizing climbing, combat, and activities requiring both hands.

name: Missing Ingredients
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: a lack of certain ingredients severely hampers one Technique or two Forms, halving relevant Lab Totals (-1 Upkeep).

name: Missing Sanctum Marker
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the sanctum marker is not prominently displayed or is missing, inviting Hermetic intrusion (-1 Aesthetics).

name: Mists of Change
description: A Muto Corpus ritual (Level 60) with an Animal requisite in which patches of mist transform anyone remaining in the target area into a random creature for a Year.

name: Mithras
description: A luminous Persian-origin sun god worshiped by the Cult of Mithras as savior of Creation and divine Bull-Slayer; Castra Solis is named for his sun-god aspect.

name: Mithridates VI
description: King of Pontus and enemy of Rome who employed Crateuas as court physician; his potions let him survive poison and torture.

name: Moat Monster
description: A creature serving as a Local Ally for the Military Camp covenant situation, also referenced as a covenant Boon.

name: Mobile
description: A Free laboratory Structure Virtue: the entire lab can be readily moved, e.g. on a ship or cart, usually taken with the Unstable Flaw (+1 Experimentation).

name: Monastic Vows (Hermetic)
description: A Major Hermetic Flaw in which the magus has taken vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience, forbidding him from owning vis and limiting him to functional magic devices.

name: Monica Ierne
description: The second-in-command of House Tremere, an Archmaga and master of combat magic originally from the Stonehenge Tribunal who serves as an excellent field commander.

name: Monstrous Blood
description: A Minor Supernatural Flaw in which the character's essential nature has been changed through exposure to the Magic realm, giving her true form unfortunate supernatural properties and a visible deformity, while granting a -1 bonus to Aging rolls.

name: Morag
description: A giant driven from his mountain home by diabolists who has taken to robbery near a covenant, holding a captured knight hostage in a cave; he craves revenge against the diabolists.

name: Moravia
description: The eastern March of Bohemia bordered by the Carpathian Mountains and Hungary, through which flows the River Morava; home of the covenant of Roznov.

name: Morlen of Merinita
description: A young Merinita magus among the members recruited to Nigrasaxa.

name: Mortuary Society of Kassala
description: A society in Kassala, Alodia that makes Kassalan Dust and practices Kassalan Exorcism rites against ghosts and the physical dead.

name: Moses
description: Biblical prophet referenced in the Divine setting material.

name: Motion Sickness
description: A Minor General Flaw causing the character to become violently ill when riding a horse, in a cart, or sailing, doubling fatigue loss on long journeys.

name: Mount Blanik
description: A mountain covered by a Divine regio, with an underground cavern holding the sleeping army of St. Wenceslaus, the Knights of Blanik, awaiting Bohemia's direst need.

name: Mount Olympus
description: The mountain home of the Greek gods from which Hephaestus was twice cast out; also the location of an all-Verditius covenant and a Forge of Hephaestus.

name: Mount Pilatus
description: A mountain in the Alps where climbing can generate terrible storms, cited as an example of a Site of Weakness Hook.

name: Mount Purgatory
description: A mountain commonly believed to sit at the center of the antipodal region directly opposite Jerusalem, atop Hell, a place of contrition and repentance.

name: Mount Saint Odile
description: A mountain in the northern Vosges housing the convent of St. Odile and a holy spring with a Divine aura of 4, a place of pilgrimage especially for those with eye diseases.

name: Mountaintop
description: A Free laboratory Structure Virtue: the lab sits at a mountain peak, a dramatic remote setting prone to winds and snows (-1 Safety, +1 Upkeep, +2 Aesthetics, +2 Auram).

name: Mournful Mound
description: A hill containing the barrow of the Black Serpent, reached beyond the court of the sons of the King of Suffering, where Peredur slew the serpent.

name: Muirgheal
description: A Quaesitor who led the Order's investigation into the Normandy restless-dead crisis and invited the Gifted Donatores to join the Order en masse.

name: Mummel Lake
description: An enchanted isolated lake near Seebach in the Black Forest, home to a Nixe (water-nymph) whose jealous elemental spirits may slay the mortals she bewitches.

name: Munster
description: A prosperous market and episcopal city on the Munsterland plain, founded as a monastery in 805 to convert the Saxons.

name: My New Best Friend
description: A Creo Mentem 25 spell of Henri de Tours that makes a target believe the caster is an old friend by substituting the caster for one of the target's real friends.

name: Myrmecoleon
description: A mythical creature whose exoskeleton provides a Shape and Material bonus of +6 to deprivation and starvation effects.

name: Mystery of Ascendancy to the Hall of Heroes
aliases: Ascendancy to the Hall of Heroes
description: The innermost Mystery of the Huntress, Initiated as the Chosen of Diana via a Quest to find and slay Quendalon in Arcadia, a great Sacrifice, and ritual blinding.

name: Mystery of Divination
description: A Major Virtue acquired through Clan Ilfetu's Trial and Oath of the Prophet, alongside the Visions Flaw.

name: Mystery of Divination and Augury
aliases: Esoteric Mystery of Divination and Augury
description: An Esoteric Mystery into which Clan Ilfetu members may be Initiated, teaching the haemagmomancy divination method.

name: Mystery of Hermetic Synthemata
description: The Mystery into which a new hierophant of the Huntress is Initiated, vital to controlling the pagan messiah they hope to create.

name: Mystery of the Anima
description: A Major House Mystery of House Bjornaer that transforms the heartbeast into a spiritual or elemental form composed of an element such as earth, fire, air, water, smoke, or shadow.

name: Mystery of the Epitome
description: A Major House Mystery of House Bjornaer that perfects the heartbeast into a Beast of Virtue, granting Characteristic bonuses, Mythic Feats, and immunity to physical Flaws in inner form.

name: Mythic Feat
description: An automatically successful incredible action a Beast of Virtue may perform at the cost of a confidence Point, covering feats of Perception, Presence, Strength, and other Characteristics.

name: Mythic Germany
description: The magic-soaked lands of medieval Germany within the Holy Roman Empire, birthplace of the Order of Hermes and setting of the Rhine Tribunal.

name: Nameless Covenant
description: A Díedne covenant established on an ancient druidic shrine on Anglesey in 817, destroyed in 1011 and stricken from the records by the quaesitores after the Schism War.

name: Names of Power
description: A Mystery Virtue the Titanoi cult can Initiate.

name: Naples
description: A city whose catacombs harbored the necromancer Guorna the Fetid and her tradition, which Tytalus and Tremere destroyed.

name: Narrowly Cognizant
description: A Free Virtue indicating a faerie is aware of its faerie nature in a limited way; it tries to play its role accurately and cannot break role even unto death.

name: Natrix
description: The filius of Lacerta in a Clan Arelie sept in Iberia.

name: Natura Antiqua
description: A covenant of nature magi founded in the East Anglian fens in 1133, destroyed by Geoffrey de Mandeville during the Civil War in 1143.

name: Natural Environment
description: A Major laboratory Structure Virtue: natural scenery such as forest, desert, or river is in or around the lab, granting Aesthetics and terrain-appropriate Specializations.

name: Natural Magician
description: A practitioner of non-Hermetic natural magic; Amabel the Learned is one, as powerful as many Hermetic magi, and some churchmen have begun employing such magicians.

name: Naumburg
description: A well-fortified town high above the River Saale with its own bishop, beginning construction of a cathedral dedicated to St. Peter and St. Paul.

name: Nebelkönigin
description: A magically enhanced ship, pride of Waddenzee's pirate fleet, stolen from Oculus Septentrionalis (built by the Verditius shipwright Marcus) while it carried vis and magical books.

name: Necessary (Realm) Aura for (Ability)
description: A Minor Supernatural Flaw giving a -3 penalty to a particular Ability when the character is not in the appropriate supernatural aura.

name: Necessity
description: The underlying laws of the universe in Criamon cosmology that forced the immortals into the cycle of time for three eternities.

name: Nef
description: The main carvel-built trade ship of the Mediterranean, following a Roman design with lateen rigging borrowed from the Arabs and up to three masts.

name: Neo-Mercurians
description: A Hermetic Mystery Cult interested in Roman ceremonies and culture, said to be related to the Cult of Mercury.

name: Nephilim (Virtue)
description: The Free Mythic Companion Virtue defining a character as a Nephilim.

name: Neptune's Brooch
description: A wondrous carved precious stone made by a jeweler that prevents the wearer from drowning by letting him float on water (Craft Level 14).

name: Neptune's Imprisoning Arms
description: A Muto Aquam spell (MuAq 25) created by Falke that forms semi-solid 'vines' of water that can hold a small boat or up to six people, operating like Trap of the Entwining Vines.

name: Nestor
description: Iacob's faerie caricature, a white (albino) crow that accompanies him on his travels and identifies him as the Prophet of the God of Truth.

name: Nestor of Tremere
description: The current curator (head) of the oppidum of Tablinum, who holds a collection of Arcane Connections used to enter its regiones.

name: New Aristotle
description: The body of newly translated works of Aristotle dubbed by scholastic leaders, central to the twelfth-century recovery of philosophical knowledge.

name: New Forest
description: A royal forest in England cited as a legendary forestry income example.

name: Niall
description: The example player who creates the magus Darius of Flambeau throughout the Detailed Character Creation worked example.

name: Nibelungs
description: A legendary race of men from the Lower Rhine who collaborated with dwarves and giants to conquer the wild river; their lost treasure is the Rhinegold.

name: Night Terrors
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is plagued by horrible nightmares, requiring a Stress Roll against Ease Factor 9 to avoid terrors and Long Term Fatigue loss.

name: Nike
description: The Daimon of victory in both battle and peaceful competition, daughter of Styx and Pallas, invoked in an Orphic Hymn used in eristic moots.

name: Niobe
description: A Criamon maga who longed to be Prima but was never selected; her perfect transmission created a study pond as she faded into Twilight.

name: Nixe
description: A water-nymph faerie dwelling in the enchanted Mummel Lake who bewitches young men with her beauty, drawing the jealousy of the lake's elemental spirits.

name: No Hands
description: A Major General Flaw in which the character has no hands; magi take a -5 penalty to all Casting Scores, offset by the Subtle Magic Virtue or Still Casting.

name: No Sense of Direction
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is completely unable to follow directions and frequently gets lost; incompatible with the Well Traveled Virtue.

name: No Stores
description: A Minor laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab has nowhere to store supplies and cannot withstand shortages (-2 Safety).

name: Nomos
description: In Tytalan philosophy, the abstract force of law, convention, or custom—a human invention that glues society together but is changeable and thus open to challenge.

name: Nortorf
description: A small town in Holstein at the meeting of roads to Schleswig, Lübeck, and Hamburg, site of the prophesied infernal ash seedling cut down each New Year's Night by a white horseman.

name: Notary
description: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a legal official employed by lords or towns who draws up contracts, witnesses charters, and affixes a seal.

name: Notger
description: Liege's most famous bishop, granted the diocese as a fiefdom by Otto II, responsible for many of Liege's grandest buildings, after whom it became a prince-bishopric.

name: Notre Dame de Paris
description: The Paris cathedral whose recently completed nave is 112 feet tall, with its chancellor wielding power over the university.

name: Nottingwood
description: A town in a story seed that entered a charter agreement with a faerie king, electing a council of seven aldermen and hosting faerie merchants and knights.

name: Nuremberg
description: An important Franconian trading city at a crossroads of trade routes, home to the Kaiserburg imperial castle and an unofficial capital of the empire.

name: Oath of Fealty
description: A Major Story Flaw in which the character has sworn loyalty and support to someone outside the covenant; magi are forbidden from such oaths by the Hermetic Code.

name: Obano
description: A 25-year-old journeyman swordsmith originally from Aragon, strong and scarred, who holds evidence of his former master's illegal dealings.

name: Obsessed
description: A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character is fixated on a prized object, action, or ideal that interferes with more immediate tasks.

name: Occulta
description: A covenant founded in the East Anglian fens in 893 by newly gauntleted magi; it failed to establish resources and collapsed in 897.

name: Odofredus
description: A great debater at Bologna and frontrunner for rector of the Faculty of Law, rival of Accursius in completing a legal digest.

name: Odysseus
description: The legendary hero whose famous tale of resisting the sirens illustrates how the Seirenes' magic could be defeated.

name: Offa's Dyke
description: A great earthwork of more than seventy miles marking the England-Wales boundary, completed in 787 with the faerie Huarwar's aid.

name: Ogam
description: Runes carved into trees and stones or written in ashes by the Damhadh-Duidsan to curse, steal life, inflict wounds, and heal.

name: Ogmios
description: A Gaulish god of strength, eloquence, and poetry worshiped at the western Vosges springs, identified by the Romans as Hercules.

name: Ointment for Congealing Blood
description: A Theriac of Level 20, Potency Moderate, a compress of tormentil and comfrey that stays bleeding and cures a Medium Wound from a slashing weapon over a month.

name: Ominous Levitation of the Weighty Stone
description: A ReTe 15 spell that moves a stone through the air; when released it falls naturally and bypasses Magic Resistance, dealing damage based on the stone's size with a successful aiming roll.

name: On Divers Arts
description: A famous craft manual by the monk Theophilus about painters, glass makers, and metalworkers that adds +4 to a craftsman's Workshop Total.

name: Opening the Tome of the Animal's Mind
description: An Intellego Animal spell (Level 25) that lets the caster read an animal's memories of the past day by touching its head.

name: Ophia Sirnaus Isle-Warden
description: Clan Chief of Clan Sirnas, a serpent-heartbeast maga who lives on an uninhabited Aegean island with a shrine to Artemis.

name: Opulent
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab is comfortable and well furnished (+1 Upkeep, +1 Health, +2 Aesthetics, +1 Teaching).

name: Order of Montjoie
description: The oldest of three monastic orders dedicated to ransoming slaves, now failing and negotiating to be absorbed by another order.

name: Order of St. John
description: A religious order that built the Jerusalem Hospital for those injured on Crusade.

name: Order of the Green Cockerel
description: A Hermetic group described in The Mysteries, Revised Edition, likely to include at least one member of the Collegium.

name: Order of the Lady of Mercy
description: An order of monks founded in 1218 dedicated to ransoming slaves.

name: Original Research
description: The pursuit of advancing Hermetic theory through novel investigation, which Pralicians are especially likely to undertake.

name: Orlando
description: A musician and magus who knows Sorcerous Music and Subtle Magic, used as an example of casting spells while singing or playing his lute.

name: Orn
description: The ancestor after whom the Clan Wilkis Sept of Orn is named.

name: Orphedra
description: A cruel Follower of Merinita at Dankmar (age 139), the covenant's link to the dark fae who specializes in illusions, cold, darkness, and fear; she taught Schadrit Faerie Magic.

name: Orpheus
description: The legendary Thracian poet, musician, and magician taught by Hermes, regarded by his cult as the first user of Hermetic magic and who descended to the Underworld for Eurydice.

name: Ossium of Bjornaer
description: A magus of House Bjornaer whose version of Talons of the Winds produces an eerie keening sound; his wizard's sigil makes many of his spells eerie or frightening.

name: Otto I
description: Son of Henry the Fowler, crowned at Aachen in 936, who defeated the Magyars at the Battle of the Lech (Lechfeld) in 955 and was crowned emperor in Rome in 962.

name: Outdoors
description: A Major laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab is not housed in a building and is fully exposed to the elements, taken with the Natural Environment Virtue.

name: Owein son of Uryen
description: A figure at Arthur's court in the Dream of Rhonabwy who played gwyddbwyll with Arthur while his magical ravens battled Arthur's men.

name: Owl of Virtue
description: A Great Beast Mythic Blood lineage granting the Silence of the Smothered Sound feat, a Focus in Ghosts, and the Nocturnal flaw.

name: Paderborn
description: A town at the source of the River Pader, famous as the site of the 799 meeting of Charlemagne and Pope Leo III that agreed the establishment of the Holy Roman Empire.

name: Pagan Theology
description: An Ability covering non-Christian religious doctrine; the second book of Aristotle's Metaphysics is a tractatus on it.

name: Painting
description: A Craft/Profession Ability representing skill at painting, used in the example maestro Grifo's Aesthetic Quality calculations.

name: Palatial
description: A Major laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab is lavishly outfitted with the best comforts and decoration (+1 General Quality, +3 Upkeep, +2 Health, +4 Aesthetics).

name: Pancrestis
aliases: Pancrestis filius Occultes, Follower of Bonisagus
description: A young journeyman of House Bonisagus at Heorot, filius of Occultes and mentored by Philippus Niger, keen to learn Norse magic but deeply fearful of the wilderness.

name: Pandora
description: A clay woman that Hephaestus made for Zeus, listed among his famous treasures.

name: Panther of Virtue
description: A symbolic beast whose hide provides a Shape and Material bonus of +6 to song and melodious sounds.

name: Paralyze a Man at R: Eye
description: The magical feat granted to magi of the Wolf of Virtue Mythic Blood lineage.

name: Paris (son of Priam)
description: Son of the faerie lord Priam of Ilium, who holds a beauty contest during Ilium's mid-summer fair.

name: Parsirus
description: A Verditius magus of Ungulus, beloved of Sinead, who was killed by the dragon.

name: Parzival
description: A poem by Wolfram von Eschenbach of which the legend of the swan knight Lohengrin forms part.

name: Pass the Unyielding Portal
description: A Muto Herbam spell (Level 5) that makes the wood of a door pliable, allowing the magus to bend it open regardless of most locks or bars.

name: Path
description: A House Criamon tradition combining a field of study, set of values, and lifestyle, each granting different Mystery Virtues; clutches originally followed a single path.

name: Path of Aging
description: A forest path through which Alexander of Jerbiton sought to reverse aging, requiring sacrifices and a quest to drink from the Fountain of Youth, yielding the Immortality of the Forest Virtue.

name: Path of Energy
description: A forest path discovered by Terious of Flambeau to replenish spent spellcasting energy from the forest, yielding the Life Boost and Mythic Blood Virtues.

name: Path of Warping
description: A forest path walked by Kleon of Criamon to influence the effect of Wizard's Twilight on his Gift, yielding the Puissant Enigmatic Wisdom and Twilight Mastery Virtues.

name: Paths through the Forest
description: A tradition of nature magic inherited from Merinita, walked by many exsules, which may let them overcome one or more of the Lesser Limits of Hermetic magic.

name: Patron
description: A sponsor who agrees to support an artist for an undetermined length of time, funding all of his work; losing one costs 12 Artist Reputation experience points.

name: Peasant
description: A Free Social Status Virtue for a free (non-serf) character who lives by working the land, possibly controlling and hiring labor if wealthy.

name: Peitho
description: The Daimon of persuasion and charming speech, daughter of Styx and Pallas, who with her sister Bia represents forceful inducement.

name: Pelagius
description: One of Jerbiton's allies who traveled Europe seeking further recruits for the expanding House.

name: Pelican of Virtue
description: A symbolic bird whose beak provides a Shape and Material bonus of +8 to healing and nurturing.

name: Penetration Ability
description: An Ability that provides a Penetration bonus; creatures and characters without it have a Penetration bonus of zero.

name: Penteli
description: The marble quarries near Athens, cited as a legendary mining income example.

name: Perceive Motives
description: An Intellego Mentem effect (InMe 10) enchanted into Falke's talisman, like Sight of the Transparent Motive but with zero Penetration to avoid affecting Hermetic magi.

name: Perceive the Eyes of Knives
description: A new Intellego Mentem spell (InMe 20) invented for Tabanus that indicates whether anyone in the target room has hostile thoughts toward the caster.

name: Perception of Conflicting Motives
description: An Intellego Mentem 15 spell known by Imanitos Mendax.

name: Perception of the Conflicting Motives
description: An Intellego Mentem spell (Level 15) that detects the conflicting motives behind a target's actions, often cast before a Muto or Rego spell to change emotions.

name: Perceval
description: A Redcap in his late forties contemplating retirement; tall, thin, balding, married to Lucy, with a brooch that makes him and his horse invisible.

name: Peredur
description: A knight-hero of a Mabinogion tale who slew the Black Oppressor and the Black Serpent of the Barrow with the aid of a magic stone given by a mysterious lady.

name: Peredur's concealment stone
description: A magic stone given to Peredur by a mysterious lady that hid him from the seeing stone pillar guarding the Black Serpent's cave, letting him slay the serpent unseen.

name: Performance Artist
description: An artist who performs art using a Profession Ability, such as jugglers, musicians, and minstrels, taking the Social Status Virtue Wanderer.

name: Persephone
description: The queen of the Greek Underworld who, with Hades, was moved by Orpheus's song; the sirens felt guilt at failing to save her from Hades.

name: Persia
description: The land of the Magians, original priestly caste, and home to most Mazdean communities, lying east of Mythic Europe.

name: Person
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Virtue: another person, such as a family member or maid, frequents the lab (-1 Safety, +1 Corpus or Mentem).

name: Personal Power
description: A Minor Supernatural Virtue giving the character an at-will supernatural power equivalent to a Formulaic Hermetic spell of level 25 or lower.

name: Personality Flaw
description: A category of Flaw reflected by an extreme Personality Trait that shapes how a character behaves.

name: Pessimistic
description: A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character always expects the worst.

name: Peter Lombard
description: A scholar who taught at pre-university Bologna and Paris and wrote the Sentences and biblical glosses, compared in a story seed to the works of a Hermetic writer.

name: Peter the Lombard
description: Author of the Sententiae (Sentences), one of the authoritative sources for the Academic Ability Theology: Christian.

name: Peter von Wurzburg
description: A master of House Verditius at Fengheld, a famed grower of grapes and maker of wine who cultivates special varieties into wine as Charged Items.

name: Petronilla of Leicester
description: A woman recorded as having armed herself as a knight and fought in battles during the reign of Henry II; a namesake later haggled the right to choose her own husband. An example of absence-based female power.

name: Petrus Musandinus
description: A great Salernitan master under whom Gilles de Corbeil trained in medicine.

name: Phaeton
description: A young sun god of folklore who, in river myth, drowned in the Po after falling from the solar chariot, his body never recovered.

name: Phantasmal Fire
description: A Creo Imaginem spell with an Ignem requisite that makes an image of a fire that dances, illuminates, crackles, and apparently warms but does not actually burn; popular at gatherings of House Flambeau.

name: Pharmaceutical Theriac
description: An experimental-philosophy product forming part of the corpus of Medicine; a medicinal cure-all preparation, often a restorative, that some empirici sell genuinely and others fake.

name: Pharmocopoeians
description: A tradition referenced as the model for the Taltos, focused on herbcraft and pharmacology.

name: Phessallia of Merinita
description: An old, cold Merinita maga of Voluntas connected with the faeries of winter, skilled in Perdo, who possesses faerie items obtainable only as gifts.

name: Philip Augustus
description: King of France for whom Gilles de Corbeil serves as archiater (chief physician).

name: Philip of Oldcoates
description: The sheriff of Northumbria who holds Mitford castle and refuses to surrender it to Roger Bertram despite royal summons.

name: Phillipus de Grevia
description: The chancellor of Notre Dame at Paris, who holds power to confer degrees and excommunicate university members and uses these rights to dominate the masters.

name: Phimosis
description: A Minor Choleric Disease afflicting promiscuous men, caused by excess lust, usually clearing on its own.

name: Phlegethi
description: Fire elementals ('burners') that rarefy only from naturally occurring flame; short-lived, fast-moving creatures driven to burn and consume cold, that can beguile those who stare into their flames.

name: Phthisis
description: A Major Phlegmatic, epidemic Disease that pollutes the vital faculty with phlegm and spreads via putrid breath.

name: Phyllia
description: A master maga of House Bjornaer, the Eagle Elder at Crintera with a polecat heartbeast; a widely-traveled Harmonist and notorious gossip.

name: Physicus
description: A term applied to anyone with advanced education in both medicine and natural philosophy, distinguishing educated medics from educated chirurgeons.

name: Physis
description: In Tytalan philosophy, the abstract force of nature or self encompassing instincts, ambition, and competition, derived from a higher divine authority and thus permanent and unquestionable.

name: Piercing the Magical Veil
description: An Intellego Vim (InVi 20) spell that detects and analyzes magical power.

name: Pietro
description: A magus of House Diedne of Oakdell covenant against whom Cirion of Tremere declared Wizard War in 1004 AD.

name: Pillars of Hercules
description: Islands at the western edge of the known world near Granada, thought to contain uncontrolled gateways to Arcadia and the Magical realm.

name: Pisa
description: A north Italian city of famed merchants, favored by the Holy Roman Emperor, which acts as the port for landlocked Florence.

name: Plague of Frogs
description: A Rego Animal spell that spontaneously generates a swarm of up to thousands of frogs in a touched pool of water.

name: Plagued by Demon
description: A Flaw involving demonic persecution that cannot be taken if the saga excludes demons.

name: Plagued by a Demon
description: A Story Flaw granted to a child chosen by the demon Bordelon as her personal tormentor.

name: Plain of Wolves
description: A battlefield of the Schism War where the Tytali fought alongside Houses Tremere and Flambeau, referenced by the Tremere Primus Cercistum.

name: Plant's Withering Bane
description: A Perdo Herbam spell (Level 20) that withers and destroys one living plant up to the size of a small tree.

name: Pliny
description: The Roman author cited as mentioning an ancient mariner who circumnavigated Africa and found the place where much of Europe's gold originates.

name: Pneumonia
description: A Serious Phlegmatic Disease, an inflammation of the lungs caused by polluted air, prone to a Crisis on the seventh day.

name: Po
description: A river in which the young sun god Phaeton is said to have drowned after falling from the solar chariot.

name: Poena
description: The Prima of House Tremere at the domus magna Coeris in the Transylvanian Tribunal, said to know the names and strengths of every member of her House.

name: Poisoning the Will
description: A ritual spell that curses a place such as a valley, town, city, or covenant, gradually sapping the will and vitality from the people there.

name: Political Agent
description: A thematic covenfolk template skilled in Intrigue, Guile, and Order of Hermes Lore, employed by covenants involved in Hermetic politics.

name: Pollute Water
description: An Aquam power of the basilisk Sordus that turns all standing water within 5 paces stagnant and putrefies other liquids; he cannot control it.

name: Pomeranian Forest
description: One of Germany's most oppressive forests, dominated by pine, fir, holly, and evergreen oak; reputedly a stronghold of witches and werewolves and home to the sacred grove of Romowe.

name: Pomeranian tradition
description: A surviving pre-Hermetic magical tradition with which some of Bjornaer's descendants seek détente, fearing their Founder left it before learning all its rites.

name: Poor (Characteristic)
description: A Minor General Flaw lowering a Characteristic already at -3 or lower by one further point.

name: Poor Concentration
description: A Minor General Flaw giving the character a -3 penalty to Concentration rolls due to a short attention span.

name: Poor Disputer
description: A Minor General Flaw causing a character to suffer a -3 penalty on disputatio die rolls.

name: Poor Formulaic Magic
description: A Minor Hermetic Flaw subtracting 5 from every roll to cast Formulaic spells, though not Ritual spells.

name: Poor Living Conditions
description: A Minor General Flaw giving an additional -1 Living Conditions Modifier, cumulative with the base modifier.

name: Poor Reader
description: A common Flaw among the exsules, most of whom have studied from vis for their entire careers.

name: Poor Student
description: A Minor General Flaw subtracting 3 from Advancement Totals derived from teaching and books.

name: Poorly Insulated
description: A Minor laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab is poorly shielded from the outside, easily overheard and a nuisance to neighbors (-1 Safety, -1 Aesthetics).

name: Pope
description: The head of the Church, granted by the Divine a Magic Resistance of 25 (the highest among listed leaders) and an Aura of Rightful Authority, lost upon excommunication.

name: Pope Alexander III
description: Pope who issued an 1179 decree, followed by most communities, requiring the expulsion of lepers.

name: Pope Gregory VII
description: A church reformer who decreed in 1079 that all cathedrals must make schooling compulsory for priests.

name: Pope Gregory the Great
description: A pope, later a saint, at whose earnest request God allowed the Roman Emperor Trajan to be saved after death, with a warning not to ask such things again.

name: Pope Innocent III
description: The pope who established Dominic's Order in 1216, sanctioned the Franciscans, recognized subdeacons as a major order, and was himself a university man.

name: Pot Plants
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab contains dozens of potted plants (+1 Upkeep, +1 Aesthetics, +1 Herbam).

name: Potent Spells
description: Spells that gain a Potency bonus to Casting Score derived from Casting Items combined into the spell's design.

name: Pound of Enumerus
description: A Hermetic accounting concept named after the magus Enumerus: at least one pound of covenant spending each year that can never be fully accounted for.

name: Powys
description: An ancient Welsh principality in the central regions, centered on the fort of Mathrafal; home of Gwenwynwyn and the abbey of Strata Florida.

name: Praefactus of Bonisagus
description: A magus of House Bonisagus whose wizard's sigil makes him appear as dignified as possible; his version of Seven-league Stride always lets him arrive in a safe place.

name: Prague
description: Bohemia's principal settlement, straddling the River Vltava, with Prague Castle, the Basilicas of St. George and St. Vitus, and a large slave market controlled by the Knights of the Sword.

name: Preaching
description: A Profession-type Ability used to emotionally influence an audience or teach Theology; in 1220 almost exclusively practiced by Dominican friars.

name: Precarious
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab sits in a supernaturally dangerous place such as inside a volcano (-1 Safety).

name: Precious Ingredients
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab is supplied with more expensive ingredients than typical (+1 General Quality, +2 Upkeep, +1 Longevity Rituals).

name: Predecessor
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab retains foibles of its notable previous owner (-1 Safety, +1 Warping, +1 Experimentation).

name: Predictive Stigmata
description: A Minor Story Supernatural Flaw whose stigmata predict future challenges symbolically and may flee the body to become adulterations if ignored.

name: Prelum of Tremere
description: Goliard's filia at Blackthorn, a polite young maga with a remarkable talent for Vim, contrasting with her sister Fornax.

name: Premonstratensians
description: An order of regular canons relying on the Rule of St. Augustine.

name: Premysl
description: A farmer found plowing with two oxen who became Libuse's husband and the founder of Bohemia's ruling Premyslid dynasty.

name: Preserved
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: the lab or its contents are immune to natural decay (-1 Upkeep, +1 Warping, +2 Health, +1 Aesthetics, +1 Creo).

name: Pretense
description: A faerie's skill in mimicking a particular human Ability through glamour; not quite the same as an Ability, a skilled observer may detect its use to reveal a faerie's nature.

name: Preternatural Growth and Shrinking
description: A Muto Corpus spell (Level 15) that adds +1 to the target's Size or decreases it by up to 2 points.

name: Prevailing Discipline
description: An optional measure, tracked like Prevailing Loyalty, of how disciplined a covenant's covenfolk are, modifying rolls related to their duties.

name: Priam
description: The elderly faerie lord of Ilium who claims descent from Zeus and granted the town its charter; his son Paris hosts a beauty contest at the mid-summer fair.

name: Priamitus
description: Son of Mercere who sought out hedge wizards of the Cult of Mercury and worked to reconstruct the Roman cult, bringing the Mercurians into House Flambeau.

name: Priceless Ingredients
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab is supplied with copious gold and gems (+2 General Quality, +4 Upkeep, +2 Longevity Rituals).

name: Prime Qualities
description: Properties of a thing derived from its matter and essential form, including the elemental mixture of hot, cold, moisture and dryness, readily discerned with the senses.

name: Primitive Equipment
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character can use only the simplest tools and equipment, suffering penalties when forced to use anything beyond Inexpensive weapons and armor.

name: Primus Johannes
description: A non-magus notary who unexpectedly claimed Criamon Primacy; his ghost is the House expert in Hermetic legal precedent and he secured the Privileges of Criamon.

name: Prince of Gwynedd
description: A Welsh noble who has expressed interest in examining the seemingly immortal Gwrhyr; a court date has been set in the Fate of Cad Gadu story.

name: Principal
description: A character (often a magus) who controls an agency of agents.

name: Principia Magica
description: The authoritative summa on Magic Theory written by Bonisagus; the Great Library holds three copies.

name: Pripet Major
description: A covenant in the Novgorod Tribunal near the terminus of the one-way faerie trod from the Ziegensteine on Rugen.

name: Pripet Marshes
description: A wilderness ancestor site in the Novgorod Tribunal, the supposed origin of all the Slavic people, protected by the covenant Pripet Maior.

name: Prison of Flames
description: A Muto Ignem spell (Level 20) that turns a bonfire into a prison shaped like a miniature castle; a person inside is unburned but takes +15 damage trying to escape.

name: Privileges of Criamon
description: A Grand Tribunal ruling that allows for House Criamon customs such as the ceremonial slaying of a willing Primus.

name: Probe Nature's Hidden Lore
description: An Intellego Herbam spell (Level 4) that tells you what kind of plant you are touching and gives an image of it in its natural habitat.

name: Probe for Pure Silver
description: An Intellego Terram spell that lets the caster smell silver and follow the scent.

name: Production Artist
description: An artist who produces tangible artwork using a Craft Ability, akin to a craftsman, taking the Social Status Virtue Craftsman.

name: Profession: Chamberlain
description: A Profession Ability used (with Presence) to compute the loyalty bonus contributed by a Chamberlain specialist.

name: Profession: Marshal
description: A Profession Ability dealing with understanding, purchasing, and caring for horses, functioning like Medicine for veterinary treatment.

name: Profession: Master of Kennels
description: A Profession Ability governing the care of dogs, treatment of their diseases, and acquisition and breeding of hounds.

name: Profession: Minnesinger
description: A Profession Ability for the German minstrel art; Wolfram von Eschenbach uses it to determine his songs' Aesthetic Quality.

name: Profession: Trouvère
description: A Profession Ability for the northern French minstrel art; Brogo uses it to compose and perform songs with a high Aesthetic Quality.

name: Prognosis Total
description: A medical total (Intelligence + Medicine + modifiers) compared against a disease's severity to determine whether a physician is skilled enough to plan therapy.

name: Prohibition
description: A Minor Supernatural Flaw in which the character has had a Conditional Curse (Geas) cast upon him and must obey its restrictions or suffer the curse in full.

name: Prolific Artist
description: A Minor Supernatural Virtue that reduces the time to create a piece of artwork by one quarter, but prevents the use of assistants.

name: Prone to Chance
description: A Minor Ordeal Flaw making a Verditius magus keen on risk-taking, forcing experimentation on every applicable laboratory activity; incompatible with Averse to Risk.

name: Protagoras
description: A Sophist quoted in the Analects of Tytalus who taught that humans are the yardstick for deciding what is real, and that there is no independent truth.

name: Protected Guest
description: A covenant membership status extended to visitors by a single full member, affording basic rights but no vote or council obligation.

name: Protector
description: An honorary Durenmar title for the magus responsible for the covenant's martial defense, traditionally a Flambeau; currently held by Philippus Niger.

name: Psychodrama
description: An allegorical story taking place in the mind of a meditating Criamon magus, amounting to spiritual combat against the self, used to dramatize introspective avenues.

name: Puissant Artes Liberales
description: A Virtue making a character particularly adept with all seven liberal arts; the Sons of the Peters receive an Infernally tainted version from demonic tempters.

name: Puissant Awareness
description: A species Virtue of the Familiar Cat granting a bonus to the Awareness Ability.

name: Puissant Corpus
description: The Minor Hermetic Virtue of the Damhadh-Duidsan tradition, granting bonus effective Corpus.

name: Puissant Craft or Profession Ability
description: A Minor Virtue a maestro may select at no cost, granting a bonus to a Craft or Profession Ability such as Painting.

name: Puissant Enchanting Music
description: A Virtue adding a bonus to the Enchanting Music Ability; held by the Minstrel template.

name: Puissant Enigmatic Wisdom
description: A Hermetic Virtue gained as the first Fruit of the Path of Warping.

name: Puissant Heartbeast
description: A common Virtue for Bjornaer magi giving a bonus to the Heartbeast Ability.

name: Puissant Imaginem
description: A Minor Hermetic Virtue boosting the Imaginem Art, available to Confraternity of Irene Initiates.

name: Puissant Intellego
description: A Hermetic Virtue granting a bonus to the Intellego Technique; possessed by Tabanus.

name: Puissant Medicine
description: A Virtue that enhances a character's effective Medicine Ability score.

name: Puissant Mentem
description: A Minor Hermetic Virtue boosting the Mentem Art, available to Confraternity of Irene Initiates.

name: Puissant Swordsmith
description: A Virtue providing a bonus to the Swordsmith Craft Ability, held by the example craftsman Klaus.

name: Pulch
description: A magus of House Merinita who haunts the Kammerforst posing as a Waldgeist, chastising those who steal wood, and skirts close to the edge of Hermetic Law.

name: Pull of the Watery Grave
description: A Rego Aquam spell (Level 35) that creates a strong undertow pulling objects smaller than a rowboat 25 fathoms into the depths.

name: Purgatory
description: A realm beyond Mythic Europe; summoning a spirit residing there requires a Ritual spell.

name: Purification of the Festering Wound
description: A Creo Corpus spell that provides a bonus to a wound Recovery roll, adding to any bonus from medical attention.

name: Push of the Gentle Wave
description: A Rego Aquam spell (Level 15) that forms a low wave to propel a small boat slowly through the water.

name: Pyramids
description: Monuments in Egypt near which magi established a covenant and a desert laboratory beside the great Sphinx.

name: Pyrenees
description: The mountain range between France and Spain where Flambeau hid in a cave, founded Val-Negra, and where his lost talisman is thought to lie.

name: Quaertus of Bonisagus
description: A magus of House Bonisagus credited as author of the encyclopedia De Ordinis Hermetici, covering the Code of Hermes and Order of Hermes Lore.

name: Quarter Days
description: The four festival days marking the mid-points of the Hermetic stellar seasons, cited as good days for covenant meetings.

name: Quaternuli
description: David of Dinant's confiscated book of 'little note-books'; a tractatus describing the Infernal Virtue Incantation with a Quality of 13.

name: Quedlinburg
description: A Saxon town that was briefly the German capital under Henry the Fowler, later ruled by abbesses of a collegiate foundation; the lair of the Boglin lies near it.

name: Queen Isabella
description: The king's mother and countess of Angoulême, wife of Hugh de Lusignan, threatening to withdraw her support unless she receives more aid.

name: Queen of Snowflakes
description: A powerful faerie, former lover of the Blackberry God, who controls the land above the tree-line and obstructs the Worshipful covenant's vis collection.

name: Queen of Winter
description: A powerful supernatural being who holds the Baltic Sea in ice each winter; she is propitiated by the ritual spell Appease the Queen of Winter and opposed by the sun-god Svantovit.

name: Quench the Raging Conflagration
description: A PeIg 20 spell that extinguishes any fire up to the size of a house fire, learned by many Flambeau magi to control accidental Creo Ignem fires.

name: Quiet the Cursing Tongue
description: A ReVi spell of the Lineage of Pralix that prevents a target from using lower-level curse magic.

name: Quiet the Raging Winds
description: A Perdo Auram spell (Level 20) that stops all wind from blowing on the caster, leaving only calm air.

name: Quinotaur
description: A creature of Neptune that, in legend, seduced and impregnated Merovech's mother in the sea, giving Merovech two fathers and a magical bloodline.

name: Quinsy
description: A Serious Phlegmatic Disease contracted from swallowing worms that live in and swell the tonsils.

name: Quintus
description: A magus used as an example for writing books, with Ignem 24, Communication -1, and Language 5, who writes an Ignem summa.

name: Rabies
description: A Serious Choleric Disease caused by the bite of a mad dog, inflaming the choler and reducing the sufferer's mind to that of a furious beast.

name: Rain of Oil
description: A Muto Auram ritual (Level 50) that turns rain into droplets of flammable oil, drenching the landscape; can be ignited with Creo Ignem magic.

name: Raised from the Dead
description: A Major Story Supernatural Flaw in which the character died and was brought back through a holy miracle, beginning with at least three Warping points plus more over time.

name: Raised in the Gutter
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character was raised on the margins of society and suffers -3 when using social Abilities among her betters.

name: Ralph de Neville
description: The vice-chancellor of England, a bastard son of a baronial family and royal clerk who does almost all the chancellor's work in the absence of the Great Seal.

name: Ramius
description: A mid-rank House Tremere magus who defected to House Flambeau after the Sundering of Tremere in 848 AD; skilled in mundane arms, he created the School of Ramius and fought Moorish wizards in Iberia.

name: Ranulf de Blundeville
description: Earl of Chester since 1180, an elder statesman of England and head of the palatinate of Cheshire, on Crusade in the Holy Land in 1220.

name: Rarefication
description: The magical process by which pure physical matter takes on pseudo-life and self-organizes into an elemental, catalyzed by spells, botches, or spontaneous Warping in a Magic aura.

name: Rat Up a Drainpipe
description: A Minor General Virtue letting a character run through urban areas unobstructed using acrobatics, climbing, and dodging, aiding opposed Athletics rolls when chased.

name: Realia
description: Collections of mundane or magical objects (preserved animals, minerals, gemstones, bones) that magi study as a tractatus and use as clues for Intellego magic.

name: Realm Interaction Table
description: A rules table modifying how the prevailing Aura affects power recovery; Jumayl recovers Might per hour equal to the prevailing Aura as modified by it.

name: Realms of Power: Faerie
description: An Ars Magica sourcebook whose character creation and advancement rules can handle faerie-realm legendary artists.

name: Realms of Power: The Infernal
description: An Ars Magica sourcebook cited for rules on Infernal Ceremonies and infernalist abilities relevant to the False Power Flaw.

name: Rebellious
description: A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character reacts adversely to any attempt to impose authority and works against those in command.

name: Rector Maris
description: A covenant founded on the Isle of Man in 866 and destroyed within six months.

name: Rector Novus
description: A covenant founded on the Isle of Man in 938 and destroyed within a year.

name: Refinement
description: A laboratory Characteristic representing its sophistication; together with Size it sets the space for Virtues, and is improved through seasons of work requiring Magic Theory.

name: Reforging Enchanted Items
description: A Minor House Mystery of Verditius allowing a magus to repair, smelt, and reforge enchanted items to enhance their magical potential or extract vis.

name: Reforging Items
description: A Minor House Inner Mystery of Verditius for re-forging or repairing items, part of the Confraternity of Roland's mystery path.

name: Regimen
description: A tailor-made recipe of diet, exercise and bloodletting prescribed by a physician to control the non-naturals and ensure eucrasia, providing a Living Conditions bonus.

name: Reginald
description: A wandering minstrel who plays a rebec of exceptional quality inherited from his minstrel father; his playing causes Imaginem vis to accumulate in the instrument's bowstrings.

name: Reginald's Rebec
description: A three-stringed fiddle of exceptional quality played by the minstrel Reginald; it grants a +3 bonus to Music rolls and accumulates Imaginem vis in its horsehair bowstrings when played well.

name: Rego Mentem
description: A Hermetic Technique-and-Form combination (Control Mind) used to make disloyal covenfolk loyal or to compel obedience regardless of emotion.

name: Rego Vim
description: A Hermetic combination governing control of magic; Rego Vim spells and wards can dampen a legendary artist's powers and bar him from areas.

name: Regular
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character lives according to a strict religious rule and must spend one free season on worship; suitable for monks and canons.

name: Reismann Ex Miscellanea
description: The probable founder of the Rusticani tradition, a hedge wizard who swore the Oath at the Rhine Tribunal of 963 and wrote a summa on Craft Masonry.

name: Relics of the Three Magi
aliases: relics of the three wise men
description: A fabulous golden casket in Cologne's cathedral containing the bones of the three wise men who visited the infant Jesus, taken from Milan by Frederick Barbarossa in 1164.

name: Religious
description: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a monk, nun, beguine, anchoress, anchorite, holy hermit, or similar religious figure.

name: Relisius
description: A contemporary House Bonisagus magus well known for his Christian faith and advocacy of harmony between Magic and the Divine.

name: Relocation
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: the lab's physical-world location can be magically adjusted, e.g. via a powerful Rego Terram effect.

name: Remi of Museau
description: A friendly, effusive 48-year-old Master magus of House Jerbiton at Triamore, a veritable polymath accomplished in mundane tasks and magic alike.

name: Remora of Virtue
description: A symbolic fish whose fins provide a Shape and Material bonus of +7 to slowing or halting a moving object.

name: Removal of the Conspicuous Sigil
description: A Perdo Imaginem spell (Level 20) that obscures grooves, runes, and writings so they are not visible while the overall shape of the medium remains, e.g. hiding runes on a sword blade.

name: Reorder the Contents of the Armarius
description: A Rego Animal 10 spell with Intellego requisite that sorts books in a chest or closet into a chosen sequence; an optional Mentem requisite raises it to level 15 for emotional or read-status sorting.

name: Repair Cracks and Tears
description: A Creo Animal 20 ritual that heals cracks and tears in the parchment and leather of a book, used for historically significant works like Bonisagus's diaries.

name: Repellent
description: A Major General Tainted Flaw in which the character has a physical characteristic of his demonic creator, causing -6 to rolls requiring trust but granting a minor advantage.

name: Replenishing the Fount of the Magus
description: A CrCo 30 spell created by Terious of Flambeau allowing a magus on the Path of Energy to restore lost Fatigue levels from the forest; recorded in the Great Library but never successfully cast.

name: Resonance
description: The sympathetic link between a Hermetic book's construction materials and its subject; resonant materials add quality points to a book studied by magi.

name: Restless Dead
description: Corporeal dead rising from graves and ghostly visitations that terrorize Mythic Europe; the Donatores combat or quiet them, distinguishing Infernal from Magic or Faerie origins.

name: Restore the Faded Threads
description: A Creo Vim spell that temporarily restores faded spell traces to a fresh state so they can be examined.

name: Restore the Moved Image
description: A Rego Imaginem (General) spell that cancels a Rego Imaginem spell which moved an image, putting the image back where it belongs if the caster matches the spell's level.

name: Restricted Learning
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character can only apply experience points to five chosen Abilities and cannot learn new Abilities without Teaching or Training; required of all mundane animals.

name: Restriction (True Feeling)
description: A Major Hermetic Flaw of the Cult of Orpheus.

name: Retetarius Bjornaer
description: Deputy chief of Clan Wilkis appointed by the prima, with a salmon heartbeast, dwelling in the River Danube.

name: Reveal the Hidden Words
description: A MuAq 5 charged-item effect that makes any group of words written in the enchanted colorless liquid visible for a Diameter duration.

name: Reveal the Lurking Watchers
