description: An InVi 30 spell that allows the caster to see creatures of the Magic realm within his field of view and identify them as possessing Magic Might.

name: Reveal the Magical Deception
description: A new Intellego Vim spell (InVi 25) invented for Tabanus, designed to overcome spells that hide traces of magic such as Masking the Odor of Magic.

name: Revealed Flaws of Mortal Flesh
description: An Intellego Corpus spell (Level 10) that finds any medical defects in a person or being touched, more specific than Physician's Eye.

name: Revealed Flaws of the Mortal Flesh
description: A spell that instantly diagnoses a disease's cause and effect and adds +3 to the Prognosis total if the character designs the follow-up treatment.

name: Revenge of the Bitten Toad
description: A PeAn 20 Flavor-Target spell inflicting a Heavy Wound on any creature that bites or tastes the caster.

name: Rewriting the Mind
description: A Muto Mentem Ritual that utterly changes the target's cognitive goals, hopes and desires to an agenda dictated by the magus.

name: Rhiannon
description: A timid maga named Prima of House Merinita at the Grand Tribunal of 997, four generations descended from Quendalon; she defended House Diedne during the Schism War and died of old age.

name: Rhine-Main-Danube Canal
description: A proposed canal connecting the Main (a Rhine tributary) and the Danube to create a trade corridor across the continent, around which a saga could be designed.

name: Rhinegold
description: The lost treasure of the Nibelungs, possibly located at the Rhinefalls and jealously guarded by the powerful Rhine elemental in revenge for his entrapment.

name: Rhonabwy
description: A warrior of Powys who, sleeping on an ox-skin in a foul hall, dreamed of being taken by Iddawg to King Arthur's court where ravens battled Arthur's men.

name: Rhone
description: A river that ends at the wild, inhospitable Camargue Delta where a ghostly horse keeps a larder of wicked children.

name: Richard Rufus the Deacon
description: A learned theologian scholar at Schola Pythagoranis who writes tracts justifying the use of magic for virtuous ends, risking trouble with church authorities.

name: Richenda Spinosa
description: An atypical journeyman maga of House Flambeau at Irencillia of secret faerie heritage descended from Kupala; her scarred Gift left her unable to use fire magic, so she turned to Herbam thorn magic and seeks vengeance on her master Indulius.

name: Rings of Verditius
description: Five magic rings, one for each finger and thumb, that Verditius forged from all he had learned, perhaps the most powerful magic rings in Hermetic history.

name: Ripper
description: A Minor Supernatural Virtue with two inflexible powers: destroying cloth or disemboweling an animal at Sight range without words or gestures.

name: Rise of the Feathery Body
description: A Rego Corpus spell (Level 10) that allows the target to float vertically to any height carrying up to 50 pounds, but not move horizontally.

name: Rising Passion
description: A Creo Mentem 15 spell invented by Imanitos Mendax that raises uncontrollable carnal lust in a target.

name: Ritual Power
description: A Major Supernatural Virtue giving an at-will supernatural power equivalent to a Ritual Hermetic spell of level 25 or lower, costing Fatigue and Confidence.

name: Robert Wood
description: An outlaw of Yorkshire in the late 1100s, presumed a rustic-magic hedge wizard and exceptional archer/bowyer/fletcher with magic in his craft, registered as a vis source by Voluntas covenant.

name: Robin Hood
description: Cited as a legendary example of crime income, operating with demonic assistance.

name: Roland
description: A great Frankish knight, one of Charlemagne's 12 peers, slain at the Battle of Roncesvals in 778, who wielded the magic sword Durendal forged by Wayland with Verditius as apprentice.

name: Rolling Stone
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character has moved so often that she finds it hard to form community attachments, giving -1 to social rolls within a community.

name: Rollright Stones
description: A thirty-meter stone circle of twenty-five stones in Oxfordshire, said to be a petrified army and its king; includes the King Stone whose chips ward against demons, watched over by a witch in the form of an elder tree.

name: Roma Nova
description: A covenant of traditionalist Latin magi founded in Kent in 946, unpopular with Bjornaer, Díedne, and Ex Miscellanea; destroyed by the Díedne in 1008.

name: Roman Emperor Trajan
description: A Roman emperor whom God allowed to be saved after death at the request of Pope Gregory the Great.

name: Romer
description: A young giant of Romerstein castle who fell in love with and secretly married Ruma, daughter of the dwarf king.

name: Romowe Oak
description: A surviving magical forest spirit of Pomerania in the Eastern Marches; it is likely to possess seekers who attempt communion with it.

name: Room of Stale Air
description: A Perdo Auram spell (Level 15) that makes the air in a room stuffy and uncomfortable, penalizing physical exertion of breathing creatures.

name: Rope of Bronze
description: A Muto Herbam spell (Level 15) with a Terram requisite that turns a piece of plant-fiber rope into superior bronze that does not break under normal circumstances.

name: Rosalba
description: Covenant founded by Flavia of Jerbiton in 820 in the Yorkshire Dales; destroyed in 899 when all its magi were killed in a Wizards' War with Blackthorn.

name: Roscius
description: Filius of Verditius who stole the sword Durendal and took it to Verdi; by studying it he and his filii became famous makers of magical swords, founding the Confraternity of Roland.

name: Rosmert
description: Handri's faerie caricature, the imperious-looking Queen of Irencillia's fae and monarch of the Faerie Court.

name: Rostock
description: An expanding Baltic trading town and port, chief town of the Mecklenburg dynasty of Sorbian princes, overshadowed by neighboring Lubeck.

name: Rottweil
description: A town of Roman origin (Arae Flaviae) on the eastern edge of the Black Forest, overlooking the upper River Neckar, where butchers trained Rottweilers to pull carts.

name: Roughting Linn
description: A rock face in Northumberland carved with over sixty cup-and-ring markings, thought to be maps or faerie memorials and possibly carved by Gerfallon of Semitae.

name: Round Table
description: The Arthurian Round Table that rises from a bog each midsummer near Tintagel, which a king might seek to seize.

name: Royal Prise
description: A special low price that royalty expects when buying at fairs, effectively a tax on the seller; King Henry III's Westminster fair promised to drop these prises.

name: Roznov Castle
description: The castle housing the Rhine covenant of Roznov on the side of Mount Radhost, with Igor Rastvan's great-hall laboratory at one end.

name: Ruach
description: A minor demon in spiritual form that attends a Demonic Blooded character, using its Misfortune Power to blight her enemies and reporting to her demon parent.

name: Rudolph of Bonisagus
description: A magus of House Bonisagus and the brainchild behind plans to establish a Fengheld chapter at Durenmar.

name: Ruma
description: Daughter of the dwarf king and a mermaid, able to transform into a stream of water; she surfaced to create the Rumaquelle while searching for her husband Romer.

name: Running Water Weakness
description: A demonic weakness preventing the demon from crossing running fresh water deriving directly from the earth.

name: Rus
description: One of the three legendary founding brothers of the Slavic peoples, who settled at the River Dnieper with his tribe, the Russians.

name: Rübezahl
description: A Waldgeist who haunts the forests of the Riesengebirge (Giant Mountains).

name: Sabina of the Seine
description: A relatively young maga who leads the Viticulturalists league and keeps its collection of casting tablets for agricultural rituals.

name: Sachiko of Merinita
description: A probably-female Merinita magus of Burnham whose sigil appears at tribunals but who is otherwise unknown to the tribunal.

name: Sacrifices
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: animal sacrifices are needed for the lab to function (+2 Upkeep, -1 Safety, +1 Warping, -1 Health, -3 Aesthetics).

name: Sagitar of Tremere
description: A Tremere magus who falsely claimed the Criamon Primacy, discovering it was voluntary mystical slavery; his contrite ghost haunts the Cave of Twisting Shadows.

name: Sailor's Foretaste of the Morrow
description: An Intellego Auram spell (Level 15) that tells the caster precisely tomorrow's weather and gives a general impression of the week ahead at the casting location.

name: Saint Andrew
description: A saint whose relics were stolen from Constantinople by the bishop of Amalfi in 1210, prompting Andru's personal grudge.

name: Saint Anthony's Fire
description: A Minor Sanguine Disease from possession by a minor demon in the intestines; cured by exorcism.

name: Saint Barbara
description: A patron saint of French masons, whose feast day is December 4.

name: Saint Bartholomew
description: The patron saint of tanners, whose feast day is August 24.

name: Saint Crispin
description: One of the patron saints of shoemakers, a third-century Roman preacher who made shoes; feast day October 25.

name: Saint Crispinian
description: One of the patron saints of shoemakers, a third-century Roman preacher who made shoes; feast day October 25.

name: Saint Denis's Lendit Fair
description: A fair near Paris founded by King Dagobert in the seventh century for the benefit of the Abbey of St. Denis; once the most important fair in France until the Champagne cycle took over.

name: Saint Dominic
description: Founder of the Order of Preachers (Dominicans), a trained scholastic from the cathedral school of Palencia preaching against heresy in Lombardy; historically dies 6 August 1221.

name: Saint Dunstan
description: The patron saint of blacksmiths, whose feast day is May 19.

name: Saint Eligius
description: The patron saint of armorers, whose feast day is December 1.

name: Saint Elisabeth
description: Daughter of the king of Hungary and wife of the landgrave Louis IV of Thuringia, who devotes her life to the needy; subject of the miracle of roses and later canonized as patron of Marburg's poor.

name: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary
description: A saint to be adopted as patron of bakers, who will die in 1231 and be canonized four years later; feast day November 17.

name: Saint Francis
description: Founder of the Franciscan Order, living near Assisi and growing his newly formed mendicant order.

name: Saint Gertrude of Nivelles
description: The patroness of the recently dead who appeared in visions to many (often unGifted) Donatores, with souls in her care for their first night after death.

name: Saint Godric
description: A historical peddler, merchant, pirate, hermit, and saint of northeastern England who settled at Finchale near Durham; renowned for austerity, hymns, and prophecy, he died in 1170 at age 105.

name: Saint Homobonus
description: The recently canonized patron saint of clothiers, a tailor from Cremona who gave free clothes to the poor; his feast day is November 13.

name: Saint Honoratus of Arles
description: The patron saint of bakers, whose feast day is January 16.

name: Saint Luke
description: One of the patron saints of glassmakers, whose feast day is October 18.

name: Saint Marina the Monk
description: A medieval saint, used as a character-concept example, who lived disguised as a monk, accepted false blame for a pregnancy, and was revealed to be a woman only after death.

name: Saint Mark
description: One of the patron saints of glassmakers, whose feast day is April 25.

name: Saint Nicholas
description: A saint venerated in northwestern Mythic Europe for miraculously resuscitating three children murdered and pickled by an innkeeper; the planned Kolding church is dedicated to him.

name: Saint Odilo
description: The Abbot at Cluny who created the Feast of All Soul's Day and promoted the Truce of God; patron saint of souls in Purgatory who appeared to Donatores in holy orders.

name: Saint Paul
description: An apostle cited regarding slavery, counseling slaves to obey their masters while requiring masters not to abuse them.

name: Saint Stephen
description: The first Christian martyr and patron saint of masons, whose feast day is December 26.

name: Saladin
description: The conqueror to whom Jerusalem fell in 1187, during which Margaret of Beverley helped defend the city.

name: Salamander
description: A fire-dwelling creature whose skin provides a Shape and Material bonus of +8 to extinguishing fire.

name: Salgfräulein
description: A wood-wife who dresses in white and sits under old larch trees, singing.

name: Salmo
description: A descendent of Ilfetu who became primus after the Schism War and refocused House Bjornaer toward a more traditional Hermetic mould.

name: Samuel ibn Tibbon
description: The translator who rendered Maimonides' Guide for the Perplexed from Arabic into Hebrew.

name: Sap the Griffin's Strength
description: A general Perdo Vim spell invented by Philippus Niger, like Demon's Eternal Oblivion but working on creatures with Magic Might.

name: Sardinia
description: The Mediterranean island, dotted with nuraghi and magic auras, where Hephaestus built his famous forge and House Verditius's domus magna Verdi stands.

name: Savantism
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is simpleminded with halved experience but exceptionally gifted in one favored Ability with a +3 specialization bonus.

name: Saxony
description: A large and important duchy of fertile lowlands and cities in the Rhine Tribunal, ancestral home of the Welf family and rival to the Hohenstaufens.

name: Scales of the Magical Weight
description: An Intellego Vim spell used to weigh an unknown amount of vis against a known amount to determine the number of pawns present.

name: Scarf of Healing
description: A wondrous scarf that copies the effects of the spell Bind Wound (Craft Level 14).

name: Scattering Like Light
description: A MuTe(Im) Level 30 spell that changes metal in an object into iconic species carried off by passing light, disintegrating objects; originally created for metal plating.

name: Scent of the Predator
description: A CrMe 20 Scent-Target spell that fills anyone smelling the caster with a sensation of menace, cowing or intimidating targets.

name: Schleswig
description: A Holstein town by the fjord of the River Schlei, grown next to a Benedictine cloister of St. Johannis near the ruins of the old Viking city of Haithabu.

name: Scholastus
description: A magus of House Jerbiton, the sole surviving member of Treverorum, who announced his covenant's abolition in 1172 AD and departed for the Greater Alps, held liable for its unpaid fine.

name: Scholomance
description: A covenant in the Transylvanian Tribunal that is a school for future apprentices, agents, and companions, set in an intermittently accessible regio and reputed to be a school for sorcerers run by the devil.

name: School of Chartres
description: A medieval cathedral school whose writers (Thierry the Breton, William of Conches, Bernard Silvestris) produced foundational works on cosmology and natural philosophy still taught in Mythic Europe's universities.

name: School of Ebroin
description: A minor combat school within the Schools of Sebastian family, based on conjuring animals.

name: School of Marosa
description: A minor combat school within the Schools of Sebastian family, based on Herbam attacks.

name: School of St Geneviève
description: A cathedral school in Paris where the scholastic luminary Peter Abelard taught.

name: Schools of Magical Combat
description: Informal styles of fighting magic recognized within House Flambeau, each named after the pioneering magus who invented it, used to classify combative approaches.

name: Schöne Lau
description: A beautiful reclusive water faerie of Blautopf Pool with webbed feet and powers of divination, banished there by her faerie-king husband because she could not laugh; she foretells visitors' futures.

name: Scilly Isles
description: Islands southwest of Land's End said to be the last sinking remnants of the drowned land of Lyonesse, settled by those who fled to the high ground.

name: Scintilla of Flambeau
description: A Flambeau maga who came to Burnham from eastern Europe, rumored to be a powerful fire maga but has done nothing noteworthy in Stonehenge.

name: Scribes' Guild
description: The guild responsible for producing parchment for books, referenced in the seasonal production chart.

name: Scrofula
description: A Serious Melancholic Disease from cold dry city winds; said to be cured by the touch of the Kings of England or France.

name: Sculpt the Living Water
description: A Muto Aquam spell (MuAq 20) created by Falke that allows the caster to mentally mold water as if it were clay for Sun duration.

name: Searching the Haystack for a Needle
description: A Rego Mentem spell granting +3 to sight-based Perception rolls for a specific object or quality, often used to locate vis.

name: Sebastian
description: An eighth-century hedge wizard who joined the Order as a Flambeau magus despite Deficient Arts, developing a combat method based on his only strength, the Form of Aquam; namesake of the Schools of Sebastian.

name: Secondary Insight
description: A Minor Hermetic Virtue making magical study versatile, granting bonus experience in several Forms when studying a Technique, and in Techniques when studying a Form.

name: Seed of Betrayal
description: A Muto Mentem 15 spell invented by Imanitos Mendax that turns a target's emotions toward his masters into contempt, making him readily betray them.

name: Selene
description: A famous Younger Titan, the Moon, named among the offspring of the Titans.

name: Semitae's horses
description: A breeding line of horses raised by Semitae that are not frightened of magi; traded to other covenants but no one else has managed to breed them true.

name: Sempringham
description: The first and most important house of the Gilbertine order in eastern England.

name: Seneca
description: A crazed Durenmar magus obsessed with building the tallest tower in the world; his magical botch sent him into Final Twilight and collapsed his half-built tower, now Seneca's Folly.

name: Seneca's Folly
description: A jumble of ancient overgrown timber beams at Durenmar, the ruins of a giant tower whose builder Seneca was sent into Final Twilight by a botch.

name: Sense Holiness & Unholiness
description: A Supernatural Power allowing perception of holy and unholy qualities, such as the Manifest Sin Flaw, through one or more senses.

name: Sense of Magical Power
description: An Intellego Vim spell that tells the caster whether he is currently in a Magic aura.

name: Sense the Feet That Thread the Earth
description: An Intellego Terram spell that feels what is moving along the ground within a mile; derived from the Terram tradition from which Guernicus the Founder came.

name: Sense the Lingering Magic
description: The Hermetic effect (Target: Smell) underlying Philippus Niger's Sniff Out the Witch power for detecting magical residue.

name: Sense the Nature of Vis
description: An Intellego Vim spell that reveals which Art a supply of raw vis is connected to, shown by a color-coded aura.

name: Sentences
description: A work by Peter Lombard whose reading might lead to a breakthrough regarding the Divine realm's suppression of magic, per a story seed.

name: Sentient
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: the lab has developed an independent mind, likely from long exposure to a high-level magic or faerie aura.

name: Sept
description: A local grouping within House Bjornaer to which a magus may belong; sept members typically Initiate a magus into cults and provide mentorship.

name: Serica
description: A distant eastern land the Romans called the source of the finest silks and spices, from which Europe imports luxuries by paying tons of silver through Arabic intermediaries.

name: Sericans
description: The people of Serica, whom no European merchant has ever met; some Hermetic scholars believe they are monsters who eat silver, given their insatiable demand for it.

name: Serrifuloria of Merinita
description: A magus of House Merinita believed to have discovered a unique path within the Arcadian forest, stripping herself of emotions as magical jewels to partially overcome the Limit of True Feeling.

name: Servant
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Virtue: a full-time mundane lab servant from the covenfolk performs the most menial tasks (Safety bonus from servant's Intelligence, +1 Aesthetics, +1 Mentem).

name: Servant of the (Land)
description: A Major Story Flaw in which a powerful magical creature has saved the character and set him a difficult task, imposing a Prohibition until the task is complete.

name: Servus Maris
description: An attempt to found a Manx covenant in 1160, destroyed by a dragon within six months; one magus was sent back with the message 'Don't come back.'

name: Sever the Ties That Bind
description: A Major or Minor Ordeal Flaw causing a Verditius magus to lose emotional bonds with family and friends, appropriate for learning Bind Curse.

name: Sever the Unwanted Limb
description: A Rego Corpus 25 spell that cleanly and painlessly amputates one of the target's limbs without bleeding, leaving the Lame or Missing Hand Flaw.

name: Severicus
description: A master of House Tremere at Roznov Fort, a tall, bald, Terram-specialist magus who detests change; one of only two Tremere in the Rhine to hold his own sigil and controls about two-fifths of the Tremere sigils.

name: Severus Maximus
description: A magus of House Flambeau who declared Wizard War against Caithlinn of House Diedne of Oakdell covenant in 1004 AD.

name: Shackles of the Frozen Ice
description: A ReAq 10 spell that freezes a circular portion of water into ice, trapping anyone in it; the ice holds fast regardless of Magic Resistance but only inflicts cold damage if it penetrates.

name: Shadows of the Fires past
description: An Intellego Ignem spell (Level 15) that reveals where fires have been in the past lunar month as a light red flickering haze, with an intuitive sense of when.

name: Shamir
description: A magical stone said to be held within the pillars of Solomon's temple that could cut other stones.

name: Shapechanging
description: A non-Hermetic Major Virtue option for the Damhadh-Duidsan tradition.

name: Shattering the Malicious Rune
description: A general Perdo Vim spell invented by Philippus Niger, like Unraveling the Fabric of (Form) but targeted specifically at rune-magic.

name: Shell of False Determinations
description: A Creo Vim ritual that creates a shell of magic on an item, giving false information to magi who investigate its powers.

name: Shell of Opaque Mysteries
description: A Creo Vim ritual similar to Shell of False Determinations that causes all attempts to investigate a magic item to fail unless the magus's roll exceeds the ritual's level.

name: Sheltered Upbringing
description: A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character grew up isolated from society and cannot understand most human customs, barring several social Abilities at start.

name: Shiver of the Lycanthrope
description: An Intellego Animal spell (Level 10) that makes the caster feel a shiver when touching a person or beast that is a lycanthrope.

name: Shoes of the Zephyr
description: Wondrous horseshoes that allow a horse to fly, running across the sky as if it were land (Craft Level 19).

name: Short of Breath
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character quickly tires during extended physical activity, receiving -3 to Stamina rolls to avoid fatigue.

name: Short-Lived Magic
description: A Minor Hermetic Flaw in which the character's spells do not last as long as they should, with each duration category reduced.

name: Show of the Flames and Smoke
description: A Muto Ignem spell (Level 10) that makes a fire produce colored smoke, streams of flame, and strange noises, entrancing or horrifying onlookers and potentially igniting nearby objects.

name: Shroud Magic
description: A Muto Vim spell that lets a magus suppress or alter the sigil in a spell currently being cast.

name: Shrouded
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: the lab is hidden or protected by a supernatural effect such as The Shrouded Glen (+1 Warping, halve Aesthetics).

name: Side Effect
description: A Minor Hermetic Virtue giving a magus's magic an incidental, generally useful feature whose intensity scales with spell level, such as a temporary Presence bonus after casting.

name: Siena
description: A north Italian city whose goldsmiths are renowned throughout Europe.

name: Siffed of Criamon
description: A young Criamon magus among the members recruited to Nigrasaxa.

name: Sight of the Warm Surface
description: A MuIm 20 synaesthetic spell that transforms the species of warm surfaces, normally sensed by touch, into species the eye can perceive.

name: Sign Language
description: An Ability equivalent to a Living Language, developed by monks to communicate during times of silence, understood only by monks of a particular monastery.

name: Significato
description: Magically occurring phenomena that illuminate truth and let magi generate study totals through mystical experiences instead of studying from vis.

name: Signum Irruptus
description: A master of House Criamon and leader of the covenant Heorot, obsessed with the trolls (whom he believes descended from degenerate gods), having lost his left arm and 14 grogs to his studies.

name: Sikelgaita of Sicily
description: A Lombard princess and wife of the Duke of Apulia and Sicily who fought dressed as a knight, rallying troops at the Battle of Dyrrachium against the Byzantine Empire; an example of conquest-based female power.

name: Silbury Hill
description: An artificial mound 500 feet in diameter and 120 feet high south of Avebury, said to be the cursed burial place of King Sel, entombed on horseback with his treasury.

name: Silent Shout
description: A CrIm 10 miniature spell that creates a burst of species matching the caster's voice striking the target's head, used on battlefields or to instruct apprentices.

name: Silva of Merinita
description: A maga of House Merinita whose spell variants have whimsical qualities, such as comical coloration on created toads or a happy, playful wave.

name: Silvery Scales of the Knight
description: A CrTe(An) 30 spell that conjures a suit of full chain mail armor styled after the caster's Wizard's Sigil; being magical, the wearer cannot grapple a magic-resistant creature while wearing the gauntlets.

name: Similarity
description: A natural principle stating an effect resembles its cause, imbuing objects with Shape and Material bonuses; apothecaries call it the doctrine of signatures.

name: Simile
description: The pattern underlying the natural range of variance in a class of objects, distinct from the Platonic form; familiarity with it adjusts Finesse rolls for crafting.

name: Simple Minded
description: A Flaw possessed by all Rottweiler grogs reflecting limited intellect.

name: Simprim of Guernicus
description: The mid-twelfth-century House Guernicus magus who started the Transitionalist movement seeking greater legal powers for the Quaesitores.

name: Simulacra
description: A common automaton power (base effect 15, Creo Imaginem) making the automaton look, smell, and sound real rather than a facsimile.

name: Sinead Ex Miscellanea
description: An ancient maga of Ungulus, focused on combat against magical beasts, who burns for revenge on the dragon that killed her beloved Parsirus but is magically pushed away from it.

name: Sinead's enchanted iron items
description: A number of iron items worn by Espera of Merinita, all enchanted to defend against faeries, against the faerie lord she offended.

name: Sinews of Knowledge
description: A covenant that has close and friendly relations with Durenmar, lying along a well-traveled Redcap route south toward the Greater Alps Tribunal.

name: Singlemindedness of the Concentrating Wizard
description: A Rego Mentem spell granting +3 to Concentration rolls while automatically failing non-Concentration Intelligence rolls.

name: Sinus Wodinis
description: A second covenant of Bjornaer magi on the southeast coast of Norway, presumed part of the Novgorod Tribunal, whose existence is known only to Crintera.

name: Sir Robert the Dragonslayer
description: An example character cited to illustrate how a high Reputation can make people doubt a character's identity.

name: Siren Song
description: The Major Non-Hermetic Virtue of the Seirenes that empowers a character's music to command those who hear it.

name: Sirens
description: Powerful magical creatures whose magical song lured sailors to drown; they taught Thelxiope their magic and turned to stone after Orpheus defeated them.

name: Sirnas
description: One of Birna's six apprentices, told to 'Protect,' with a stag heartbeast, who originated among the Wends of the Baltic Coast and founded Clan Sirnas.

name: Site of Legend
description: A Free laboratory Supernatural Virtue: stories and legends are associated with the lab, granting appropriate Characteristic and Specialization adjustments.

name: Skilled Smuggler
description: A Minor General Virtue letting a character hide one dagger-sized item, imposing -9 on Awareness rolls to find it.

name: Skinchanger (Dove)
description: A Major Supernatural variant of Skinchanger using prepared feathers or feather-engraved stones to become a dove, associated with the Daughters of Four Fathers tradition.

name: Slave
description: A new Major Status Flaw for a character of likely Slavic origin who has been sold into captivity and is wholly beholden to a master's will.

name: Slave-Owner
description: A new Minor General Virtue making a character the legal owner of one (largely unskilled) slave, lost if the slave is freed or killed.

name: Slavers' Guild
description: A small guild occupying a grey area between craft and service guilds, dealing in the sale of non-Christian slaves; its members are skilled in Sailing and Leadership.

name: Slaves
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: human slaves are employed in the lab as labor or experimental subjects (+1 Upkeep, -1 Safety, -1 Aesthetics).

name: Slay the Innocent
description: A Perdo Corpus (Animal) spell (PeCo[An]30) that Mari Amwithig modified to include an 'enemy' charm in the Charm Magic example.

name: Sleep Disorder
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character cannot sleep soundly and risks nodding off during quiet periods, losing Long Term Fatigue; incompatible with Night Terrors.

name: Slow Power
description: A Minor Supernatural Flaw in which one of the character's supernatural powers requires an additional round of preparation to activate.

name: Slow Reflexes
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character does not react well to surprises, receiving -3 to Initiative in situations warranting a quick response.

name: Smoke Oil
description: A Level 10 Alteration Reagent that evaporates into a thick gray fog filling about a hundred cubic paces when its sealed container is opened.

name: Sniff Out the Witch
description: A 0-point Vim power of Philippus Niger that lets him smell the residue of magic on those with magical powers, with a Penetration of 5.

name: Snow and Wind
description: Spirits of winter that descend each year to frolic in mountain lakes and bring the change of seasons; water collected as their favored lake freezes is a source of Muto vis.

name: Snowdonia
description: The mountainous region of North Wales where Cad Gadu's island lies and where Cad Gadu magi once encountered Gerfallon etching a map into a mountainside.

name: Sol Invicti
description: A holy Hermetic societas connected to the late Roman sun-cult of Sol Invictus, mentioned as related to the Cult of Mercury.

name: Solomon
description: The legendary king whose encoded words of command sahirs chant to summon jinn, and a book in whose hand is a coveted item.

name: Sons of the Peters
description: A small, argumentative group of northern speculative grammarians basing their method on Peter Helias and Peter of Spain; secretly aided in their disputationes by demonic tempters granting an Infernally tainted Puissant Artes Liberales.

name: Soothe Pains of the Beast
description: A Creo Animal Ritual spell (Level 20) that cures one Light Wound suffered by an animal, resembling a ritualistic laying-on of hands.

name: Soothe the Ferocious Bear
description: A Rego Animal spell (Level 10) that calms an animal until it is threatened or aroused again, requiring soothing speech.

name: Soothe the Ferocious Boar
description: A Rego Animal spell (ReAn 10) known by Ioannes Acer with Mastery in Fast Casting.

name: Sophists
description: An antagonistic group of ancient Greek scholars and teachers of rhetoric whose teachings on the rivalry between nature and custom heavily influenced Tytalus's philosophy.

name: Soporific Sponge
description: A Theriac of Level 15, Potency Mighty, a precious secret of the School of Salerno combining opium, mandrake, hemlock and hyoscyamus into a hypnotic aid that induces deep slumber.

name: Sorcerer's Flower
description: A pale violet anemone growing on the slopes of the Brocken, reputed to be a source of vis.

name: Sordello
description: A practicing Italian poet living in Florence who has begun to write poetry in the spreading troubadour style.

name: Sordus
description: A basilisk with Magic Might 30 that serves as Philippus Niger's familiar; a knee-height gray lizard with a Gaze of Death and powers that wither plants and pollute water.

name: Sovereign Ward
description: A powerful taboo: a faerie cannot harm someone carrying its sovereign ward, and direct contact with it destroys the faerie's body.

name: Spacious
description: A Minor laboratory Structure Virtue: the lab has spare room so outfittings can be spread out (+2 Safety, +1 Aesthetics).

name: Speak with the Living Flame
description: A spell whose Bjornaer version is a Range Personal, Target Hearing effect with a free Mentem requisite that interprets the sound of fire into thoughts.

name: Specimens
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab has a large collection of related things stored in visible containers (+1 Upkeep, +1 Aesthetics, 1 Form Specialization point).

name: Speech with the Silent
description: A Major Supernatural Virtue granting the ability to charm elemental objects into assisting, as Path of Strife magi do.

name: Speyer
description: A Rhine city originating as a Roman military camp, favored seat of the Salian dynasty, with a great cathedral whose bells mysteriously toll on imperial deaths.

name: Spirit Form
description: A power (Vim) of the angels Nasir and Seferiel that lets them become a creature of pure spirit, unable to affect or be affected physically.

name: Spirit Votary (Virtue)
description: The Free Mythic Companion Virtue defining a character as a spirit votary.

name: Spirit of a Person's Anger
description: An incorporeal Mentem spirit of Might 20 with the Wrathful Flaw and a Fury power that drives targets into uncontrollable rage; appears to Second Sight as a furious red-faced man.

name: Spirit of the Rhine
description: A powerful water elemental spirit of the Rhine, pinioned at the Rhinefalls by a giant's rock; Schwall has served it through Quests and plots to release it.

name: Sprouting Out of Season
description: A Creo Herbam 20 spell (R: Touch, D: Sun, T: Ind) that causes the seed of any plant to sprout in a single day or night.

name: St Nerius
description: A magus famous for his Christian devotion and sanctity, generally said to have been a member of House Criamon.

name: St Peter
description: One of the twelve Apostles, the first Bishop of Rome and the rock on which the Church was built.

name: St. Adalbert of Prague
description: A saint who defeated the spirit of Romowe, drove it back into the Holm Oak, and lit the fire that keeps it trapped; his relics are housed at the Basilica of St. Vitus in Prague.

name: St. Anthony's Fire Demon
description: A minor disease demon with Might 10 (Corpus) that lodges in a victim's intestines causing escalating wounds, exorcisable by a ritual of the Order of the Hospitalers of St. Anthony.

name: St. Augustine of Canterbury
description: The Benedictine monk who came to convert the Saxons and founded the monastery and abbey at Canterbury that bears his name.

name: St. Benedict
description: The saint under whose monastic rule Bricstan wished to live; he appeared in a blaze of light and broke Bricstan's fetters in prison.

name: St. Boniface
description: An 8th-century missionary saint who miraculously felled the Donar Oak, fragmenting the primeval forest, and raised Mainz to an archbishopric, becoming its first archbishop.

name: St. Collen
description: A hermit living on the side of Glastonbury Tor who confronted Gwynn ab Nudd, banishing the faerie king and his castle with holy water.

name: St. Crispianian
description: Patron saint of leatherworkers and cobblers (with St. Crispin); brother of St. Crispin who preached in Gaul.

name: St. Crispin
description: Patron saint of leatherworkers and cobblers (with St. Crispianian); one of two brothers of a noble Roman family who preached in Gaul in the third century.

name: St. Curig
description: A Welsh saint whose gold-and-silver-encased staff, kept in the church of St. Germanus, miraculously cures tumors in exchange for an offering.

name: St. David
description: A saint who came from Wales to Glastonbury to rededicate the old church but was told in a dream that God had already dedicated it; he was wounded then healed as a sign.

name: St. Davids
description: A Welsh cathedral and see; Gerald of Wales campaigned to make it an archbishopric over the Welsh sees, without success.

name: St. Edmund
description: A king of East Anglia martyred by the Danes and beheaded, his head guarded by a wolf; his shrine is at Bury St. Edmund's and he appeared in armor to condemn Henry of Essex.

name: St. Eloi
description: Patron saint of goldsmiths and jewelers; a preacher who became Bishop of Noyon in seventh-century France.

name: St. Erhard
description: The uncle of St. Odile who baptized her, upon which she miraculously recovered her sight.

name: St. Erkenwald
description: A seventh-century bishop of London and patron saint of the city; the blasphemer Eustace who mocked his shrine was struck down by divine judgment.

name: St. Etheldreda
description: A saint whose tomb at Ely is a major pilgrimage site; she appeared with St. Benedict and St. Sexburga to miraculously free the prisoner Bricstan.

name: St. Georgen
description: A Benedictine monastery founded 1084 as a daughter house of Hirsau, finally destroyed in 1208 by strange dark vines that killed its monks; suspected to be the work of Dankmar or the forest itself.

name: St. Gildas
description: A saint and monk at Glastonbury Abbey who reconciled King Arthur with his brother Hueil, a king in Scotland who fought against Arthur.

name: St. Giles' Fair, Winchester
description: The most important fair in England, the only one where Redcaps are always in attendance, sited around the church of St. Giles outside Winchester's walls; tin from Cornwall and gold from Wales are obtained there.

name: St. Hubert
description: The successor of St. Lambert who raised a grand tomb over the site of Lambert's martyrdom at Liege.

name: St. Joseph
description: Patron saint of woodworkers; the foster father of the Son of God who lived in Judaea and died in the first century.

name: St. Lambert
description: A 7th-century bishop of Tongeren martyred at the site of Liege amid a Merovingian feud; his tomb drew pilgrims and the cathedral of St. Lambert was erected over it.

name: St. Lebuinus
description: A saint who was the first to erect a chapel on the site of Deventer in 768; the present church of Deventer is named after him.

name: St. Liudger
description: A saint who rebuilt the chapel at Deventer in 776 after it was destroyed by Saxon heathens.

name: St. Livier
description: A local lord and saint beheaded by Attila when the Huns sacked Metz, who afterward picked up his head and walked to his burial place on a nearby hilltop.

name: St. Mary's Abbey, York
description: A large Benedictine monastery in York founded in 1080 whose dissatisfied monks went on to found the Cistercian Fountains Abbey; led in 1220 by Abbot Robert of Longchamp.

name: St. Maurice
description: Patron saint of dyers and weavers; an Egyptian soldier and principal officer of the Theban legion in the third-century Roman army.

name: St. Michael's Mount
description: The place where the flood drowning Lyonesse finally stopped and where the first Trevelyan landed on his white horse.

name: St. Nicholas
description: A patron saint of merchants in general; the fourth-century Bishop of Myra in Turkey.

name: St. Odile
description: A 7th-century saint born blind to duke Adalric, who miraculously recovered her sight upon baptism, established a convent at the Hohenburg, and brought forth a curative spring.

name: St. Patrick
description: A holy man who came from Ireland to Glastonbury and was made abbot, bringing the monks under a rule of life just before the time of Arthur.

name: St. Swithin's Soupbowl
description: An ancient stone column topped by a stone bowl, set there by Viking raiders; water left in the bowl by sunrise on St. Swithin's Day becomes Aquam vis by sunset.

name: St. Swithun
description: A saint to whom the cathedral priory (Oldminster) of Winchester and a church over Kingsgate are dedicated.

name: St. Ursula
description: A British princess who undertook a pilgrimage with 11,010 virginal handmaidens and was martyred with them at Cologne by the Huns; a church in Cologne marks their burial.

name: St. Vincent
description: Patron saint of wine; a deacon of Saragossa in northern Iberia who was martyred in 304.

name: St. Wenceslaus
description: Bohemia's patron saint and former duke, murdered by his pagan brother Boleslav; it is foretold he will rise from the dead, take the sword of Bruncvik, and call forth his sleeping army at Mount Blanik.

name: St. Werburg
description: A saint whose Benedictine abbey lies in Chester; in legend she resurrected an eaten goose and forbade geese from entering a particular field forever.

name: St. Wulfstan
description: A bishop of Worcester before and after the Norman Conquest, credited with miraculously saving Bristol merchants at sea and abolishing the Bristol slave trade.

name: Staff of St. Curig
description: A relic staff encased in gold and silver with a cross-shaped top, kept in the church of St. Germanus, that miraculously removes tumors when pressed against them with an offering of a penny.

name: Stag Clan
description: A Crintera clan that oversees the covenant's defense; its members are the most skilled soldiers, fighting with swords, and its leader serves as turb captain.

name: Stance of the Patient Tree
description: A Muto Corpus spell (Level 35) with a Herbam requisite that turns the caster into a tree about 12 feet high; a tree branch lets the caster change back.

name: Station of the Perfect Tool
aliases: The Avenue of Subduing the Meat
description: The first Station of the Criamon Path of the Body, reached via the Avenue of Subduing the Meat, where the magus realizes the body is the perfect tool for Hermetic magic.

name: Stationer
description: A covenant staff member employed in the book trade to coordinate production, purchase scribal supplies, and dispatch books, often dealing with Redcaps.

name: Statutes of Lübeck
description: Special privileges granted to Lübeck by Henry the Lion that let it govern itself independently under a merchant council led by the Älderman.

name: Steadying Hand
description: A power of the angel Nasir (5 points, Animal/Corpus) that, by touching a target, ensures their footing is firm so they will not slip or fall while contact is maintained.

name: Stellapser
description: A ruin in the West Country near which the region is suitable for magical colonization.

name: Stellasper
description: Covenant founded by Criamon magi in 1025 in the Scilly Isles southwest of Cornwall; destroyed in a great storm in 1163.

name: Stephen Eruditus
description: The Jerbiton magus who founded and leads Libellus; trained in the Rhine Tribunal, around seventy but looks mid-thirties, with a reputation for risk-taking.

name: Stephen Langton
description: The Archbishop of Canterbury (born 1165, archbishop since 1207), a noted Paris theologian who helped draft Magna Carta and seeks to establish the archbishop as the highest ecclesiastical authority in England.

name: Stettin
description: A small port city on the River Oder overlooked by an old Wendish fortress, the ancestral home of the Pomeranian rulers, with the church of St. Jakob completed in 1187.

name: Steward of the House
description: The administrator of House Jerbiton between primacies, resident at Valnastium and appointed at the Primus's whim, who organizes elections.

name: Still Casting
description: A Mastered Spell special ability allowing a maga to cast a spell without gestures at no penalty.

name: Still the Raging Waters
description: A Rego Aquam spell (ReAq 15) created by Falke that stills the waves on a small body of water to mirror-smoothness.

name: Stir the Slumbering Tree
description: A Muto Herbam spell (Level 25) with a Mentem requisite that raises a tree to human-like consciousness, able to see, hear, and rearrange its branches.

name: Stockade Parma Magica
description: A Minor Hermetic Flaw in which the character cannot suppress his Parma Magica once erected, so friendly spells must penetrate it as if hostile.

name: Stone of the Black Serpent
aliases: the stone in the serpent's tail
description: A wish-granting stone in the Black Serpent's tail that gives its holder as much gold as desired; Peredur took only this from his victory.

name: Stone to Falling Dust
description: A Perdo Terram spell that turns one solid non-living object of base Individual size or smaller into a pile of dust.

name: Stone-Cutting Knife
description: A Rego Terram 15 enchanted chisel that shapes and forms stone as a stonemason would, usable to carve blocks from a quarry; can boost quarry productivity.

name: Stones
description: A Serious Choleric or Phlegmatic Disease in which coagulated bile or phlegm forms hard stones in the gallbladder, kidney, or bladder.

name: Strassburg
description: A Rhine trade city at the confluence of the Ill and the Rhine, originally the Roman Argentoratum, whose powerful boater's gild controls much of the Upper Rhine trade.

name: Strata Florida
description: A particularly important Cistercian monastery in Powys, Wales, serving as a repository of history and mausoleum of princely dynasties.

name: Strife
description: In Criamon cosmology, the force that divides and promotes separation; one of the two great forces of the universe, reflected by the Art of Perdo and the source of magic's power.

name: Stubnitz Forest
description: The largest forest on Rugen, on the Jasmund peninsula, deep within which the covenant Crintera lies; also containing the mysterious Hertha Lake.

name: Stuck in Your Ways
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character insists on doing things his old covenant's way, using the lower of an Ability and his current Covenant Lore for certain Stress Rolls.

name: Student of Faerie
description: A Virtue representing study of faeries; very common among Faerie Doctors.

name: Student of Magic
description: A Virtue suggested as appropriate for Mercurian characters.

name: Student of Magic Realm
description: A Mystery Virtue the Titanoi cult can Initiate.

name: Studio
description: A Free laboratory Structure Virtue: an ornate room outside the lab displays the owner's prized possessions to guests, commonly built by Verditius magi.

name: Styx
description: The wife of Pallas, representing the underworld river upon which solemn oaths are sworn; her name means "hatred" and she bore the Daimons Zelos, Kratos, Peitho, Nike, and Bia.

name: Subterranean
description: A Free laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab is underground, lacking natural light and requiring more candles (+1 Upkeep, -1 Health, -1 Aesthetics, +1 Terram).

name: Subtle Form
description: A power (Corpus) of the angels Nasir and Seferiel that lets them change their appearance to look like any human being without changing their statistics.

name: Subtle Taste of Poison and Purity
description: An Intellego Aquam spell (Level 5) that lets the caster taste all properties of any liquid or mixture of liquids tasted.

name: Succubus
description: An Infernal entity that sometimes poses as a faerie partner, making intercourse with it worse than the mortal sin of faerie bestiality.

name: Sula
description: The autocrat of Durenmar, a wrinkled and gentle woman over ninety who arranges accommodation for visitors with uncanny ease.

name: Suleiman's Wrath on the Oath-Forsaken Jinni
description: A PeVi spell that weakens and possibly destroys a creature with Magic Might, permanently destroying one reduced to zero Might.

name: Summoning
description: The Major non-Hermetic Virtue of the Witches of Thessaly tradition, described in Realms of Power: The Infernal.

name: Summoning Circle
description: A laboratory Feature: an elaborate pentagram marked on the floor into which things are summoned, providing Experimentation, Spells, Creo, Rego, Animal, and Vim Specializations.

name: Summoning the Creeping Death
description: A Cr(Re)An 25 spell that conjures an obedient asp with deadly venom but no Might; sometimes used by School of Sebastian followers but disdained by other Flambeau magi as ignoble.

name: Summoning the Spirit of Anger
description: A ReMe 40 spell that calls a spirit of wrath to the magus's location via an Arcane Connection or its full name, inflicting a Warping Point on the source of the anger.

name: Sundering of Tremere
description: An event that reduced House Tremere's power, after which Blackthorn's influence in the tribunal was diminished.

name: Superior Construction
description: A Free laboratory Structure Virtue: the lab benefits from distinguished construction techniques or materials (+1 Safety, +1 Aesthetics).

name: Superior Decoration
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab is luxuriantly decorated, e.g. with fine tapestries (+1 Upkeep, +2 Aesthetics, +1 Imaginem).

name: Superior Equipment
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab has higher-quality equipment such as Venetian glassware (+1 General Quality, +2 Upkeep, +1 Safety, +1 Vis Extraction).

name: Superior Heating
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab has superior heating facilities so the occupant is never chilly (+1 Upkeep, +1 Health, +1 Aesthetics, +1 Ignem).

name: Superior Lighting
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab is very well lit so things are easy to find and books easy to read (+1 Upkeep, +1 Aesthetics, +1 Texts, +1 Imaginem).

name: Superior Tools
description: A Free laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab's tools were produced by master craftsmen (+1 Upkeep, +1 Safety, +1 Items).

name: Supernatural Ability
description: A non-Hermetic supernatural skill that an apprentice may possess; whether it is retained, converted into a Hermetic Virtue, or lost depends on the master's Intellego Vim Lab Total.

name: Supple Iron and Rigid Rope
description: A Muto Terram spell that makes a flexible object stiff or a stiff object flexible, with appropriate Form requisites.

name: Suppressed Gift
description: A Major Hermetic Story Flaw in which the character has The Gift but cannot access its power, temporarily unable to perform Hermetic magic, improve Arts, or use Parma Magica.

name: Suppressing the Wizard's Handiwork
description: A Rego Vim spell that cancels one of the caster's own active spells for as long as concentration is maintained, with effects returning when concentration breaks.

name: Susanna
description: The liberal-minded mater of Petrus Virilis, who researched fertility and the Gift and has since entered Final Twilight.

name: Susceptibility to Magic
description: A Minor Curse (Rego Vim effect) that strips a victim's natural resistance to magic, imposing a -3 to resist spells and supernatural effects.

name: Susceptibility to Sunlight
description: A Minor Supernatural Flaw in which direct bright sunlight causes the character pain and exhaustion, giving -2 to sight rolls in bright environments and Fatigue loss outdoors.

name: Susceptibility to Warping
description: A Minor Supernatural Flaw in which the character gains an additional Warping Point from each Realm whenever he gains one in a year, without contributing to Twilight.

name: Suspirium
description: A ninth-century Bjornaer magus, the most recent common ancestor of Stellatus and Lacerta, after whom their sept was renamed.

name: Svantovit
description: A four-faced Slavic sun- and war-god worshipped at Arkona, whose Faerie aura lingers despite the temple's destruction; opposed to the Queen of Winter, granting Falke's ritual a bonus.

name: Swabia
description: The duchy surrounding the Black Forest, extending to Bavaria and the Alps, whose recent history is dominated by the rival Zähringen and Hohenstaufen families.

name: Swan Clan
description: The smallest Crintera clan, comprising crafts-folk and companions with non-shapechanging magical powers; led by Janis, contact with the pagan Forest Brothers of Rügen.

name: Swift Knives, Invisible
description: A Perdo Animal 40 spell with Rego requisite that reduces a dead animal to its components, such as wool, hide, meat, organs, and skeleton.

name: Sword from the Unseen Scabbard
description: A CrTe 15 spell that conjures a steel longsword lasting about two minutes; it must penetrate Magic Resistance to harm magic-resistant opponents.

name: Sword of Bruncvik
description: The legendary sword that St. Wenceslaus is foretold to take up when he rises from the dead to lead his army.

name: Swordsmiths' Guild
description: The craftsmen's guild of swordsmiths; Klaus the example craftsman is a master of it.

name: Sympathy
description: A combined natural principle of affinity and similarity through which objects resonate, e.g. a bloodstone resonating with wounds; basis of many Shape and Material bonuses.

name: Synthemata
description: Signs, symbols, or passwords that link a magician to a supernatural creature, used in theurgic incantations; any being with a Might score has them.

name: Szarlen
description: A demon who operates a lead mine for the Polish town of Beuthen in return for services such as appropriating the Church's tithe or requiring worship.

name: Tablinum
description: A storehouse of information and artefacts in the Transylvanian Tribunal under the control of House Tremere, existing across numerous regiones entered only via spells requiring Arcane Connections held by its curator.

name: Tainted Offspring
description: A Major Story Tainted Flaw in which the character has a child marked for great but unpleasant things by a powerful demon, requiring struggle against the demon's servants.

name: Tainted Virtues and Flaws
description: A category of Virtues and Flaws associated with the Infernal realm, gained through demonic corruption; Supernatural abilities they grant are always Infernal powers.

name: Taklamakan Desert
description: A desert where Infernal storm spirits such as the Buran of Yenghissar are likely to be found.

name: Tales of the Ashes
description: An Intellego Ignem spell (Level 5) that lets the caster see what touched ashes originally were and how and when the object was burned.

name: Talhaearn Tad Awen
description: One of the five great Welsh poets believed by the Order to have left Daimons behind after death.

name: Taliesin
description: One of the five great Welsh poets believed by the Order to have left Daimons behind after death.

name: Talion of Flambeau
description: An ancient Flambeau magus, second oldest in the tribunal, who became praeco after Immanola was disqualified; renowned for mastery of Perdo.

name: Talos
description: A bull-headed bronze statue (automaton) made by Hephaestus that guarded Crete.

name: Taltos
description: Wizards among the Magyar people of Hungary who use herbcraft to boost their physical characteristics and martial skills and to heal; many have Skinchanger; a Pharmocopoeian variant.

name: Tandaline
description: A Follower of Bonisagus of Trianoma's lineage, a master of Muto and Auram, closest confidante of Murion and a Tenens Occultorum who maintains the House's correspondence.

name: Tannhäuser
description: A young 13th-century knight and poet of legend who discovered Venus's subterranean home, the Venusberg, and later sought absolution from the Pope.

name: Tarantism
description: A condition that works wholly differently from a disease, stemming from a faerie curse.

name: Tarnkappe
description: A magical cloak of darkness taken by Siegfried from the dwarf Alberich, used to render him invisible and substitute for Gunther in the contests with Brünhild.

name: Taste of the Dulled Tongue
description: A Perdo Imaginem spell (Level 5) that hides the taste of any substance, liquid or solid.

name: Teeth of the Earth Mother
description: A Muto Terram spell that springs twenty sharp white marble pillars from the ground in a circle, able to cage, wall, or skewer enemies for +25 damage.

name: Tello
description: The Bishop of Palencia who works with the king to stabilize the university, allowing the masters an advisory council under the chancellor.

name: Telramund
description: A rebellious vassal of the late duke of Brabant who sought the dukedom and Elsa's hand and was defeated by Lohengrin in single combat.

name: Templar Administrator
description: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a brother of the Poor Knights of the Temple of Solomon who administers the order's holdings rather than fighting; available only to male characters.

name: Templar Confrere or Consoeur
description: A Free Social Status Virtue for an associate member of the Poor Knights of the Temple of Solomon who has taken one or two Templar vows.

name: Templar Office Holder
description: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a character holding a position in the local hierarchy of the Poor Knights of the Temple of Solomon, such as deputy commander or marshal.

name: Templar Prestige
description: A Minor General Virtue: a member of the Poor Knights of the Temple of Solomon who enjoys great respect among fellow brothers, starting with a Reputation of level 4 within the Templars.

name: Templar Servant
description: A Free Social Status Virtue for a servant working at a Templar commandery, supported and protected by the order's papal bull.

name: Templar Specialist
description: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a skilled employee of the Poor Knights of the Temple of Solomon filling a crucial role such as craftsman or translator.

name: Temple of Isis
description: An abandoned but well-repaired Roman temple within a magical regio in Florence's Piazza San Firenze, a potential covenant site holding relics of the Cults of Isis and Mercury.

name: Tenens Occultorum
description: A House Bonisagus office held by Tandaline, appointed by Murion, involving keeping written contact across the House.

name: Terious of Flambeau
description: A magus of House Flambeau who walked the Path of Energy, became a living embodiment of the genius locus, and contributed the spell Replenishing the Fount of the Magus to the Great Library.

name: Terschelling (island)
description: A Friesian island on a deserted coastline that is home to the Waddenzee covenant and thousands of seabirds.

name: Test of Fastness and Fading
description: An Intellego Aquam 5 spell that confirms the quality of a container of ink, dye, or paint, verifying it will not fade, flake, or eat through parchment.

name: Test of the Flames
description: A CrIg 15 spell filling a circle with waist-high flames doing +5 damage per round; of ancient Cult of Mithras origin, once used by Flambeau magi as an endurance test alternative to certamen.

name: Tethered Magic
description: A Minor Hermetic Virtue letting a magus pass control of non-Ritual spells to others or tether them to objects, at the cost that all his spells become Arcane Connections to him.

name: Thamik of Verditius
description: A young Verditius magus among the members recruited to Nigrasaxa.

name: Thann Chapel
description: A chapel west of Mulhouse in the southern Vosges, built over a miraculous holy staff containing the ring and thumb of Theobald of Gubbio; has a Divine aura of 3 and is a place of pilgrimage.

name: Thaumaturgical Transformation of Plants to Iron
description: A Muto Herbam spell (Level 20) with a Terram requisite that makes any plant as hard as iron, up to the size of a small tree.

name: The (Over) Familiar Cat
description: A magical familiar cat with Magic Might 10 (Imaginem) bonded to a magus, with powers of night-vision and invisible movement and shared-senses bond effects.

name: The Ague
description: A Major Phlegmatic Disease (Severity 14) caused by bad air around sewage and tanneries, marked by continuous fever with chills.

name: The Alder Prince
description: The compassionate, secretive faerie ruler of the western Alder Forest among the Courts of the Seasons, strongest in spring, who woos and is repeatedly entrapped by the Willow Maiden.

name: The Ambulatory Laboratory
description: A Rego Terram 30 spell that transports a chamber's movable contents to another room via Arcane Connection, used by magi to move their labs without mundane effort.

name: The Animal Powers
description: Ancient mysterious entities that ruled the Stubnitz region before the Bjornaer; revered at Crintera as animal-shaped fetishes said to house primordial spirits of nature.

name: The Antigones
description: A new generation of interventionist Jerbiton magi ('those like their ancestors'), trained after the fall of Constantinople, who favor political engagement, aggression, and large House covenants.

name: The Apple That Etches
description: A Creo Herbam 20 ritual that creates 100,000 oak galls used for ink, useful to covenants closed off from the mortal world with abundant Herbam vis.

name: The Apple of the Kyffhauser
description: A magic spirit (Magic Might 70) manifesting as a withered apple tree at the base of the Kyffhauser, guarded by men-at-arms, that grants victory and lordship to whoever hangs their shield on it.

name: The Archpoet
description: An anonymous bawdy twelfth-century Latin poet and famed leader of the Goliardic tradition, rumored to have been a magus, whose poems a Bonisagus magus claims encode Mentem lore.

name: The Art of Magic
description: Bonisagus's epitome concerning Magic Theory, etched by later magi into 36 six-foot clear crystals at the Forest of Shining Stone, Durenmar.

name: The Auberge
description: A long-forgotten Mercere way station on a river island, accessible only through a Roman ruin's doorway into a Magical regio; its three spirit guardians give departing magi food containing Vim vis.

name: The Avariciousness of the Ptolemies
description: A Rego Animal 4 ward that prevents those lacking Magic Resistance from removing a book across an inscribed circle or doorway.

name: The Baltic Sea
description: The sea across which Baltic trade ceases each winter when the Queen of Winter freezes it; a ritual at Arkona must be performed to thaw the ice.

name: The Bears' Cave
description: A hidden primeval cave in the northern Harz (Magic aura 3) strewn with ancient bear bones that may be harvested for Animal vis; secret vis source of a Bjornaer bear lineage.

name: The Beast Remade
description: A Muto Animal spell (Level 25) with a Corpus requisite that gives a land beast a human form while retaining its intellect and some animal feature.

name: The Betrayal
description: The event in 961 AD when Kalliste exposed Tasgillia's diabolism publicly, shaming House Tytalus; Tytali view it as Kalliste betraying the Founder's principle of putting nature before custom.

name: The Black Fir
description: A sinister magical fir tree near Durenmar's Great Library, key to a faerie revenge plot; it slowly inches toward the Tower of Bonisagus as part of the King of the Black Mountain's scheme.

name: The Black Horse of Busha
description: A proud black stallion seen as a figure in black shale in the Howgill Fells, said to travel the mundane world under cover of storms with purposes that bode no good.

name: The Blinded Sentry
description: A Perdo Mentem 5 spell invented by Imanitos Mendax that renders a target insensate for a moment, registering only the initial touch.

name: The Bohemian Forest
description: A massive forest, safe from man due to harsh climate and peat bogs, haunt of lynx, wolves, deer, and giants; home to Irencillia and (in its south) Fenistal.

name: The Book of Mundane Beasts
description: A free Atlas Games supplement describing beasts of Mythic Europe, on which the Virtuous Hound, Familiar Cat, and skinchanger's raven form are based.

name: The Book of One Thousand and One Nights
description: A collection of stories begun in the ninth century around which the Keepers of the Thousand Tales formed; they believe several of its characters are magi who have passed into Arcadia.

name: The Book of Poisons
description: A book by Ibn Wahshiya, quoted for a recipe to make a poison from a scorpion-stung mouse, hellebore, and other ingredients.

name: The Bookstand of Hespera
description: A wooden lectern enchanted (ReHe 15) to follow the magus around the lab, holding a Lab Text and adding two points to a Texts Specialization.

name: The Box of Unguarded Thoughts
description: A small silver coffer inlaid with mother-of-pearl that collects nearby stray thoughts and distills them into silver coins containing Mentem vis, potentially serving as Arcane Connections.

name: The Brushstrokes Revealed
description: An InIm 10 spell that makes species cast by an object within a circle more vivid, revealing tiny details otherwise invisible, used to investigate artworks and creation.

name: The Buskam
description: The largest of Rugen's mysterious findlinge boulders, partially submerged off the Monchgut peninsula and a site of Slavic worship; said to be left by giants from an epic battle.

name: The Cabal of Erigone
description: A House Tytalus cabal, symbolized by a triangular clavicula, determined to prevent Caecilius of Durenmar from becoming praeco of the Rhine Tribunal.

name: The Cabal of the Broken Ocean
description: A House Tytalus cabal, symbolized by a clockwise turbo of four lines, that provides covert support to the pagans of Lithuania against the Teutonic Knights.

name: The Cabal of the Lance
description: A House Tytalus cabal, symbolized by a helix made from chain, covertly shielding a newly formed covenant from the intrigue of its Tribunal for an unclear purpose.

name: The Cabal of the Shining Eye
description: A House Tytalus cabal, symbolized by a concha with an eagle at the center, dedicated to maneuvering the Roman Tribunal into colonization of North Africa.

name: The Carnal Wolf
description: An adulteration caged within the Cave of Twisting Shadows, a great wolf with jaws too large to close, embodying the carnal urges of Demetrius; used to teach apprentices about spiritual impurity.

name: The Carpenter's Keen Eye
description: An InHe 15 spell (Voice, Momentary, Group) by which a magus learns whether wood is suitable for carpentry and what treatment it needs.

name: The Cerne Giant
description: A blatantly phallic figure carved on a Dorset hillside, said to be the lingering presence of a giant who terrorized the area before being slain; barren women who sleep on the phallus may conceive.

name: The Clandestine Mask
description: A MuIm 4 spell that blurs the caster's face and distorts her voice so she cannot be recognized; the disguise's form is determined by the caster's sigil.

name: The Clean Slate
description: A Perdo Mentem spell that wipes the target's memory clean, removing identity, Academic/Arcane/Martial/Supernatural Abilities, and all Arts.

name: The Cloudless Sky Returned
description: A Perdo Auram spell (Level 45) that clears the sky within the caster's vision of clouds and meteorological activity short of a hurricane or tornado.

name: The Constant Expression
description: A Major Hermetic Flaw: the maga perpetually casts non-fatiguing Spontaneous magic effects, losing a permanent long-term Fatigue level and making laboratory work risky.

name: The Courts of the Seasons
description: Four intrinsically linked faerie woodland courts (Holly, Alder, Oak, Willow) tied to the passage of the seasons, formed when one forest spirit splintered into four and each allied with a faerie lord.

name: The Crintera Schism
description: A saga concept revolving around the troubles within Crintera: the shapeshifter feud, the Harmonist-Wilderist split, and the Rügen crisis, culminating in the covenant being sundered and warring domus magnae.

name: The Crone
description: An aged, respected village woman with the Unaging Virtue whose menstrual blood contains Creo vis; though not Gifted, she knows something of magic and serves as a vis source near a covenant.

name: The Crown of Hermes
description: An elaborate jewel-encrusted golden crown (Cr(In,Mu,Re)Me 50) whose creator is lost to memory; it lets its wearer enter a trance to create and work in an imaginary laboratory, inflicting Warping points.

name: The Cult of Vesta
description: A Merinita cult founded by magae of Brittany who venerate faeries as household gods (lares), adopt Vesta as patron, and take vows of chastity in exchange for faerie powers.

name: The Daughters of Echo
description: A Jerbiton league interested in magical methods of recording and reproducing events, led by a Merinita maga near Burnfoot in Hibernia.

name: The Dead of Ascalon
description: The cursed corpses of a Muslim fleet defeated off Ascalon in 1123; their skulls, smuggled aboard rival ships by a merchant house, cause every cursed voyage to end tragically.

name: The Death of Vermin
description: A Rego Animal 20 enchanted box that fills specific vermin with a desire to enter it, gathering them to be destroyed.

name: The Demand of the Frustrated Scholar Soothed
description: A Rego Animal 40 spell that teleports a book within 500 paces to the caster's hand via an arcane connection; higher-level versions reach up to seven leagues.

name: The Dragon of Brünn
description: A dragon that lived in a cave by the River Svratka near Brünn and devoured townsfolk, until a travelling butcher killed it with a lime-stuffed ox pelt; its stuffed carcass hangs in Brünn's town hall.

name: The Dumb Waiter
description: A Rego Terram level 35 enchanted device that instantly transports food and dishes from the kitchen to specified places in the covenant within 50 paces.

name: The Ear for Distant Voices
description: An Intellego Imaginem spell (Level 20) that lets the caster hear what is happening in a designated place to which they have an Arcane Connection.

name: The Eastern Marches
description: The wild northeastern reaches of Germany between the Elbe and Oder, roamed by werewolves, witches, and giants, where pagan Slavic beliefs linger; claimed by the Rhine Tribunal.

name: The Edges of the World
description: Four regiones corresponding to the four elements and humors to which a spirit-traveling Criamon magus is sequentially drawn, and from which he must escape back to his body.

name: The Enchanted Chef
description: A Rego Herbam (Animal, Aquam, Ignem) 45 enchanted pot that processes and transforms food into a described dish as if cooked, substituting Communication + Finesse for Craft: Cook.

name: The Enchanted Porter
description: A Rego Terram 15 enchanted glove that lifts and pushes an inanimate object while the user holds and moves it; based on The Unseen Porter.

name: The End of Hatred
description: A PeCo 50 Orphic spell that instantly slays a target against whom the caster has the Enemies Flaw; used only once in the Cult's history.

name: The Ever-Watchful Turb
description: A Perdo Mentem spell that prevents a target group from falling asleep by quelling the inclination to rest.

name: The Exsules
description: A small band of fewer than a dozen renegade House Merinita wizards based at Fenistal who rejected the Order; they know imperfect Hermetic magic and Parma Magica and prefer to turn nature against their enemies.

name: The Externsteine
description: An array of thirteen tall sandstone rocks on the southeastern edge of the Teutoburger Forest, a former pagan site now bearing a consecrated chapel with a Divine aura of 4.

name: The Eye of the Sage
description: An Intellego Corpus spell (Level 30) with an Imaginem requisite that lets you see a specific person and what is within one pace of them, clearly enough to read.

name: The Faithful Made Whole
description: A sample relic power (4 points, Init +15, Corpus) that cures the recipient of all disease and heals all physical wounds.

name: The Falcon's Hood
description: A Perdo Animal spell that destroys an animal's vision, with the blindness healing as a Medium Wound; also referenced earlier as PeAn 20.

name: The Fallen Temple of Mercury
description: A fallen temple of Mercury still containing details of some of the powerful rituals of the Cult of Mercury, referenced as a place/treasure (via the supplement Mythic Locations).

name: The Far-Speaking Voice
description: A CrMe 20 spell that delivers two minutes of one-way conversation into the mind of a target to whom the caster holds an Arcane Connection.

name: The Feengrotten
description: Hidden crystal caves (Magic aura 1) on the eastern edge of the Thuringian Forest whose shifting passages cover explorers in glittering dust that is Imaginem vis for those genuinely lost.

name: The First Furrow Guides the Second
aliases: The Principal Aide to the Forger's Art
description: A Creo Imaginem 25 spell with Intellego requisite that lays a book page's image over a blank sheet so a scribe can trace it, creating identical copies and avoiding the scribing penalty.

name: The Flying Castle of Thomae
description: A flying castle crafted by a follower of Tytalus decades ago that simply vanished from Hermetic knowledge, referenced as a treasure to hunt (via the supplement Legends of Hermes).

name: The Genethlialogical Investigation
description: An Intellego Corpus 15 spell by which the caster learns a target's place and time of birth; casting it on a magus is tantamount to declaring Wizard's War.

name: The Gentle Beast
description: A Rego Animal spell (Level 25) that calms an animal, making it nearly fearless and tolerant of being ridden or handled.

name: The Gentle Herd
description: A ReAn 20 spell (Touch, Concentration, Group) that renders a group of animals calm and placid even while unusual events occur, ideal for soothing cattle being magically milked.

name: The Geographica
description: A lost work by Ptolemy giving exact longitude and latitude for hundreds of legendary sites, many containing vis; House Mercere offers great quantities of vis for a complete copy.

name: The Giant's Grave
description: A rectangular bed of large stones in the Everstorf Forest north of Schwerin, said to be the grave of a giant trapped and buried by villagers of Naschendorf.

name: The Giant's Ring
description: The ring of great healing stones standing on a hilltop in Ireland that Merlin transported by his art to become Stonehenge in England.

name: The Giants' Castle
description: The remains of a primeval Celtic fortress on the edge of the Bohemian Forest, with a Magic aura of 3, where large fractured rocks were originally gathered by giants who may still visit.

name: The Gift (child story seed)
description: Not an entity; placeholder removed.

name: The God of Law
description: In the new dualist faith near the Bohemian Forest, the stern god who created and rules the material world but cares not for its inhabitants, falsely worshipped (the faith claims) by the Church.

name: The God of Truth
description: The creator deity of a new dualist faith in the villages near the Bohemian Forest, said to be immaterial and found only in wild places, opposed to the God of Law; his angels are said to be faeries, and his prophet is Iacob.

name: The Great Play
description: A tournament hosted every few years by the Shadow-Masters in which a built labyrinth or setting filled with illusions challenges participants; succeeding wins the responsibility to host the next event.

name: The Guide for the Perplexed
description: A great summa on Jewish philosophy and theology written by Maimonides in 1190, infused with Aristotelian ideas, that sparked controversy among Jewish scholars.

name: The Half Shell
aliases: The Large Ship The Half Shell
description: A large ship serving as the mobile site (an Edifice Boon) of the Swashbuckling covenant.

name: The Herbal of Crateuas
description: Crateuas's catalog of herbs and their powers, written in ancient Greek; a summa for several Abilities and rumored source of Insight into the Root-Cutter Virtue.

name: The Horsemen
description: Ghostly faerie riders of the Wild Hunt (Faerie Might 20) embodying icy winter storms, who can spread fear, control winds, and inflict cold; they can produce spells like Broom of the Winds.

name: The Hounds
description: Immense insubstantial grey dogs of the Wild Hunt (Faerie Might 10) whose howls are arctic winds and whose bites inflict an effect similar to Talons of the Winds.

name: The Incoherence of the Incoherence
description: A book by Averroes refuting al-Ghazali's The Incoherence of the Philosophers.

name: The Incoherence of the Philosophers
description: A book by al-Ghazali rejecting the ideas of Aristotle, Plato, and Socrates as harmful to the faithful.

name: The Incubus's Trick
description: A spell that turns a male caster into a woman, the counterpart of The Succubus's Trick.

name: The Inexorable Hunter
description: A magical power of the Virtuous Hound (Animal, 2 points) allowing it to flawlessly follow a creature's scent until it is located, despite the prey's ruses.

name: The Invisible Glass-worker
description: A ReTe 4 spell (Touch, Momentary, Individual) that transforms a piece of glass into a finished form as if shaped by a glassworker.

name: The Keepers of the Pearl of Great Price
description: A Jerbiton league whose members surreptitiously stave off poverty in large cities; leaderless since crusaders sacked their Constantinople headquarters.

name: The Keepers of the Thousand Tales
description: A group of Merinita magi and companions formed in the Holy Land to collect, catalog, and spread the greatest stories, believing faerie immortality is ensured through legend; they have covenants in the Levant and Iberian Tribunals.

name: The Key of Theodorus
description: A ReTe 5 Hermetic spell (R: Touch, D: Mom, T: Part) that magically opens any single lock regardless of complexity, named for Theodorus of Samos.

name: The King's Goblet
description: A wondrous gold cup that trembles in the holder's hand if a poisoned beverage is poured into it (Craft Level 13).

name: The Kiss of Death
