description: A Perdo Corpus spell (Level 45) by which the person kissed dies suddenly, leaving only the black imprint of the caster's lips; requires no spoken words.

name: The Konigstuhl
description: A 380-foot chalk cliff on Rugen; legend says whoever climbs it from the sea becomes king of Rugen, as Valdemar I did, and cheaters fail.

name: The Laboratory of Bonisagus
description: A Creo Terram 45 ritual that furnishes an empty chamber with a fully equipped standard Hermetic laboratory better than normal, granting Flawless Equipment, Flawless Tools, and Spotless.

name: The Lens of Wisdom
description: A crystal lens bound in brass that, focusing the summer-solstice noon sun on a blank parchment, burns indecipherable glyphs into the page, each page containing Intellego vis.

name: The Lightning-Bringer
description: A highly magical device of copper spheres, gold rods, and enchanted glass vessels invented by a Tremere Archimagus; on each new moon it summons a thunderstorm and accumulates its lightning as Auram vis.

name: The Limit of Aging
description: A lesser limit of Hermetic magic: it cannot halt or reverse natural aging or remove Decrepitude, only slow it.

name: The Limit of Creation
description: A lesser limit of Hermetic magic: it cannot create anything permanently without raw vis.

name: The Limit of Energy
description: A lesser limit of Hermetic magic: it cannot restore physical energy (Fatigue levels) or Confidence.

name: The Limit of Experience
description: A lesser limit of Hermetic magic: it cannot create or transfer skills, knowledge, or Abilities in a person.

name: The Limit of Magic Resistance
description: A limit noting that non-Hermetic magic (and Faerie powers) cannot grant general Magic Resistance, though Hermetic magic can.

name: The Limit of Time
description: A lesser limit of Hermetic magic: it cannot alter the passage of time, affect the past, or scry on past or future.

name: The Limit of Vis
description: A lesser limit of Hermetic magic: it cannot change the Art to which raw vis is attuned.

name: The Limit of Warping
description: A lesser limit of Hermetic magic: it cannot affect warping changes once they have happened; Wizard's Twilight is one manifestation.

name: The Limit of the Infernal
description: A lesser limit of Hermetic magic: Intellego magic is almost useless against the Infernal, revealing only what demons want believed.

name: The Limit of the Soul
description: A lesser limit of Hermetic magic: it cannot create an immortal soul, true human life, or restore the dead to life.

name: The Linden of Neustadt
description: A protective Forest spirit (Magic Might 30) manifesting as a great lime tree that has adopted the town of Neustadt as its realm and grants victory and virtues to the town's defenders.

name: The Line of Quendalon
description: The lineage of magi descended from Quendalon who Initiate the three Arcadian Mysteries; many are Seekers devoted to experimental research, sometimes called 'The Last Commission' for Bonisagus's reputed charge.

name: The Long Man of Wilmington
description: A figure about 240 feet tall picked out by trenches on a Sussex hillside, grasping two staves; said variously to represent St. Paul or the keeper of the gates of dawn who may open them for travelers.

name: The Luneburg Heath
description: A wild heathland south of Luneburg where shepherds tend flocks of Heidschnucken, goat-sheep crossbreeds descended from Corsican mouflon.

name: The Magestones of Verditius
description: Onyx-pebble enchanted devices crafted by Verditius, each bearing a powerful Creo Vim effect that manifests a Magic aura of 3; three were secretly gifted to Oculus Septentrionalis, the rest guarded by Durenmar, and their technique was never replicated.

name: The Magic Fountain
description: A spring near the Brocken that grants visions to those who drink from it.

name: The Many-hued Conflagration
description: A Muto Ignem spell (Level 5) that makes a fire burn brightly in shifting colors, potentially blinding onlookers for a round if they fail a Stamina roll.

name: The Margravate of Lusatia
description: A mainly forest-wilderness margravate east of the Elbe bordering Silesia, populated by Sorbs and ruled by the margraves of Meissen.

name: The Marvelous Hound
description: A Muto Animal (Corpus, Mentem) 34 enchanted collar that transforms a normal hound into an erect, handed servant with a grog's intellect while retaining hound loyalty.

name: The Master of Naumburg
description: A young, enigmatic architect and sculptor of German origin who travels Germany working on great churches; some claim his unmatched work is aided by sorcery.

name: The Maze of Singing Mirrors
description: A repository where copies of all recordings made by the Daughters of Echo are kept and sold to Jerbiton magi unable to attend performances.

name: The Miniature of Immortality
description: A ritual Creo Herbam spell (Level 20) that creates a painted miniature of a person or scene on a wooden panel within voice range.

name: The Motivated Plow
description: A Rego Terram 15 enchanted plow-shaped device that transforms hard-packed earth into well-plowed soil in a circle; based on The Forgiving Earth and doing the work of about three laborers.

name: The Mundane
description: That which is not supernatural; areas not occupied by another realm, having no aura rating, consisting of ordinary people and places.

name: The Mystical Carpenter
description: A ReHe 25 spell (Touch, Momentary, Group) that cuts, splits, carves, and joins a pile of wood into a desired form, substituting Perception + Finesse for Craft: Carpenter.

name: The New Iconophiles
description: A Jerbiton league, led ideologically by the Primus, attempting to recover the artistic treasures of Constantinople; based in Valnastium.

name: The Obedient Fire
description: A ReIg 20 spell that controls the rate and direction a fire spreads, able to make it move as fast as a man walks; the fire's heat is non-magical and bypasses Magic Resistance.

name: The Odenwald
description: A German forest that comes into bloom earliest and most spectacularly, an ideal site for the Court of the Alder Prince, with bandits lurking on its western edge.

name: The Old Ones
description: Powerful magical creatures who died or fell asleep millennia ago; finding the resting place of one of them is listed as a possible object of a quest.

name: The Ore Mountains
description: A bleak, unsettled range covered with evergreen forest adjoining the Spruce Mountains in Franconia, where silver and tin have recently been discovered, giving rise to mining towns like Freiberg.

name: The Path of Beacons
description: A Criamon path lacking a clutch that teaches Mysteries allowing each magus to create a sanctuary from the strife of the world; its eldest magus lives in a regio on the Isle of Arran.

name: The Path of Orpheus
description: A rumored great ritual following Orpheus's trek into the Underworld to restore a beloved to the living world, requiring vast vis and Wizard's Communion.

name: The Path of Strife
description: The Criamon path of worldly magic that transgresses House morality; its servants kill, lie, and destroy demons to prolong the universe, and they cannot enter Final Twilight.

name: The Path of Walking Backwards
description: A newer Criamon path brought by Abdkypris from the Sufi, involving complete surrender to the harmonic force to flee back to the Spharios; uses dancing/spinning meditation.

name: The Path of the Mirror
description: The Criamon path followed only by living Primi under instruction of their predecessors, a series of Initiations for those who choose to serve the worldly House.

name: The Phantom Blacksmith
description: A ReTe 20 spell (Touch, Momentary, Group) that transforms ready iron into a crafted result as if worked by a blacksmith to the magus's instructions.

name: The Phantom Gift
description: A Creo Vim spell that makes the target appear tainted with magic as most magi are, causing beasts and people to react to him as a magus.

name: The Pipers
description: Two immense standing stones near the Merry Maidens, said to be demons sent to tempt the dancing girls who were unable to flee divine justice and turned to stone.

name: The Pirates' Graveyards
description: A haunted region in Drenthe near the River Ems where pirates of Friesia bury their dead under standing stones; Lucas von Beck harvests vis and bodies there for necromancy, though its power may not be magical.

name: The Places I've Been - You Wouldn't Believe Me
description: A book describing a Greek Isles covenant whose soldiers ride gigantic terrapins into naval battle.

name: The Plunder of Twenty Geese
description: A Muto Animal 15 spell that transforms up to 100 feathers into goose wing feathers preferred for pens; a Rego variant at level 20 strips and tempers the pens.

name: The Poet's Bust
description: A Rego Terram spell (Level 5) that changes a block of stone into a carved bust of a person the caster touches.

name: The Ponderers of Weight and Distance
description: A Jerbiton league of merchant magi interested in gaining money through mundane trade and manipulating economies, seemingly based in the Rhineland.

name: The Private Speech of Eros and Psyche
description: An In(Cr)Me 60 ritual Orphic spell allowing the magos and a target to speak mentally at will, regardless of distance, for one year.

name: The Prodigious Plant Pot
description: A large clay pot enchanted (CrHe 30) that grows a seed into a mature plant in a day, adding to a lab's Experimentation and Herbam Specializations; made by Ricardus Caespuus.

name: The Remote Entrance Portal
description: A Rego Corpus 50 enchanted device acting as a magical transporter activated only from within a covenant, moving seen targets up to 500 paces inside without arcane connections.

name: The Resolute Mind of the Tireless Researcher
description: A Rego Mentem Level 20 spell devised by Andreas of House Bonisagus that fixes a magus's mind on lab work for a day; daily use warps the mind and requires the Addled lab routine.

name: The Rhinefalls
description: The greatest waterfalls in Europe near the southeastern edge of the Black Forest, with a central rocky island holding a Magic aura and a regio leading to the Rhine spirit's realm.

name: The Riches That are Rightfully Mine(d)
description: A CrTe 35 ritual spell (Touch, Momentary, Individual) that fills a chest with up to ten cubic feet of silver pennies, worth about 2000 Mythic Pounds; a copy resides in the Great Library of Durenmar.

name: The Riesenstein
description: A great stone near Zuschen hurled by the Devil at the village of Neueburg; it bears three red stains that weep bloody tears worth Ignem vis every All Hallow's Eve.

name: The Rooster's Crow
description: A PeVi Sound-Target spell that strips Might from demons who hear the caster's shout if it penetrates their Magic Resistance.

name: The Rosstrappe
description: A rock across a ravine from the Hexentanzplatz bearing a giant horse's hoofprint, from the legendary leap of Princess Brunhilde fleeing the knight Bodo.

name: The Rottweiler
description: A characteristic black-and-tan dog breed of the Black Forest, bred from Roman dogs and wild dark faerie species; some have faerie blood granting longevity and Second Sight, and at least one Rhine magus uses them instead of grogs.

name: The Rumaquelle
description: A magical green-watered spring in the southern Harz, said to be where Ruma, daughter of the dwarf king, surfaced as a stream to reunite with the giant Romer.

name: The Salernitarian Women
description: A famous group of women at Salerno studying medicine, renowned as obstetricians and surgeons, legendarily credited with curing the Duke of Normandy.

name: The Sanctuary of Hercules
description: A hidden cave of magical springs on the western Vosges, with a Magic aura of 3, where the Gauls worshiped Ogmios and the Romans Hercules, ringed with ancient altars.

name: The Schwanenburg
description: An old castle on a hill overlooking Cleves by the Rhine, named after the Knight of the Swan, Lohengrin.

name: The Scribe's Touch
description: A Perdo Animal 3 spell that trims the magus's quill with the flick of a finger.

name: The Severed Limb Made Whole
description: A Creo Corpus ritual (Level 25) that reattaches a detached limb, though decay on the severed limb persists after reattachment.

name: The Shadow of Human Life
description: A Creo Imaginem spell (Level 40) with a Mentem requisite that gives a human image (as in Phantasm of the Human Form) limited freedom and simulated intellect, functioning as a stupid independent human.

name: The Shadow of Life Renewed
description: A Creo Corpus ritual (Level 75) with a Mentem requisite that brings the semblance of life to a corpse; the closest the Order of Hermes has come to raising the dead.

name: The Shadow-Masters
description: A troupe of Merinita magi who, using Plato's cave allegory, fashion illusory figures and stories to reinforce belief in the imaginary; they host the Great Play and Initiate Glamour, Animae Magic, and Perpetuity.

name: The Silent Vigil
description: A Muto Corpus spell (Level 45) with a Terram requisite that lets the caster move into and become part of a rock formation at least twice their size.

name: The Singers in Hollow Rooms
description: An example Jerbiton league that calls up the ghosts of ancient artists; its homages involve constructing or searching for tombs.

name: The Single Ocean
description: A Jerbiton league exploring the cities of the Levant and North Africa, seeking peaceful relationships with Jewish and Muslim sorcerers, led by Edward the White.

name: The Sorcerer's Fork
description: A Muto Vim spell that splits another spell into two or more identical spells of reduced power against separate targets.

name: The Source of the Danube
description: An enchanted spring in the eastern Black Forest, source of the River Danube, with a Faerie aura and a regio whose top level holds a gateway into Arcadia and abundant Aquam vis; presided over by the faerie Danu.

name: The Spell of Wrought Iron
description: A ReTe 15 spell (Touch, Momentary, Group) that transforms raw pig-iron into plain bars of wrought iron, separating out the slag.

name: The Sphinx
description: A legendary monument near the Pyramids in Egypt studied by magi who erected an open-desert laboratory beside it.

name: The Spider
description: A character from The Travels of Fedoso who may assist player characters in a faerie wood; possibly a spirit or faerie said to have predicted the depredations of an evil magus.

name: The Stone of Death
description: An ancient stone aligned to the winter-solstice sunset; during the third decan of Gemini, daily animal sacrifices made at the rising of Saturn cause Perdo vis to form from the blood.

name: The Stultified Peasant
description: A Perdo Mentem spell that destroys a target's imagination, removing his ability to think and leaving him standing mouth open.

name: The Subtle Chain
description: Philippus Niger's enchanted silver chain that forms a 3-pace circle and creates a variety of once-per-day warding effects against demons, spirits, beasts, and faeries.

name: The Succubus's Trick
description: A MuCo 5 spell that causes a female caster to adopt male physical characteristics; named after gender-changing demons of lust.

name: The Swabian Jura
description: A series of harsh limestone hills separating the Danube and Neckar valleys, dotted with stalactite grottos such as the Nebelhöhle and Wimsener Höhle.

name: The Teufelskuche
description: A forgotten stone circle and altar in the Haldensleben Forest near Magdeburg where the pagan god Woden was worshipped; it is the origin of the Wild Hunt.

name: The Teufelsmoor
description: An extensive swampy peat wasteland northeast of Bremen with an ill reputation, almost always mist-covered and shunned by locals; a possible covenant location.

name: The Three Faerie Cords
description: Three additional negative cords (leaden, iron, tin) discovered by Farrago Bonisagi that permanently bind a faerie familiar by hindering the maga's mind, body, and spirit to offset cord decay.

name: The Thuringian Forest
description: One of Germany's largest forests, covering nearly a hundred miles of the Thuringia-Franconia border, the traditional boundary between northern and southern Germany.

name: The Tireless Servant
description: An animated skeleton automaton (ReCo 25/40) that fetches and holds objects on verbal command, adding to a lab's General Quality and Safety.

name: The Twice-Gifted Coin
description: A PeMe 15 spell (Touch, Momentary, Individual) that erases the target's memory of having paid a coin, so he pays again; sometimes enchanted into a toll-gate.

name: The Unbidden Task
description: A MuMe 25 spell that creates a recurring prospective memory in a target, prompting them to infer and act on a reason for it.

name: The Unnamed Cabal
description: A House Tytalus cabal, symbolized by a counterclockwise swirl of five lines, whose goal is to keep the other cabals in conflict; supposedly composed of the most powerful Tytalus Archmagi.

name: The Venusberg
description: A splendid subterranean home of the goddess Venus beneath a mountain in an unknown spot in Germany, discovered by the knight Tannhäuser.

name: The Verminous Infestation
description: A Rego Animal spell (Req: Perdo, Corpus) that infests a target with fleshworms in his intestines, inflicting the Worms disease immediately.

name: The Virtuous Hound
description: A magical beast with Magic Might 10 (Animal), an intelligent bloodhound recruited as covenfolk who can flawlessly track prey and speak; based on the bloodhound from The Book of Mundane Beasts.

name: The Vitalizer of Provisions
description: A Creo Animal (Herbam) 19 enchanted chest that preserves food placed within it, preventing decay while the door remains closed.

name: The Viticulturalists
description: A Jerbiton league that believes peasant life has virtue and engages in magically assisted manorial agriculture, led by Sabina of the Seine.

name: The Voice of the Bjornaer Magus
description: A Muto Animal 15 spell allowing a Bjornaer caster in animal form to speak with a human voice, cast without words or gestures.

name: The Vosges Mountains
description: A mountain range bounding Upper Lorraine to the east, once dominated by a secretive fir spirit that was extinguished by the planting of the holy staff at Thann.

name: The Wartburg
description: A great unbreached castle near Eisenach, ancestral home of the landgraves of Thuringia and famed center of literature and music hosting the Sangerkrieg.

name: The Wayfarers
description: A group of Merinitae who style themselves Arcadian experts, recording earthly gateway locations and guiding travelers into Faerie; they typically Initiate Arcadian Travel and rival House Mercere's Redcaps.

name: The Weightless Transportation of Books
description: A Perdo Animal 25 spell that makes the books within a chest almost weightless, easing transport or reducing a library's load on covenant floors.

name: The Welcome Addition of False Sunlight
description: A Creo Ignem 15 spell creating a steady, cool, smokeless, non-flickering light; often enchanted into library devices that float, embed in ceilings, or overlook desks.

name: The White Horse of Uffington
description: A horse figure carved into a Berkshire hillside that can rise and move about the country or Arcadia as a white horse of surpassing beauty, uncontrollable by mortals.

name: The Wild Huntsman
description: A grim Unseelie faerie lord (Faerie Might 50) on an immense black horse, focus of every Wild Hunt, perhaps once a fragment of Woden, who seeks to maintain winter's hold on the land.

name: The Winding Path
description: The 'path' of Criamon magi who do not consciously develop themselves spiritually; the widest path of directionlessness, first followed by Juliasta.

name: The Wizard's Bridle
description: Philippus Niger's feared magical item, a head frame and shackles that trap a victim's tongue and limbs to prevent casting, enchanted with Bind The Gift and Hinder the Gift; used once to restrain a Marched Tytalus magus.

name: The Ziegensteine
description: A megalithic barrow of stone slabs under a giant oak near Monchgut on Rugen, used as a cemetery by the volkhvy; secretly a faerie-trod gateway through Arcadia to the Novgorod covenant Pripet Major.

name: The nameless goblin
description: A goblin noble who rebelled against the goblin king and was stripped of his name and transformed into a stalactite; the stalagmite he grows beneath himself yields Terram vis when ground to powder.

name: Theban League
description: A military alliance formed by magi in the north of the Empire to resist the emperor, the Infernal, and House Tremere; they joined the Order under Jerbiton's nominal leadership and later founded the Tribunal of Thebes.

name: Theban Legion
description: A legion of early Christians, including St. Victor, said by legend to have died at the Roman colony that became Xanten.

name: Theban Tribunal magus Lucian
description: Duplicate placeholder removed.

name: Thelxiope
description: The founder of the Seirenes, a Greek woman saved by the sirens and taught their magic, who then traveled Europe rescuing and training Gifted girls.

name: Theobald
description: A bishop of Gubbio in Umbria whose episcopal ring and thumb, carried by his loyal servant, miraculously rooted a staff into the ground in the Vosges, leading to the founding of Thann Chapel.

name: Theocracy
description: A covenant governance form in which the magi rule as priests through lesser priests, as in the Worshipful covenant.

name: Theodore Lascaris
description: The Byzantine Emperor living in exile in Nicea, whose agent seeks the magi's help to contact the goddess Hecate and expel the Latin usurpers from Constantinople.

name: Theodorus of Samos
description: The sixth-century Greek inventor credited with creating the first locks in Mythic Europe; namesake of the spell The Key of Theodorus.

name: Theophilus
description: The monk credited as author of the craft manual On Divers Arts.

name: Theopholus of House Jerbiton
description: A magus of House Jerbiton with the Gentle Gift who covertly teaches Magic Theory to university students to find naturally inclined Gifted individuals and recruit covenant members.

name: Thera
description: A volcanic island, site of Akrotiri, whose ancient people discovered many magical and technological secrets; now infested with vampires.

name: Theriac (cure-all)
description: A wonderful cure-all for any ailment sold by traveling empirici, often claimed to be from a secret family recipe; real theriacs exist but most sold are pondwater and grass.

name: Theriomorphy
description: A Minor House Mystery of Bjornaer allowing a magus to apply a Quality or Virtue of his Heartbeast to his human form via partial physical change.

name: Thetis
description: A sea nymph who, with Eurynome, rescued and raised the cast-out Hephaestus and built him an underwater forge.

name: Theurgic Spirit Familiar
description: A Mystery Virtue the Titanoi cult can Initiate.

name: Thief of Emotions
description: A new Major Supernatural Virtue granting the Emotion Theft Supernatural Ability to remove an emotion from one person and transfer it to another; the second Fruit of the Arcadian Path.

name: Thief's Slippers
description: Wondrous shoes that let the wearer move without making a sound (Craft Level 15).

name: Thierry of Chartres
description: A scholar who taught at the cathedral school of Chartres.

name: Thoroughfare
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: supernatural creatures such as gnomes pass through the lab and cause minor nuisance (-1 Safety).

name: Thoughts Distinctly Burned
description: A Rego Aquam 15 spell that controls ink so it forms patterns on pages corresponding to the magus's spoken words.

name: Thoughts within Babble
description: An Intellego Mentem spell (Level 25) that lets the caster understand the speech of those within the target area, including misused language.

name: Through the Aegis
description: An Ars Magica supplement containing five fully developed covenants, one for each season plus one that returned from Winter to Spring.

name: Thunor
description: An old Germanic thunder god worshiped by the German tribes.

name: Thuringia
description: A landlocked upland region of the Rhine Tribunal bounded by the Kyffhauser Mountains and the Thuringian Forest, quaint rather than bustling.

name: Tie the Threads That Bind
description: A general-level Rego Vim ritual formulaic spell used uniquely to unite an automaton's magic into a cohesive unit, requiring a level equal to the construct's Magic Might + 15.

name: Tillitus of House Bonisagus
description: A magus of House Bonisagus of the covenant Semita Errabunda who invents Rego Vim warding spells against magical creatures in a spell-invention example.

name: Tincture of Parsley
description: A Theriac of Level 10, Potency Strong, a herbal infusion that acts as an antidote to any serpent bite when consumed immediately after the bite.

name: Tinderdry
description: A Level 5 alchemical Reagent, a wool-like substance that when rubbed over damp wood dries it enough to be lit with flint and steel.

name: Titania
description: A faerie queen who gifted the King of England a hippogriff that fell ill from London's strong Divine aura.

name: Titanoi Cult Lore
description: A cult lore Ability taught to magi raised in the Titanoi Mystery Cult of House Tytalus.

name: Tius
description: The battle god of the Germans, worshiped by Hermann and the Cheruski, whose priests' magic aided the tribes at the Teutoburger Forest.

name: Tobias
description: An example swineherd whose body Antigone inhabits during a psychodramatic Quest on the Avenue of the Unexpected Pages, charged with delivering a candlestick.

name: Tom the Cutpurse
description: An example agent of Carolus, a thief with a Bond of Gratitude who is asked to steal a mayor's signet ring using Dexterity plus Legerdemain.

name: Tonic of Gold
description: A Theriac of Level 5, Potency Weak, made with minute quantities of gold, that restores a Winded character to a non-fatigued state.

name: Torture Chair of Zeus
description: A mechanized chair Hephaestus made that Zeus used to torture Hera; rediscovered by Milo and prize of the first Verditius Contest, won by Gelon.

name: Touch of the Goose Feather
description: A Perdo Corpus spell (Level 5) that causes the target to let out a loud sneeze, disrupting concentration and activities.

name: Touch of the Pearls
description: An Intellego Aquam spell (Level 5) that tells the caster whether a touched liquid is poisonous, like a pearl, without tasting it.

name: Toul
description: A venerable city forty miles up the Mosel from Metz, formerly Roman Tullum, surrounded by tall white stone walls and remaining loyal to its duke.

name: Toulouse
description: A location in the Provencal Tribunal where the covenant of Tolosa Paratge resides.

name: Tower of Notatus
description: A tower at Durenmar conjured by and named after the first Primus of House Bonisagus; it houses most Bonisagus magi and Murion's sanctum.

name: Tower of Trianoma
description: The youngest of Durenmar's three towers, named in honor of Trianoma; its basement houses one of the Rhine's official Mercer Houses.

name: Tower of Whirling Water
description: A Rego Aquam spell (Level 35) that forms a waterspout under the caster's mental direction, damaging and potentially drowning those it hits.

name: Traditional Ward
description: A taboo that a faerie may not touch with its glamour; it cannot regenerate Might in the ward's presence and is harmed if forced to touch it.

name: Traditionalists
description: A philosophical faction within House Guernicus that believes the Code should be preserved as it has been since the Founding.

name: Transitionalists
description: A philosophical faction within House Guernicus, started by Simprim, that believes the Code should be revised and seeks greater legal powers for the Quaesitores.

name: Transmission
description: The process by which a Criamon magus passes learned wisdom on to other members of the House, sometimes encapsulating it perfectly into a place or object upon entering Twilight.

name: Trapping the Fire
description: A Muto Ignem spell (Level 25) with a Terram requisite that turns the heat and flames of a large campfire into a small hard object such as a gem; breaking the object releases the flame.

name: Treading the Ashen Path
description: A Perdo Herbam spell (Level 30) that withers and destroys plant material in front of the caster as they walk up to 7 miles; invented by a magus of House Flambeau.

name: Treasure of the Nibelungs
description: The great treasure Siegfried won from the Nibelungs, later sunk in the Rhine by Hagen and lost forever after the tragedy of the Nibelungenlied.

name: Tree Falling in the Forest
description: A Pe(Re)He 35 spell that instantly cuts down a tree in a chosen direction; with an aiming roll it can fall on a creature for up to +18 damage and bypasses Magic Resistance.

name: Tres Ex Miscellanea
description: A rustic magus tried at the Provencal Tribunal of 1214 for interfering with mundanes after declaring Wizard's War and destroying a rival covenant's tower with an army.

name: Trethevy Quoit
description: A group of standing stones supporting a capstone, believed to be the home of a powerful faerie who does not like to be disturbed.

name: Trevelyan
description: The first Trevelyan, the only man who escaped the drowning of Lyonesse by riding his white horse ahead of the flood to St. Michael's Mount.

name: Trianoma's third filia
description: Reference duplicates Irmele.

name: Trianomans
description: Wandering magi who politically defend certain sites of mystical significance across Mythic Europe.

name: Tribunal Field of Durenmar
description: The traditional grounds at Durenmar where the Rhine Tribunal gathers, containing the Forum and the ancient seat of Bjornaer; site of the Order's initiation ceremonies.

name: Tribunal of Novgorod
description: A Hermetic Tribunal whose covenants often take advantage of the great fair of Thessalonica (the Demetria).

name: Tribunal of Transylvania
description: A Hermetic Tribunal whose covenants frequent the great fair of Thessalonica for its eastern goods.

name: Trinitarians
description: An order of monks active since 1198 dedicated to ransoming slaves.

name: Tristan
description: Hero whose place of birth was the land of Lyonesse.

name: Troche of Colocynth
description: A Theriac of Level 5, Potency Weak, a compressed pill that causes violent bowel evacuations and can purge retained humors from a patient with a melancholic disease.

name: Trods
description: Special pathways that lead into and out of Faerie, connecting regio levels to each other and the mundane world and even leading to Arcadia; Arcadian Travel lets Merinitae create them at will.

name: Trolls
description: Supernatural creatures given as an example of guardians for a magical jewel in a tournament special challenge.

name: Trollsynir
description: Wizards said to live in Scandinavia and Iceland who claim descent from giants and bear the power to curse their enemies; a Damhadh-Duidsan variant.

name: Trotula of Salerno
description: A famous recent example of a female physician (medica) practicing medicine in Mythic Europe.

name: Troupe Upbringing
description: A Minor General Virtue for a character raised among entertainers, granting +2 to rolls involving abilities in a selected area such as acrobatics or storytelling.

name: Trouvères
description: A type of minstrel from northern France, concentrating on Arthurian poems, of whom Chrétien of Troyes is the most famous.

name: True Merinitae
description: A cult and House lineage following Mendalus's effort to reconstruct Merinita's nature Mysteries, who claim to learn Nature Lore directly from the Founder via Agnes.

name: True Rest of the Injured Brute
description: A Creo Animal spell (Level 20) granting an injured animal target a +9 bonus to all Recovery rolls while the spell is in effect.

name: True Sight of the Air
description: An Intellego Auram spell (Level 15) that lets the caster see clearly through smoke, fog, and dust, even if magical.

name: Trutina the Quaesitor
description: A beautiful mature maga and quaesitor who joined Burnham in 1195, says little, and instructs an unGifted Redcap to vote with Iudicium; wears the badge of House Guernicus.

name: Tuareg
description: A North African people with designated religious tribes; the Ineslemen Social Status belongs to one of these tribes.

name: Tuatha de Danu
description: The fair folk of Ireland, said to be the children of the faerie goddess embodied in the Danube.

name: Tuisto
description: The earth-born god of Germanic legend whose son Mannus sired the three ancestral fathers of the German tribes.

name: Tulgank
description: An ugly mountain-spirit faerie melded forever into his cavern floor by the Seelie he loved; his petrified hand still nurtures a rose whose petals yield Herbam vis.

name: Turb Trained
description: A Minor Social Status Virtue for a character raised at a covenant and trained to fight in the turb, allowed to learn Martial Abilities at character creation.

name: Turnis
description: The second Primus of House Verditius who developed the ritual allowing other Hermetic magi to join the House and set the rules of the Contest.

name: Twilight Mastery
description: A new Major Hermetic Virtue letting a magus choose the effects of Wizard's Twilight and induce Warping in others; the second Fruit of the Path of Warping.

name: Twist the Living Tree
description: A Rego Herbam spell (Level 25) that bends a living tree into unusual positions to form a cage, shelter, or wall while the caster maintains concentration.

name: Twisted Spine
description: A Minor Curse (Rego Corpus effect) that twists the victim's spine grotesquely, imposing -3 to social rolls.

name: Tytalan Ink
description: A charged item in the form of colorless ink that becomes visible (turns black or another color) upon a command word, used by Tytalan magi for secret writing.

name: Ulm
description: A city on the northern bank of the upper Danube first settled by Jews in the 9th century, declared a Free Imperial City by Frederick Barbarossa in 1164 and known for linen weaving.

name: Ultima Thule
description: A far-northern region where the walking dead are prevalent, leading Donatores there to concentrate on Corpus.

name: Ultor
description: A Summa on Penetration (Level 5, Quality 11) by Elaine, emphasizing penetrating the Parma Magica.

name: Unbaptized
description: A Major Story Flaw in which the character is a Christian who has never been baptized, often due to a supernatural background, and does not benefit from the sacraments.

name: Uncertain Faith
description: A Minor General Flaw in which doubt stands between the character and the Divine, giving -3 to holy influence rolls and a +1 Personality Trait that demons exploit.

name: Uncontrollable Strength
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character doesn't know his own strength, requiring a stress roll against Ease Factor 6 to avoid overdoing delicate tasks.

name: Undecorated
description: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the lab has spartan or absent decoration, making it uninspiring (-1 Upkeep, -1 Aesthetics).

name: Underwater
description: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab is filled with water instead of air, causing breathing and movement difficulties (+2 Safety, +1 Warping, -2 Aesthetics, +4 Aquam).

name: Undoing the Stonemason's Handiwork
description: A PeTe 15 spell that smashes masonry or pavement into component stones; used by School of Vilano followers to produce loose stones for ammunition or to collapse structures.

name: Unease of the Still Forest
description: A Mentem power of the bockman faeries that radiates an aura of unease up to 100 paces, silencing birds and instilling growing dread and paranoia in those within.

name: Uneven Floor
description: A Free laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab has a wonky or dangerous floor, e.g. a cave or sand-covered floor (-1 Safety, -1 Health, -1 Aesthetics).

name: Unimaginative Learner
description: A Minor Hermetic Flaw in which the character has trouble figuring things out, subtracting 3 from rolls when studying from raw vis.

name: Uninspirational
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is bland and boring; Presence and Communication may not exceed 0, and social Abilities used to impress suffer -3.

name: University of Arezzo
description: A small student-run Italian university south of Florence, founded in 1215, offering faculties of law, medicine, and the arts.

name: University of Palencia
description: A royal Spanish university founded by King Alfonso VIII of Castile in 1208, with faculties of arts, canon law, and theology, overseen by the Bishop of Palencia.

name: University of Reggio
description: A small student-run Italian university northwest of Bologna teaching law exclusively, founded by departing Bolognese scholars.

name: University of Vicenza
description: A short-lived Italian university swarmed from Bologna, lasting from 1204 until scholars returned to Bologna in 1210.

name: Unlucky
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is exceptionally unlucky, getting -1 to -3 on rolls in luck-based situations.

name: Unraveling
description: A new Mastery special ability applicable to Perdo Vim spells, adding three times the Mastery score to the spell's effective level for destroying magic.

name: Unraveling the Fabric of (Form)
description: A Perdo Vim 20 spell enchanted into Philippus Niger's talisman with ten related effects, one for each Hermetic Form; basis for Shattering the Malicious Rune.

name: Unraveling the Fabric of Imaginem
description: A Perdo Vim (PeVi 20) spell that dispels Imaginem (image) magic.

name: Unravelling
description: A Mastered Spell special ability for Perdo Vim spells, adding three times Mastery score to the effective level when destroying a targeted magical effect.

name: Unravelling the Fabric of (Form)
description: A Perdo Vim spell that cancels the effects of one spell of a specified Form; ten Form variants exist plus rarer non-Hermetic variants.

name: Unseelie
description: A dark faction of faeries; an Unseelie faerie lord holds a melancholy feast on the last day of winter at which a doomed mortal is danced to death, leaving footprints where destroying angel mushrooms grow.

name: Unspecialized
description: A Minor General Flaw in which the character does not have any specialties for any of her Abilities.

name: Unstable
description: A Free laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab is prone to movement, e.g. on a ship or earthquake-prone, causing occasional accidents (+1 Upkeep, -1 Safety).

name: Unstructured Caster
description: A Major Hermetic Flaw in which the character casts all Formulaic spells as Ritual spells (including needing vis) and may not learn Ritual spells, but casts Spontaneous spells normally.

name: Unyielding Earth
description: A Rego Terram spell that compacts the ground surface in a 15-by-15-pace area, making it more solid.

name: Upper Lorraine
description: A duchy that came into existence on the division of the Carolingian empire, a moderately populated rolling plain bounded by the Vosges, Rhine, Ardennes, and Argonne; its seat is Nancy.

name: Urgen of Crintera
description: Leader of the Weissdorngilde (Hawthorn Gild), a follower of House Bjornaer from the covenant of Crintera.

name: Uriel, the Angel of Punishment
description: An angel known as the Angel of Punishment, whom the chastising angel Kolazonta serves.

name: Ursula Densacer
description: Clan Chief of Clan Arelie, a wolf-heartbeast maga acclaimed for erudition and poetry, and a friend of Prima Falke.

name: Usama ibn Munqidh
description: A historical author (d. 1188) quoted from The Book of Learning by Example describing an angelic rescue on a mountain, illustrating the angel Nasir.

name: Usurer
description: A Minor Social Status Flaw in which the character lends valuables at abusive interest rates, earning about ten pounds of silver yearly but holding a poor reputation at level 4.

name: Uswaurpa
description: A byname ('reject') for a Bjornaer magus known to have shapeshifted before Initiation, who acquires the scorn of his peers.

name: Valdemar I
description: The Danish king whose invasion of Rügen in 1168 surprised the Bjornaer covenant of Crintera and triggered its crisis.

name: Valdemar II
description: The King of Denmark, relatively secure with Schleswig and Holstein under his control, who in the historical timeline grants Kolding a full charter in 1230.

name: Valdus
description: A magus of House Tytalus charged in 1109 AD by Treverorum for theft of vis from a site outside Trier; fined one pawn of vis and ordered to seek permission before harvesting again.

name: Vanasalus of Criamon
description: A young, friendly Criamon maga of Semitae who believes magic reflects one's personality and follows Gerfallon to understand the Enigma.

name: Vardian's Tomb
description: A covenant whose necromancer created the plague that halted Barbarossa's army at the gates of Rome.

name: Variable Power
description: A Minor Supernatural Virtue: one of the character's magic powers grows more powerful over time based on age, Might, Warping, or an Ability score.

name: Variola
description: A Serious Choleric Disease from putrid choler accumulating in the skin; highly contagious and disfiguring.

name: Varstus
description: An Italian Alps wizard skilled in sympathetic magic whom Flambeau confronted with the words 'Join us or die!' in 771 and slew when he fled.

name: Venatus
description: An eighty-year-post-Gauntlet Collegium-turned-Lyceum magus of Trianoma's lineage who discovered the New Aristotle at Bologna, split from the Collegium to found the Lyceum, and still teaches at a university.

name: Venetian Arsenal
description: The most heavily capitalized manufactory in Europe, located in Venice, capable of outfitting three war galleys per day to assemble a fleet for the Fourth Crusade.

name: Vengeful Powers
description: A Major Story Tainted Flaw in which the Infernal realm has taken interest in the character's non-Infernal Powers, causing harmful side effects whenever they are used without sin.

name: Venus
description: The goddess who dwells in the subterranean Venusberg, where the knight Tannhäuser worshiped her for a year.

name: Venus's Blessing
description: A suitable Free Virtue for Jerbiton magi, preferred for characters desiring weaker emotional attachments.

name: Verdan of Ex Miscellanea
description: A magus of House Ex Miscellanea whose sigil makes all his spells involve the color green, such as turning poisonous liquids faint green.

name: Verderis
description: The third Primus of House Criamon, author of the epic poem The Travels of Fedoso; his ghost is absent from the Cave of Twisting Shadows and he had the Premonitions Virtue.

name: Verditius' Forge
description: The laboratory built by the Founder Verditius near the Tower of Bonisagus at Durenmar, traditionally housing the covenant's Artificer.

name: Verdun
description: A border city on the River Meuse famous for the Treaty of 843, where spies and assassins can be recruited and Redcaps meet while traveling between the Rhine and Normandy Tribunals.

name: Vernacular Education
description: A minor general Virtue of secular tutoring for merchant-house scions, allowing purchase of Academic Abilities and granting extra experience points for trade-relevant Abilities.

name: Vesta
description: A Roman goddess of hearth and home whose rites were integrated into the cult of Diana and adopted as patron by the Cult of Vesta; treated as a faerie/pagan deity in Mythic Europe.

name: Viator of Mercere
description: The only Gifted Redcap in the tribunal, retired to Ungulus to develop a magical means of communication between covenants without compromising their defenses.

name: Vilano
description: A ninth-century Flambeau magus from Istria in the Transylvanian Tribunal who suffered the Flaw Weak Magic but pioneered combat with only indirect spells, famously slaying the Green Dragon of Labin with falling trees.

name: Vile Surroundings
description: A Free laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab sits in an undesirable place such as a swamp or by a filthy hovel (-2 Health, -1 Aesthetics).

name: Vile Water of Sterility
description: A Muto Aquam Ritual spell that ruins a body of water up to a small lake, making it dark, noxious, and unfit for habitation or consumption.

name: Villard de Honnecourt
description: The most famous master mason of 1220, who worked on cathedrals at Laon, Chartres, Reims, and Meux and produced tractatus sketchbooks usable to study Craft: Mason.

name: Virgin Mary
description: By far the most important saint, the mother of God, believed to have particularly strong influence in interceding with God; Margaret of Beverley was rescued by her grace.

name: Virtues and Flaws
description: Special character features: Virtues grant benefits while Flaws impose disadvantages or story hooks, including supernatural abilities, aptitudes, and personality traits.

name: Vis Extraction
description: The laboratory activity of distilling raw vis, appearing as a lab Specialization aided by superior equipment, stills, and certain Features.

name: Vis Grant
description: A covenant Boon representing the annual division of surplus vis among the members.

name: Vis Salary
description: A covenant Hook in which members must work to earn a share of vis, appropriate when individuals must petition the council for vis.

name: Vision of Heat's Light
description: An Intellego Ignem spell (Level 20) that lets the caster see the heat of objects of human body temperature or hotter, useful in the dark though not giving true vision.

name: Vision of the Scrying Pool
description: A Hermetic spell adapted from one of the lost golden-tablet rituals of the Cult of Mercury.

name: Visions of the Infernal Terrors
description: A spell that causes everything the target sees and hears to appear terrifying, potentially scaring them to death.

name: Vitriol
description: A Level 15 Alteration Reagent that creates strong acid able to dissolve stone, base metal, and wood, inflicting +10 damage if poured on a person; only glass is proof against it.

name: Voice Like a Bard
description: A common automaton power (base effect 10, Creo Imaginem) letting the automaton masterfully sing a small repertoire of ballads.

name: Voice Like a Nightingale
description: A common automaton power (base effect 5, Creo Imaginem) letting the automaton sing bird songs through its mouth.

name: Voice of the (Land)
description: A Minor Supernatural Virtue letting the character speak with any creature whose natural habitat is a particular environment, without being perceived as threat or prey.

name: Volkhvy
description: Exclusively male pagan priests of Rugen who serve gods such as the Forest Brothers and Svantovit; nearly all have the Ways of the Forest Virtue and can open faerie gates.

name: Vow of Service
description: A Flaw binding a character to a vow of service, taken by the Ghostly Warden.

name: Vulcan
description: The Roman god of fire and the forge after whom the Cult of Vulcan was renamed; Balento claimed descent from him and his Mysteries emphasized destructive fire.

name: Vulnerable
description: A Free laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab lacks even basic defenses and is easily entered (-1 Aesthetics).

name: Vysehrad Rock
description: A hilltop south of Prague where the Gifted Princess Libuse had her vision foretelling her husband Premysl, founder of Bohemia's ruling dynasty; now site of Prague's second castle.

name: Wahhab
description: An example jinni with Magic Might 15 (Ignem), a fire spirit inhabiting ancient ruins of a fane to a forgotten god in Iberia, with fire and shapeshifting powers.

name: Waldgeister
description: German wood-faeries dwelling in huge numbers in forests, some benevolent and some malicious, including Katzenveit, Gübich, and Rübezahl.

name: Wall of Living Wood
description: A Creo Herbam spell (Level 25) that creates a straight wall of living oak 20 paces long, growing quickly from nearby trees or fertile earth.

name: Wall of Thorns
description: A Creo Herbam spell (Level 15) that creates a straight wall of resilient thorny bushes up to 20 paces long and 4 paces high.

name: Walpurgis Night
description: The eve of the 1st of May on which Rhine Tribunal gatherings begin and a procession of witches takes place on the Brocken.

name: Walsingham
description: A shrine of Our Lady in Norfolk and a pilgrimage site of growing importance; the Virgin of Walsingham is claimed to be especially powerful.

name: Walter de Grey
description: The Archbishop of York (elected 1215), a royal servant and former chancellor who quarrels with Stephen Langton over the right to bear his cross in the southern province.

name: Walther von der Vogelweide
description: The most brilliant minnesanger, who bested rivals at the 1204 Wartburg Sangerkrieg and composed poems for rival claimants to the imperial throne.

name: Walther von der Vogelwiede
description: One of the most famous German minnesingers, living in Vienna at the court of Leopold VI.

name: Wanderlust
description: A Major Story Flaw in which the character is compelled to travel and cannot spend more than a season in the same place.

name: Ward Against Beasts of Legend
description: A Rego Animal 25 warding effect enchanted into Philippus Niger's Subtle Chain.

name: Ward Against Flame
description: A Rego Ignem 15 spell creating a circle that mundane fires cannot cross, used around heat sources, grain stores, and sometimes whole laboratories.

name: Ward Against Monsters Which Walk As Man
description: A Rego Corpus 25 warding effect enchanted into Philippus Niger's Subtle Chain, protecting against Might-bearing creatures affected by Corpus.

name: Ward Against Mundane Intrusions
description: A Rego Ignem 35 spell with Corpus, Animal, Aquam, and Herbam requisites that conglomerates other wards to hold off flame, light, thieves, pests, moisture, and mildew.

name: Ward Against the Curious Scullion
description: A Rego Corpus 10 spell creating a circle that humans lacking Magic Resistance cannot cross, used to bar entry to Hermetic sancta.

name: Ward against Faeries of the Mountain
description: A Rego Terram spell warding against faeries of earth and stone, working like Ward Against Faeries of the Waters.

name: Ward against Wood
description: A Rego Herbam spell (Level 25) that protects the caster from nonenchanted wood so that none of it can contact his body.

name: Ward against the Beasts of Legend
description: A Rego Animal General ward spell that prevents any magical beast whose Magic Might is at or below the spell level from affecting those within a circle.

name: Ward the Cruel Touch of Pestilence
description: A CrCo 20 spell that grants the target a +9 bonus to Stamina rolls to avoid contracting diseases.

name: Warped Senses
description: A Minor General Flaw making a character overly sensitive to environmental conditions such as light, sound, taste, smell, cold, or heat, with variants like Sensitive (Sense) and Weak (Sense).

name: Warped by Magic
description: A Minor Supernatural Flaw representing exposure to powerful magical forces, granting Warping Points, a Warping Score of 1, and a related Minor Flaw.

name: Waster of Vis
description: A Major Hermetic Flaw causing the character to waste a quarter of the raw vis pawns he uses in any application of vis.

name: Watchtower
description: A fortified stone building atop the cliffs overlooking Durenmar's valley, occupied by the Protector Philippus Niger and surrounded by blasted ground.

name: Water Elemental
description: An elemental being of water that can be created via Creo Aquam ritual and whose Might can be reduced or controlled by Aquam spells.

name: Water sprites
description: Water spirits encountered by Hagen at the River Danube who foretell that all the Burgundians but one priest are doomed to die.

name: Wayland's Smithy
description: A barrow near the White Horse that is the home of the invisible smith Wayland, who shoes horses left with a penny and is said to be able to shoe the White Horse itself.

name: Ways of the (Local Environment)
description: A supernatural Virtue possessed by the angel Nasir, tied to a local environment.

name: Ways of the Mountains
description: A Virtue possessed by Adranus, the spirit of Mount Etna, attuning a being to its mountain environment.

name: Ways of the Swamp
description: A Virtue granting bonuses in swamp terrain; possessed by the Boglin, who gains combat bonuses from it.

name: Weak Characteristics
description: A Minor General Flaw giving the character three fewer points to spend buying Characteristics.

name: Weak Enchanter
description: A Minor Hermetic Flaw in which the magus's Gift is ill attuned to creating enchanted devices, halving Lab Total for creating or investigating enchanted items.

name: Weak Personality
description: A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character lacks strong feelings, restricting Personality Traits to between +1 and -1.

name: Weak Scholar
description: A Minor Hermetic Flaw giving a -6 penalty to Lab Totals when working from the Lab Texts of others, including re-inventing spells.

name: Weak-Willed
description: A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character looks to others for guidance rather than himself.

name: Weaving
description: The commonest Craft Ability for factors, reflecting skill in producing their main product.

name: Well Insulated
description: A Minor laboratory Structure Virtue: the lab is especially shielded from the outside world, suitable for sensitive locations (+1 Safety, +1 Aesthetics).

name: Well Traveled
description: A Virtue incompatible with the No Sense of Direction Flaw.

name: Well without Light
description: A Perdo Ignem spell (Level 25) that removes light from a target structure so that only spells above level 25 can create light there; the light flows into the caster's clenched fist.

name: Welsh druids
description: Indigenous Welsh magical tradition with which House Díedne had close links, though they did not join the Order; associated with stone circles.

name: West Country
description: The covenant-free region of Devon and Cornwall, suitable for magical colonization, near the ruins of Sursum and Stellapser and sites associated with Arthur.

name: Western Christendom
description: A cultural society of Mythic Europe centered on western Europe and including the Crusader States, defining a set of Social Status Virtues and Flaws.

name: Westminster
description: The seat of the court of the King's Bench and site of the king's Maundy Thursday ceremony in Westminster Abbey.

name: Wiederich
description: The sole survivor of the Magyar attack on Sirmium in 930, a Flambeau magus who joined the German armies to avenge himself on the Magyars; his vengeful descendants persist.

name: Wieliczka
description: A location in Poland named for its salt mines, cited as a Greater mining income example.

name: Wilding
description: A Major Nature Mystery letting a maga extract temporary vis from completely natural objects according to her Nature Lore.

name: Wilkis
description: Most eloquent of Birna's six apprentices, told to 'Nourish,' a wolf from a Prussian tribe, appointed first primus of the House; founder of Clan Wilkis.

name: William Fireheart of Flambeau
description: Ungulus's most infamous member at the end of the twelfth century, who caused trouble in northern France and lost a Wizard's War to a magus of Fudarus in 1220.

name: William Marshal the Younger
description: The earl of Pembroke who holds Fotheringhay castle against royal orders and is suing Falkes de Bréauté over four disputed manors.

name: William de Fors
description: The count of Aumale who holds the royal castle of Rockingham despite government demands that he surrender it.

name: William of Conches
description: A scholar who taught at the cathedral school of Chartres.

name: William of Jerbiton
description: A Jerbiton magus of Rosalba targeted by Diana of Tremere in the 873 Wizards' War; his death began near-constant skirmishing.

name: William of Newburgh
description: A medieval chronicler quoted in the Donatores history, author of Historia Rerum Anglicarum, who recorded accounts of cadavers leaving their tombs to wander among the living.

name: William of Thanet
description: The aging, capable autocrat who has handled the day-to-day operation of Nigrasaxa since its founding.

name: William the Conqueror
description: Duke of Normandy who conquered England after the Battle of Hastings in 1066, built the Tower of London, and commissioned the Domesday Book.

name: Willigis
description: A tenth-century archbishop of Mainz from whom onwards the archbishop enjoyed the status of Archchancellor of the Empire.

name: Wilton
description: The stone-built village fifteen minutes from Voluntas that serves as part of the covenant, housing covenfolk and providing an inn for guests.

name: Wimpfen
description: A small fortified city high above the River Neckar with Roman, Frankish, and episcopal history, now a favorite imperial residence.

name: Winchester
description: A declined but important city, former capital of England, with two castles (the royal castle and Wolvesey Castle of the bishop) and the great St. Giles's Fair.

name: Wind at the Back
description: A Rego Auram spell (Level 5) that makes an existing breeze follow the caster as they travel, causing phenomena like fog or haze to follow.

name: Winfrida
description: A young, timid Follower of Guernicus (age 27) and Quaesitor at Durenmar whom Murion is grooming; one of only two Guernicus magi in the Rhine Tribunal.

name: Wings of the Soaring Winds
description: A flight spell that lets a maga move at 40 miles per hour, cited in calculations about flying to the moon.

name: Winter's Icy Grip
description: A Perdo Ignem 30 spell known by Philippus Niger, mastered for Fast Casting.

name: Wisdom from Ignorance
description: A Minor Supernatural Virtue used by certain Egyptian Sufis interested in calligraphy, allowing them to use unreadable books as sources of training for spiritual subjects.

name: Witch Marks
description: A Minor General Tainted Flaw giving the character disfigurements recognized by folk lore as belonging to diabolists.

name: Witches' Altar
description: A mass of granite blocks atop the Brocken where, every Walpurgis Night, Walpurga summons the spirits of summer to defeat those of winter.

name: Wizard's Autumn
description: A Perdo Herbam spell (Level 15) that makes all deciduous leaves on target plants turn brown and fall, affecting a small grove of trees.

name: Wizard's Eclipse
description: A Perdo Ignem ritual (Level 35) that eclipses the sun within a target area, suddenly making it as dark as night.

name: Wizard's Leap
description: A ReCo 15 spell that instantly transports the caster up to 50 paces toward a visible destination or Arcane Connection; effective as a fast-cast defense, bringing the caster's Talisman automatically.

name: Wizard's Reach
description: A Muto Vim spell that increases the range of a targeted spell by one category; ten Form-specific versions exist.

name: Wizard's Well
description: A site that Merlin is said to have created, according to the legends of the mage.

name: Wizards' Melee
description: A controversial Flambeau tournament event where teams of one magus and five grogs fight, the goal being to cast a Touch-range spell on the opposing magus.

name: Wolf Clan
description: One of Crintera's six clans; makes up the bulk of the covenant's warriors and servants, fights with axes, and protects the Prima. Its leader is traditionally a wolf skinchanger and the Prima's personal shield grog.

name: Wolf Mount
description: A faerie wolf the size of a horse (Might 20) made of the glamour of a Valkyrie, sharing her Might pool, which carries her and passengers through the sky.

name: Wolf of Virtue
description: A Great Beast Mythic Blood lineage granting the Paralyze a Man at R: Eye feat, a Focus in Wolves, and the Envious flaw.

name: Wolf's Cloak
description: A wondrous cloak made by a furrier that allows the wearer to change into a wolf until the next sunrise or sunset (Craft Level 17).

name: Wondrous Items
description: The highest quality of crafted goods, minor enchanted items whose Craft Level is 12 plus the magnitude of effect; the goldsmith Banco is renowned for making them.

name: Wookey Hole Caves
description: A deep, partly flooded cave hung with stalactites, in which something is said to live, though local legends disagree about the details.

name: Words of the Unbroken Silence
description: A Creo Mentem spell (Level 10) that lets the caster say two words directly to the mind of a target, who recognizes the supernatural origin and the caster's voice.

name: World of Forms
description: The metaphysical source from which magic draws the details of created things; magi disagree whether it is the realm of Magic, the human mind, or the mind of God.

name: Wrath of Whirling Winds and Water
description: A Creo Auram Ritual spell (Level 65) that creates an immense hurricane-intensity storm 40 or more miles wide, causing massive damage along shorelines and inland.

name: Wreaths of Foul Smoke
description: A Creo Auram spell (Level 10) that raises thick yellow sulfurous smoke that blocks sight and causes Fatigue or wound loss to those who breathe it.

name: Writ of Reprisal
description: A court order allowing a wronged merchant to seize goods from any merchant of a fraudster's home town; such a writ against the Order could trigger Quaesitor review of a covenant's representatives.

name: Wurzburg
description: An influential episcopal city in the middle of Franconia at the center of its largest vineyards; its cathedral houses the shrine of St. Kilian.

name: Xanten
description: A town on the west bank of the Rhine, formerly the Roman colony Colonia Ulpia Traiana, birthplace of the hero Siegfried and former capital of Nibelungland.

name: Xantippes
description: A magus of House Jerbiton who helped found Treverorum to recover Roman secrets, later found guilty of meddling with the mundanes of Trier using his own Mentem magics for personal enrichment.

name: Xavier
description: A Gifted magus of House Mercere, the Rhine Tribunal's only Gifted Mercere and its archivist, who dwells at Durenmar at one of the two official Mercer Houses.

name: Xenophon of Bonisagus
description: The Bonisagus magus who founded the Platonist Hermetic societas the Collegium, believing the Founder had stripped Hermetic Theory of any inquiry into magic's nature or origin.

name: Xerxes
description: A hoplite magus who took Uwe as an apprentice and trained him to become Darius, a hunter of evils within the Order; he is now too frail for combat.

name: Y Gododdin
description: The single famous poem by which the Welsh poet Aneirin is known, praising the war band of Mynyddawg Mwynfawr sent to recapture a Roman stronghold from the Saxons.

name: Yanartas
description: A site near the Antalya Gulf in Asia Minor, where the mythical Chimera fell and fire leaps from the ground, location of one of Hephaestus's forges.

name: Yenghissar
description: A small village along the route to Khashgar plagued every seven years by the Infernal storm spirit known as the Buran.

name: Yeshiva
description: A Jewish school where students learn grammar and Jewish instruction by studying the Talmud and Mishnah from the local rabbi; large ones are in Cordoba and Granada.

name: Yonec
description: The son of a hawk-knight and an imprisoned lady in a Lai of Marie de France; he avenged his father by killing the jealous old lord and took his father's place as king.

name: Yonec's ring and sword
description: Gifts the dying hawk-knight gave his lover: a ring ensuring her husband would remember nothing, and a sword for their son Yonec to avenge him.

name: York
description: The largest town of northern England and seat of the second English archbishop, a port on the River Ouse, site of the 1190 massacre of the Jews.

name: Young Henry
description: The eldest son of Henry II at whose court William Marshal served, leading his mesnie at tournaments; he died of dysentery having taken a crusading vow.

name: Zanzibar
description: A rich city, reachable by circumnavigating Africa, where gold is traded by equal weight for salt; a potential reward for an insured speculative covenant expedition.

name: Zephyrus
description: Air elementals composed of chains of octahedral corpuscles, encompassing wind, cloud, and lightning forms; utterly restless, highly perceptive travelers that crave the dissolution of barriers.

name: Zora
description: The faeblooded priestess who leads the priesthood of Hertha; she gives Crintera Creo vis yearly and is the lover of Istvan Padas.

name: Zurenzialle
description: An unremarkable magus of the 1100s who vanished from his covenant in the Greater Alps; his sodales discovered he had never been human but was a faerie being impersonating a magus.

name: Zwin Sea Dragon
description: A sea dragon that created the storm carving the Zwin channel near Brugge in a secret agreement with Derrick of Alsace, now demanding accumulated tolls via drowned-sailor emissaries.

name: al-Ghazali
description: An eleventh-century Islamic writer who firmly rejected the ideas of Aristotle, Plato, and Socrates in his book The Incoherence of the Philosophers.

name: gruagachan
description: Monstrous wizards of northern Britain who, along with the Anglo-Saxon rune wizards, joined Damhan-Allaidh to oppose the Order.

name: magical raven cloak
description: A magical cloak carried by the Skinchanger spouse covenfolk character, associated with her raven Skinchanger form.
